2331397.title: National Orientation Programme for Tribal Healers on Public Health, Kanha Shanti Vanam, Hyderabad
2331397.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
National Orientation Programme for Tribal Healers on Public Health, Kanha Shanti Vanam, Hyderabad
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 11:28AM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Tribal Affairs in collaboration with the ICMR–National Institute of Health Research (ICMR-NIHR), Bhubaneswar under the Janjatiya Health Institutional Transformation (JanHIT) initiative, has organised the 1st of its kind National Orientation Programme for Tribal Healers on Public Health on 1–2nd November 2026 at Kanha Shanti Vanam, Hyderabad. The programme was inaugurated at the auditorium of Kanha Shanti Vanam, Hyderabad by Shri. Manish Thakur, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs and Dr. Sanghamitra Pati, Director, ICMR-NIHR, Bhubaneswar in presence of Shri B. M. Santosh, IAS, Special Secretary and Director, Tribal Welfare, Telangana, Dr. V. Samujwala, Director, Tribal Cultural Research & Training Institute (TCR&TI), Telangana, and other senior officials from Ministry of Tribal Affairs and ICMR-NIHR, Bhubaneswar. The launch of this landmark initiative on the first day of the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas Pakhwada underscores the shared commitment to honouring and empowering India's tribal communities through inclusive health and capacity-building interventions.

The 1st phase of the orientation programme is being attended by around 550 tribal healers nominated by the State Tribal Welfare departments from nine states and UTs of India (Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Keralam, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli). The orientation programme aims to orient tribal healers on key public health issues and strengthen their understanding of common diseases, early identification of danger signs, and appropriate referral for timely medical care. Recognising the important role of healers in tribal communities, the initiative seeks to enhance their awareness of essential health practices and encourage linkages with the formal healthcare system.

The two-day orientation programme will cover three training modules addressing a wide range of public health concerns. These include communicable and vector-borne diseases, skin diseases, non-communicable diseases, metabolic and blood disorders, liver diseases, and mental health conditions. The sessions will also focus on appropriate referral for snakebites, scorpion & other stings, animal bites, injuries, eye and ear disorders; oral health; and newborn and infant care. The training will also include integrated practice, review sessions, a post-training assessment, and participant feedback to reinforce learning and assess the orientation's effectiveness.

Participants from different states will attend the 2 day programme, with state-wise arrangements for training sessions in regional languages to facilitate effective communication and learning. Experts from AIIMS, ICMR, Quality Control of India, MS Swaminathan Foundation, Amrita Institute, Kochi, IIHMR, Bengaluru and Piramal Swasthya, Maharashtra will be delivering sessions in respective languages for the healers. 

By orienting tribal healers on essential health concerns and appropriate referral practices, the programme seeks to promote informed community-level health support and strengthen collaboration between tribal community practices and the formal healthcare system. This structured capacity-building module developed by ICMR-NIHR, Bhubaneswar, with support from MoTA represents a milestone effort to integrate tribal healthcare practices with formal medical systems, particularly as we commemorate Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas.

The programme will conclude on 2nd November 2026 with a closing ceremony and distribution of certificates to participants.

2331390.title: Ministry of Rural Development Notifies Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026 under VB–G RAM G Act
2331390.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Ministry of Rural Development Notifies Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026 under VB–G RAM G Act
Multi-tier mechanism and digital platform for prompt, transparent, and time-bound grievance redressal
Multiple channels for grievance submission, mandatory registration, digital tracking and escalation of unresolved grievances
Enquiry to be completed within 7 working days and grievances to be resolved within 15 days
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 11:16AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, has notified the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G – Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026, establishing a structured, multi-tier and time-bound mechanism for addressing grievances relating to the implementation of the Scheme. The Rules aim to make grievance redressal more accessible, transparent and accountable, while ensuring that citizens' concerns receive timely attention and appropriate action.

Multi-tier grievance redressal mechanism

The Rules provide for the establishment of a time-bound, multi-tier grievance redressal mechanism by State Governments at the Gram Panchayat, Block and District levels. Designated Grievance Redressal Officers at the appropriate levels will be responsible for receiving, registering, enquiring into and disposing of grievances.

The District Programme Coordinator will oversee grievance redressal at the district level and ensure that grievances are addressed through the designated mechanism and the Digital Public Infrastructure for grievance redressal.

Multiple channels for submission of grievances

To facilitate easy access, any person may submit a grievance relating to any matter arising out of or connected with the implementation of the Scheme. The Rules provide for submission of grievances through multiple channels:

  • In person before the designated Grievance Redressal Officer;
  • Through speed post, with proof of delivery;
  • Through the Digital Public Infrastructure for Redressal of Grievances designated by the Central Government; and
  • Through telephone, designated helplines or any other mode decided by the State Government.

Grievances received in physical form at the Gram Panchayat, Block or District level must be entered and registered on the designated Digital Public Infrastructure on the day of receipt or, where this is not feasible, by the next working day.

Upon registration, the complainant will receive an acknowledgement containing the registration number, date of receipt and designation of the receiving authority. The acknowledgement will be provided electronically in cases of digital submission and in physical form where the grievance is received physically.

Importantly, no grievance can be refused registration on the grounds of its format, language, manner of submission or any procedural deficiency. This provision ensures that citizens can access the grievance redressal mechanism without being hindered by procedural requirements.

Defined timelines for enquiry and resolution

The Rules prescribe clear timelines to ensure prompt examination and resolution of grievances. The designated Grievance Redressal Officer is required to examine every registered grievance and undertake the necessary enquiry. For this purpose, the officer may call for relevant records, registers, documents, reports, electronic data or other information from the concerned authorities or functionaries.

Where necessary, the complainant will be provided a reasonable opportunity to be heard, either in person or through electronic means, before the grievance is disposed of.

The enquiry into a grievance is required to be completed within seven working days from the date of its receipt. Upon completion of the enquiry, the Grievance Redressal Officer will record the findings and take, or cause to be taken, appropriate corrective or remedial action in accordance with the Act and the Rules. The grievance is required to be resolved within 15 days from the date of its receipt.

The findings and action taken will be recorded on the designated Digital Public Infrastructure and communicated to the complainant. Where a grievance has been received in physical form, its outcome and the action taken will also be communicated to the complainant in physical form.

Digital tracking and escalation of unresolved grievances

The designated Digital Public Infrastructure will facilitate end-to-end tracking of grievances, from registration to final disposal. It will also enable electronic recording of the enquiry, findings and action taken, thereby strengthening transparency and accountability in the grievance redressal process.

Any grievance that remains unresolved within the prescribed period of 15 days will be escalated to the next higher level through the grievance redressal mechanism established by the State Government. The authority receiving the escalated grievance will examine the matter and take appropriate action for its disposal. Such grievances will continue to be monitored electronically until their resolution.

Provision for appeals

The Rules also provide for appeals against orders passed under the grievance redressal mechanism. Such appeals will be filed and disposed of in accordance with Schedule I to the VB–G RAM G Act, 2025.

Through these Rules, the Government seeks to institutionalise a citizen-centric, accessible and time-bound grievance redressal framework under VB–G RAM G. The multi-tier institutional mechanism, multiple channels for grievance submission, mandatory registration, defined timelines, digital tracking and escalation of unresolved grievances are expected to strengthen administrative accountability and improve the responsiveness of the Scheme's implementation.

The notification marks an important step towards ensuring that grievances relating to the implementation of VB–G RAM G are addressed systematically, transparently and within prescribed timelines, thereby reinforcing the rights and entitlements of rural households under the Scheme.

2331385.title: Khet Bachaao Abhiyaan - Rabi 2026
2331385.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Khet Bachaao Abhiyaan - Rabi 2026
“Soil Health and Sustainable Agriculture”
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi

Khet Bachaao Abhiyaan (KBA)-Rabi 2026 is a nationwide campaign running from 22 October to 30 November 2026. It promotes soil health, balanced fertiliser use, and sustainable agriculture across 34 States and Union Territories, over 700 districts and 50,000 villages, targeting around 50 lakh farmers. Key priorities include balanced nutrient management, natural farming, crop residue management, crop diversification and climate-resilient agriculture. The campaign envisages 4,150 teams involving KVKs and ATMA, supported by over 12,000 scientists and ATMA functionaries. The initiative seeks to conduct 50,000 field demonstrations and 11,750 structured training sessions. The campaign projects a social media outreach of 1.5 crore farmers, with an envisaged expansion of overall digital outreach to 2.5 crore.

 

The Foundation of Farming Lies Beneath

Soil health is fundamental to agricultural productivity, food security, and rural livelihoods. With more than 46 percent of India’s workforce engaged in agriculture and allied activities, soil health influences food systems and economic stability. Healthy soils support higher crop yields and reduce dependence on external inputs.

Recognising the importance of soil health, Khet Bachaao Abhiyaan (KBA) - Rabi 2026 “Swasth Dhara, Samriddh Kisan” is envisaged as a nationwide campaign from 22 October to 30 November 2026. It follows a convergence-based approach, bringing together agricultural departments, research institutions, and field-level functionaries to promote balanced, judicious fertiliser use and sustainable nutrient management. The campaign aims to promote sustainable agriculture, improve soil health, and encourage the judicious use of agricultural resources. It also promotes natural farming, water conservation, and efficient use of natural resources. It addresses concerns such as imbalanced nutrient application, declining soil organic matter, rising cultivation costs, and the degradation of natural resources.

The initiatives also emphasise capacity building, farm mechanisation, and demonstrations of improved agricultural technologies, including regenerative agriculture practices (farming methods focused on restoring soil health and enhancing biodiversity).

The campaign covers 34 States and Union Territories, over 700 districts and 50,000 villages. It aims to reach around 50 lakh farmers through coordinated activities. States and Union Territories have been instructed to prioritise 100 high fertiliser-consuming districts to strengthen outreach and promote balanced nutrient management.  

Through its wide reach and field-level activities, the campaign seeks to bring farmers, scientists and agricultural institutions together. This coordinated effort is expected to encourage informed farming decisions and greater adoption of sustainable agricultural practices.

 

Khet Bachaao Abhiyaan

(From 1 to 30 June 2026)

Khet Bachaao Abhiyaan was launched nationwide on 1 June 2026 as a month-long campaign to promote soil health, balanced fertiliser use and sustainable agricultural practices. The campaign deployed 1,657 multidisciplinary teams for direct field-level engagement. The initiative achieved significant outreach, conducting over 1.34 lakh awareness events for 92.44 lakh farmers, and 6,685 training sessions on green manuring and bio-fertilisers, benefiting 4.94 lakh farmers. Additionally, 3,167 field demonstrations and 4,779 interactive programs provided hands-on learning. A further 4,916 Janpratinidhi Sammelans, including those involving fertiliser and input dealers, strengthened grassroots engagement.. Overall, the campaign directly reached around 1.07 crore farmers and other stakeholders, while social media outreach covered approximately 4.5 crore citizens.

Key Objectives of Khet Bachaao Abhiyaan - Rabi 2026

The campaign aims to encourage farmers to adopt location-specific, science-based practices that improve input-use efficiency and support climate-resilient agriculture.

  • Balanced Nutrient Management: Promote General Fertiliser Recommendations (GFR) based nutrient management and the 4R Principle of fertiliser use -  Right source, Right rate, Right time, and Right place. This method ensures balanced, efficient fertiliser use aligned with Rabi crop requirements.
  • Natural Farming: Encourage the adoption of natural farming through awareness campaigns, capacity building, demonstrations and farmer-to-farmer learning.
  • Integrated Nutrient Management (INM): Promote INM and the use of suitable organic and biological inputs through awareness, capacity building and demonstrations.
  • Crop Residue Management: Promote sustainable residue management and discourage crop residue burning in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh through Information, Education and Communication (IEC) activities.
  • Crop Diversification: Strengthen oilseed and pulse production, encourage crop diversification and promote the productive use of rice-fallow areas through awareness, capacity building and demonstrations.

  • Climate-Resilient Agriculture: Implement location-specific contingency plans in drought-affected areas of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan to support climate-resilient crop and resource management.
  • Awareness of Agricultural Schemes: Create awareness about government schemes related to agriculture and their benefits.
  • Integrated Pest Management and Pesticide Stewardship: Promote awareness of pesticide quality and safe use, encourage Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and safe, need-based, label-compliant pesticide use, and discourage indiscriminate application.

 

Dhaincha and Green Gram Offer a Path to Healthier Soils

In the rice-growing areas of East Champaran, Bihar, maintaining soil fertility while managing fertiliser use is an important concern for farmers. Declining soil organic carbon and micronutrient deficiencies add to the challenge. Under Khet Bachaao Abhiyaan-2026, the ICAR-Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute (MGIFRI), Motihari, Bihar, highlighted how green manuring and biological nitrogen fixation can support soil health.

At the farmer outreach programme at the Pantoka Panchayat in Raxaul Block, East Champaran District, Bihar, farmers were encouraged to combine farmyard manure, compost, biofertilisers and crop residues with recommended fertiliser doses. The discussions covered rice nursery management and alternatives to crop residue burning, including composting, mulching and vermicomposting.

Scientists also emphasised the use of dhaincha (Sesbania sp.) and summer green gram in rice-based cropping systems. Dhaincha can contribute around 50-60 kg of nitrogen per hectare, equivalent to 110-130 kg of urea. Summer green gram can contribute 25-30 kg of nitrogen per hectare, equivalent to 55-65 kg of urea. These crops can help reduce fertiliser requirements while improving soil organic matter and biological activity.

The programme brought together 62 farmers, including 41 women. Participants expressed willingness to adopt green manuring and balanced nutrient management.

Bringing the Campaign to Farmers: Institutional Roles and Responsibilities

  • State/UT Department of Agriculture: Responsible for campaign planning and implementation, issuing necessary instructions, convening preparatory meetings, approving district-level schedules, mobilising field personnel and convergence partners, facilitating access to schemes and services, and consolidating reports.
  • Agricultural Technology Management Agencies (ATMA) and District Agriculture Administration: Responsible for coordinating campaign activities across district, block and village levels, preparing micro-plans, mobilising farmers and community institutions, facilitating venues, field access, IEC materials and logistics, and maintaining attendance and activity records.
  • ICAR Institutes, Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs), Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), and Agricultural Universities (Knowledge Partners): Provide science-based technical guidance and location-specific recommendations, nominate resource persons, support training, conduct demonstrations and farmer-scientist interactions when requested, prepare or validate technical IEC materials and advisories, share research evidence, and document lessons. Their role does not extend to State-level implementation, administrative control, enforcement or expenditure responsibilities unless separately authorised.

 

The campaign envisages 4,150 teams involving KVKs and ATMA. More than 12,000 scientists and ATMA functionaries are expected to help implement it. Through ATMA and ICAR, the campaign aims to reach approximately one crore participants.

  • Other State Departments and Agencies: Support and facilitate campaign activities, as relevant to their respective mandates, through coordinated engagement by departments and agencies responsible for horticulture, soil and water conservation, irrigation, animal husbandry, rural development, cooperatives, Panchayati Raj, environment, agricultural marketing and allied sectors.
  • Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs) and Progressive Farmers: Support local mobilisation, peer learning, demonstration visits and dissemination of validated advisories among farmers.
  • Media and Communication Partners: Facilitate the dissemination of approved campaign messages through local media, community radio, WhatsApp, Kisan Sarathi and other appropriate communication platforms, while ensuring the accuracy and verification of agronomic information shared with farmers.

Driving Farmer Awareness and Outreach

The campaign combines farmer awareness, capacity building, field demonstrations, practical exposure visits, and digital outreach to promote improved agricultural practices, strengthen technical knowledge, and extend the reach of campaign messages among farmers.

Awareness Creation for Various Activities

The campaign seeks to enhance farmers’ awareness and understanding of General Fertiliser Recommendations GFR-based nutrient management, natural farming, Integrated Nutrient Management (INM), Crop Residue Management (CRM), and improved technologies for oilseed and pulse production. It also disseminates information on Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for implementing contingency plans in drought-affected districts and key government schemes related to agriculture.

  • Each of the 950 ICAR institute teams is assigned three village visits per week, while the 700 KVK teams are expected to undertake four visits per week. Each visit targets the participation of 100 farmers.
  • Over a five-week period, the campaign envisages 5,650 awareness programmes, with an estimated outreach of 28.25 lakh farmers.

Capacity Building of Farmers

Training programmes are designed to strengthen farmers’ knowledge and technical capacities in Integrated Nutrient Management (INM), Crop Residue Management (CRM), natural farming, improved oilseed and pulse production practices, Integrated Pest Management (IPM), and other relevant thematic areas.

  • Each of the 950 ICAR institute teams is expected to conduct one training programme per week, while the 700 KVK teams are assigned two programmes per week. Each programme targets 40 participants.
  • Over a five-week period, the campaign envisages 11,750 training programmes, with an estimated outreach of 4.70 lakh farmers.

Demonstrations at Farmers’ Fields

ICAR institutes and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) organise field demonstrations at selected farmers’ fields to illustrate the potential and benefits of improved agricultural technologies. These demonstrations enable farmers to assess scientific interventions and compare their outcomes with existing farming practices. The key areas covered include Green Ammonia, Crop Residue Management (CRM), Integrated Nutrient Management (INM), Integrated Pest Management (IPM), natural farming, Integrated Crop Management (ICM) for oilseeds and pulses, biofertilisers, and organic and biological inputs.

  • The campaign envisages 50,000 field demonstrations, comprising 40,000 by KVKs and 10,000 by ICAR institutes.
  • With an intended participation of 20 farmers per demonstration, the initiative targets an estimated outreach of 10 lakh farmers.

Field Days, Harvest Days and Exposure Visits

Field days, harvest events and exposure visits to demonstration sites constitute an integral component of the campaign’s “Seeing is Believing” approach. These activities provide farmers with first-hand opportunities to observe improved agricultural technologies, understand their practical applications and assess their benefits under field conditions.

  • Each of the 1,650 teams is assigned to organise three field or harvest days and two exposure visits during the crop season, with each activity targeting approximately 125 farmers.
  • These activities are expected to collectively reach approximately 10 lakh farmers.

Social Media Outreach

Digital platforms serve as an important channel for disseminating information on improved agricultural practices, technical advisories, and campaign-related activities, thereby extending the campaign’s outreach beyond field-level interventions.

  • Organising teams to disseminate daily updates through WhatsApp, Facebook, X, and other appropriate digital platforms.
  • The campaign projects a social media outreach of 1.5 crore farmers, with an envisaged expansion of overall digital outreach to 2.5 crore.

Connecting Farmers with Schemes and Services

The campaign undertakes targeted awareness initiatives to familiarise farmers with key agricultural schemes, services and practices. These include PM-KISAN, balanced pesticide use, Soil Health Cards, the applicable fertiliser sale framework and the potential benefits of trade agreements. It also facilitates the creation and updating of Farmers’ IDs and disseminates information on crop insurance coverage under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY). In addition, saturation drives under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme seek to facilitate eligible farmers’ access to institutional credit.

Collectively, these interventions seek to strengthen farmers’ awareness of government support mechanisms and improve their access to essential agricultural services, formal credit and risk-mitigation instruments, thereby reinforcing the institutional and financial foundations of farm livelihoods.

Strengthening the Foundations of Sustainable Agriculture

The Khet Bachaao Abhiyaan-Rabi 2026 seeks to place soil health and sustainable resource management at the centre of agricultural development. Through convergence among scientific institutions, government departments, extension networks and farming communities, it aims to translate scientific knowledge into location-specific agricultural practices. Its integrated approach combines farmer awareness, capacity building, field demonstrations and digital outreach to promote improved farming practices. Alongside balanced nutrient management, natural farming and efficient input use, the campaign emphasises crop diversification, residue management, integrated pest management and climate resilience. Its focus on institutional coordination and farmer participation also strengthens grassroots extension mechanisms and access to agricultural services.

These interventions support resource-efficient farming systems, healthier soils and resilient agricultural livelihoods, contributing to the broader vision of Viksit Bharat. Furthermore, the campaign supports progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly Zero Hunger (SDG 2) and Climate Action (SDG 13).

2331377.title: Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha Arrive at Tawang Monastery; Exposition Marks a Significant Moment in Arunachal Pradesh's Buddhist Heritage
2331377.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha Arrive at Tawang Monastery; Exposition Marks a Significant Moment in Arunachal Pradesh's Buddhist Heritage
Sacred Piprahwa Relics brought to Tawang from the National Museum, New Delhi, for public veneration
Exposition to travel across Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai from 31 October to 21 November 2026
Initiative strengthens India's commitment to preserving and sharing its Buddhist civilisational heritage
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 9:37AM by PIB Delhi

The sacred Holy Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha from the National Museum, New Delhi, were ceremonially received by the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, at Tawang on 31st October, 2026, marking the commencement of a significant exposition of India's Buddhist heritage in Arunachal Pradesh. The sacred relics were accorded a traditional religious reception at the historic Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery), in the presence of Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, venerable Buddhist monks, religious leaders and devotees.

The exposition is being organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC) and the National Museum, New Delhi. It will provide devotees and members of the public an opportunity to pay homage to the sacred relics across three important centres of Buddhist faith - Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai.

The inaugural programme at Tawang was attended by Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, along with the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, venerable Buddhist monks, representatives of International Buddhist Confederation, other dignitaries and devotees.

In his message on the occasion, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi expressed happiness over the exposition of the Holy Relics of Bhagwan Buddha in Arunachal Pradesh, describing it as an occasion of immense spiritual and cultural significance. He highlighted the homecoming of the sacred Piprahwa Relics after more than a century as a moment of pride and joy, and expressed confidence that the exposition would further strengthen appreciation of India's rich Buddhist heritage and the universal teachings of Bhagwan Buddha.

The exposition holds special spiritual significance as it coincides with Lhabab Duchen, an important occasion in the Tibetan Buddhist tradition commemorating the Buddha's descent from the heavenly realm.

The sacred relics originate from Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh, an archaeological site associated with ancient Kapilavastu and the Shakya tradition of Lord Buddha. Preserved at the National Museum, New Delhi, these relics hold immense historical, archaeological and spiritual significance for Buddhist communities.

An accompanying exhibition, titled Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery, will present the history of the archaeological discoveries at Piprahwa, the significance of relic veneration and the journey of the Piprahwa heritage, including its repatriation to India.

The International Buddhist Confederation, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, will also organise an international conference titled “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond” at the Kalawangpo Convention Hall, Tawang, on 2 November 2026.

The exposition will continue at Tawang Monastery from 1 to 7 November, followed by TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila, from 8 to 13 November and the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, from 14 to 20 November 2026. The sacred relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026.

The exposition represents an important initiative to bring India's Buddhist heritage closer to communities in the North Eastern Region, while promoting the universal teachings of Bhagwan Buddha - peace, compassion, non-violence and harmony.

Through such initiatives, the Government of India continues its efforts to preserve, promote and disseminate the country's rich Buddhist heritage and strengthen India's historical and spiritual connections with Buddhist communities across the world.

2331376.title: Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal holds high-level meetings with European Commission officials and industry representatives in Brussels
2331376.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal holds high-level meetings with European Commission officials and industry representatives in Brussels
India and EU Discuss Trade Facilitation, Market Access and Deeper Cooperation in Sustainable Development and Green Technologies
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 9:34AM by PIB Delhi

Commerce Secretary, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, held high-level meetings in Brussels with Ms. Ditte Juul Jørgensen, Director-General, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security (DG TRADE); Mr. Koen Doens, Director-General, Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA); and Mr. Gerassimos Thomas, Director-General, Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union (DG TAXUD), European Commission. The meetings focused on strengthening the comprehensive economic and strategic partnership between India and the European Union.

During the meeting with Ms. Ditte Juul Jørgensen, both sides discussed measures to facilitate two-way trade, improve market access, strengthen supply chain resilience and create new opportunities for businesses in India and the European Union. They reaffirmed their commitment to a fair, balanced and mutually beneficial agreement and agreed to maintain close engagement to address the remaining procedural and implementation-related issues.

In the meeting with Mr. Koen Doens, both sides exchanged views on strengthening India–EU development cooperation and strategic partnerships, with discussions covering sustainable development, clean energy, green technologies and related areas.

The meeting with Mr. Gerassimos Thomas focused on customs cooperation, trade facilitation and preparations for the implementation of the India–EU FTA. Both sides recognised the importance of efficient, transparent and digitally enabled customs procedures in supporting businesses, reducing transaction costs and ensuring the smooth movement of legitimate trade.

Shri Agrawal also met stakeholders from the diamond industry, including representatives associated with the Antwerp diamond ecosystem. The discussions covered the global diamond value chain, certification and traceability requirements, responsible sourcing, and opportunities arising from India's growing diamond market and manufacturing ecosystem. India and Belgium have identified gems and jewellery as an important area for deeper cooperation, with Antwerp, Mumbai and Surat recognised as major diamond centres.

The Commerce Secretary participated in a BusinessEurope roundtable with European industry representatives to discuss opportunities for strengthening trade and investment ties, improving market access, enhancing supply chain resilience and advancing cooperation under the India–EU FTA. He highlighted India's strong economic growth, reform momentum and investment opportunities across key sectors, and invited European businesses to deepen their engagement with India and participate in its expanding value chains.

The engagements reflect the growing breadth of India–EU cooperation across trade, investment, development partnership, taxation and customs, and reaffirm the shared commitment of both sides to further strengthening their strategic partnership.

 

Commerce Secretary Shri @RajeshAgrawal94, Commerce Secretary, had an informal interaction with representatives of the diamond industry at the Embassy of India Brussels on 30 Oct 2026. He exchanged views with industry members on global diamond trade, emerging market trends, and highlighted the long-standing India-Belgium linkages in the diamond value chain. @PIB_India

2331374.title: Hon’ble Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh to Visit Gangtok and Mangan Districts of Sikkim on 2–3 November 2026
2331374.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2331374.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Hon’ble Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh to Visit Gangtok and Mangan Districts of Sikkim on 2–3 November 2026
Projects and initiatives worth ₹251.56 lakh to be inaugurated and launched to strengthen dairy development and livestock infrastructure
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 6:39AM by PIB Delhi

The Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Alias Lalan Singh), will visit Gangtok and Mangan districts of Sikkim from 2–3 November 2026. During the visit, the Hon’ble Union Minister will review dairy development initiatives and inaugurate a microbiology laboratory for the Sikkim Milk Union under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD). He will also launch initiatives for the establishment of 57 new Dairy Cooperative Societies (DCSs) under White Revolution 2.0 and distribute registration certificates to five newly registered DCSs. Additionally, the formation of 15 new DCSs in North Sikkim will be launched, enabling more dairy farmers to become part of the cooperative dairy network. A traceability initiative for Churpi cheese manufactured in Gangtok and Jorethang will also be unveiled.

The Hon’ble Union Minister will further promote two Fodder Plus Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) for the Sikkim Milk Union under the Government of India's 10,000 FPO Scheme. He will also unveil new products, including organic honey, Niger seed-blended powder, and organic biscuits and sweets made from millets and buckwheat, marking a significant step towards product diversification and value addition.

The visit will be attended by senior officials of the Government of Sikkim, the Mangan District Administration, representatives of the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, relevant line ministries, the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), dairy farmers, Dairy Cooperative Societies and Dairy Farmer Producer Organisations.

Sikkim has played a significant role in dairy development in the North Eastern Region (NER), with milk production of approximately 89.35 thousand metric tonnes and per capita milk availability of around 352 grams per day during 2024–25. To support the growth of the dairy sector in the state, DAHD has released ₹7,093.99 lakh under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) since 2014. Furthermore, a special project worth ₹2,763.92 lakh has been sanctioned for the development and conservation of the indigenous Siri cattle breed.

For the development and conservation of yak in Sikkim, an amount of ₹100 lakh was released during 2023–24. Additionally, ₹100 lakh has been released during the current financial year 2026–27 for the procurement of High Genetic Merit (HGM) yak bulls under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission.

Under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD), DAHD has sanctioned nine projects with a total outlay of ₹59.60 crore, including a Central share of ₹54.61 crore. Of this amount, ₹53.59 crore has been released, while ₹52.61 crore has been utilised.

Under the National Livestock Mission (NLM), DAHD has provided financial assistance amounting to ₹1,914.39 lakh for fodder production, ₹530.62 lakh for livestock insurance, ₹408.64 lakh for small ruminant and pig breed improvement, and ₹359.80 lakh for training and extension activities during FY 2020–21 to date.

The visit of the Hon’ble Union Minister underscores the Government of India's recognition of Sikkim's contribution and its importance in the dairy and animal husbandry sectors. The infrastructure and initiatives being undertaken are expected to strengthen the livelihoods of farmers and livestock rearers, promote value addition, improve supply-chain infrastructure and create new opportunities for income generation. These initiatives will also facilitate better market access for locally produced goods, including access to premium and international markets, thereby contributing to sustainable growth in the state's dairy and livestock sectors.

******

2331368.title: ‘Khadi Diwali Fest-2026’ organized at Connaught Place, Delhi, with the objective of taking Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call of  ‘ Har Ghar  Swadeshi, Ghar Ghar Swadehi’  to Gen-Z
2331368.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
‘Khadi Diwali Fest-2026’ organized at Connaught Place, Delhi, with the objective of taking Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call of  ‘ Har Ghar  Swadeshi, Ghar Ghar Swadehi’  to Gen-Z
‘Khadi Fest-2026’, themed ‘Khadi-wali Diwali’ inaugurated by KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goyal
“Purchasing Khadi, Swadeshi, and local products during the festive season will strengthen Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat”: KVIC Chairman
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 10:14PM by PIB Delhi

To disseminate Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Swadeshi in every home,’ ‘Vocal for Local,’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ among the masses, the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) organized the ‘Khadi Diwali Fest-2026’ at NDMC Palika Park, Connaught Place, New Delhi (opposite Regal Cinema). The event featured a special interaction with media representatives and a ‘Diwali Milan’ (Diwali get together). KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel joined the event as the chief guest. Held under the theme ‘Khadi-wali Diwali,’ the event aims to encourage citizens to adopt Khadi and Swadeshi products during Diwali and other festivals, provide greater recognition to the creations of Indian artisans and rural entrepreneurs, and, in particular, connect the youth with the Swadeshi movement.

Speaking on the occasion, KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel opined that the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, envisioned Khadi not merely as a fabric, but as a symbol of self-reliance, self-respect, and economic independence. Today, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Khadi and *Swadeshi* (indigenous) movement has gained new momentum and widespread public participation. The Prime Minister’s call for Har Ghar  Swadeshi, Ghar Ghar Swadehi’   extends beyond the mere purchase of indigenous goods; it s a comprehensive campaign aimed at fostering a sense of pride in Indian products, encouraging local producers, and strengthening the nation’s economic self-reliance.

Shri Goel reitrerated that the festive season is of immense significance to the Indian economy, local markets, and artisans. If every family prioritizes Khadi and other *Swadeshi* products during the festive season, the direct benefits reach millions of artisans, weavers, rural entrepreneurs, and their families across the country. He emphasized that purchasing *Swadeshi* products is not just a consumer choice, but a vital contribution by citizens toward strengthening the national economy and local employment.

The KVIC Chairman specifically urged the youth—including Gen-Z—to join the *Swadeshi* movement, highlighting that today’s youth are highly conscious of fashion, design, technology, and innovative ideas. By integrating Khadi and village industry products with modern designs, attractive presentation, superior branding, and contemporary lifestyles, these items can become even more popular among the youth. He added that young people can be more than just consumers of *Swadeshi* products; they can also serve as brand ambassadors, designers, digital promoters and entrepreneurs.

Shri Goel said that the role of the youth is crucial in realizing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of "Local to Global." Through social media, e-commerce, digital marketing, and startups, the youth can help take Khadi and village industry products to every nook and corner of the country, while also establishing a new identity for them in international markets. He further stated that to convey Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Viksit Bharat @ 2047’ and the ‘Vocal for Local’ initiative to the younger generation, KVIC has launched a podcast titled ‘Baat Khadi Ki’. Through this, efforts are being made to connect Gen-Z with Khadi and the *Swadeshi* (indigenous) movement by exploring topics such as the legacy of Khadi, modern fashion, innovation, and youth entrepreneurship. This initiative will help popularize Khadi among the new generation and strengthen the resolve for an *Atmanirbhar Bharat* (Self-reliant India).

Interacting with media representatives, Shri Goel noted that the Khadi and Village Industries sector has witnessed unprecedented progress, driven by the visionary thinking and policies of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. In the financial year 2025-26, the turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector exceeded Rs 1.87 lakh crore, while the sector has provided employment to over 2.04 crore people. He expressed confidence that, in the near future, the sector will achieve a turnover target of Rs 2.51 lakh crore.

The ‘Khadi Diwali Fest-2026,’ which commenced on October 31, offers a special discount of 20 percent on Khadi products and 10 percent on Village Industry products. This festival reinforces the message that this Diwali, we should not only light *diyas* (lamps) in our homes but also spread the light of joy in the lives of millions of artisans and rural families across the country by embracing Khadi and Swadeshi products.

***

2331362.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses the ‘Shatabdi Samaroh 2026’ organised by the Akhil Vishwa Gayatri Pariwar in New Delhi
2331362.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses the ‘Shatabdi Samaroh 2026’ organised by the Akhil Vishwa Gayatri Pariwar in New Delhi
The ‘Shatabdi Samaroh 2026’ of Gayatri Pariwar is the confluence of the sacred streams of 100 years of Akhand Jyoti, Vandaniya Mataji, and the sadhana of Pujya Acharya ji
One flame is enough to light a lamp, but to keep it burning uninterruptedly for 100 years requires austerity, sacrifice and resolve - only then does it awaken crores of souls, as the Gayatri Pariwar has done
Just as the number 100 is regarded as a symbol of completeness, this year is also a year of completeness for Indian culture and the spiritual journey
Like a lamp, Vandaniya Mata ji illuminated the path for others by performing austerities herself
Her spirit of sacrifice and service is the core essence of the Gayatri Pariwar
The great service rendered by Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya by taking Gayatri Mantra to the masses is as profound as the contribution made by the sages and epoch-makers to Indian culture
By generating faith in the Gayatri Mantra, Gurudev has given Indian spirituality and spiritual power a new life for the next hundred years
The flame that was lit 100 years ago has today become a symbol of human welfare, reaching more than 15 crore family members across over 100 countries
The Gayatri Mantra is not merely a religious ritual; it is the path to complete transformation
The 24 letters of the Gayatri Mantra are connected with our auspicious nodes
 When these powers are awakened, inauspicious tendencies are subdued and auspicious powers emerge
In a person in whom the 24 auspicious qualities arise, the path to liberation automatically opens
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 9:46PM by PIB Delhi

 Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the ‘Shatabdi Samaroh 2026’ organised by the Akhil Vishwa Gayatri Pariwar in New Delhi. The ‘Shatabdi Samaroh 2026’ is being organised to mark the completion of 100 years of the birth of Param Vandaniya Mataji of Akhil Vishwa Gayatri Pariwar and manifestation of Akhand Jyoti. On this occasion, Union Minister Shri Durgadas Uikey, Dalnayak of Gayatri Pariwar Dr. Chinmay Pandya, and several other dignitaries were present.

Addressing the ceremony, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that today is a day of faith, service and resolve. We have gathered here with reverence for Param Vandaniya Mata Bhagwati Devi Sharma, to serve in accordance with the core spirit of the Gayatri Pariwar, and with the resolve to build the India of the dreams of Maharshi Aurobindo and Swami Vivekananda. Shri Shah said that the 100 years of the manifestation of Akhand Jyoti, the 100 years of the birth of Vandaniya Mataji, and the 100 years of the sadhana of Pujya Gurudev Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya — the confluence of these three sacred streams is taking place this year. He said that the number 100 is regarded as a symbol of completeness. This year is also, in a way, a year of completeness for Indian culture and the Indian spiritual journey.

Shri Amit Shah said that Pujya Mataji herself performed austerities and illuminated the path for others. The flame that was lit 100 years ago has today become a symbol of welfare for countless people across more than 100 countries and in over 15 crore families.

The Home Minister said that in the four-day conference held in Haridwar this January, the entire Gayatri Pariwar had united and identified itself with the resolve of this Jyoti. Today, in the next stage of the same journey, two important events are taking place. The first is the ‘Deep Mahayajna’, which symbolises sacrifice, cooperation and dedication. Every lamp that is lit is a resolve that we shall use our strength for society, spirituality and the nation.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that, based on his experience, he believes the Gayatri Mantra is the path to complete transformation. It is not merely a religious or spiritual ritual. By experiencing the positive energy inherent in the mantra and enabling the mind, body and soul to realise it, it becomes a great path for bringing out the ‘sattva’ (essence) within us to the fullest. Shri Shah said that the 24 letters of the Gayatri Mantra are directly connected with our 24 auspicious nodes. Taking the 24 letters of the Gayatri Mantra as the foundation and receiving the sanskar (values) of its pure pronunciation from one’s Guru, if we awaken the 24 auspicious powers, the inauspicious powers lying within us are subdued and the auspicious powers emerge. He said that these 24 auspicious powers are linked with 24 kinds of attributes, which include foresight, restraint, austerity, courage, discrimination, intellect, protection, production, service, vitality, love, valour, concentration and others. He said that in a person in whom these 24 auspicious qualities arise, the path to ‘moksha’ (liberation) automatically opens and God leads him in that direction.

Shri Amit Shah said that the profound service rendered by Panditji by taking the Gayatri Mantra to the masses is as deep as the contribution made by the many sages, seekers and epoch-makers of India to Indian culture, our spiritual consciousness and the ‘sattva’ of the world. He said that Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya is the doctor of our spirituality. According to him, the chanting of the Gayatri Mantra awakens 24 kinds of auspicious nodes. When one correctly pronounces it from the navel to the mouth, these 24 nodes are activated and the internal secretions released from them develop the 24 auspicious powers.

The Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that many young people have benefited from the Gayatri Mantra. Their positive thinking, courage and memory power have increased, their capacity for interpretation has become sharper, and their decision-making ability has also improved. He said that Gurudev took these teachings to 15 crore families, and 15 crore families across the world is no small number. By generating faith in the Gayatri Mantra and establishing the tradition of its pure pronunciation, he not only uplifted the lives of individuals but also gave Indian spirituality and spiritual power a new life for the next hundred years. He said that we must continue to reiterate the clarion call of the digvijaya (victory in all directions) of this divine culture that he sounded, spread it, and carry it forward to the younger generation.

Shri Amit Shah said that a movement is rising through the Gayatri Pariwar, and it is the sacred duty of all of us to take it forward. This duty is to gather the auspicious forces of the entire world and guide the world onto the path of righteousness. We must continue this work until the last moment of our lives.

****

Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated various projects and laid the foundation stones for several others, worth ₹258 crore, of the Chandigarh Administration. On this occasion, Punjab Governor and Administrator of Chandigarh Shri Gulab Chand Kataria, along with several other dignitaries were present.

Addressing the gathering on the occasion, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Chandigarh was established on this day in 1966, Haryana was formed, and the Chandigarh Police came into existence. On this very day, the Chandigarh Police was also awarded the President’s Colour. He said that over the 60-year journey from 1966 to 2026, Chandigarh has earned recognition across the country for its urban planning and development. In a way, Chandigarh has become an integral part of the identity of the entire North India. Today, development projects worth ₹258 crore are being inaugurated and their foundation stones laid here.

Shri Amit Shah said that development works worth ₹258 crore, covering education, healthcare, justice, administration, research and innovation, are being inaugurated and their foundation stones laid today. He said that the City-UT Bus Depot, built at a cost of ₹68 crore, is being inaugurated. Type-3 residential quarters, constructed at a cost of ₹68 crore, have also been built to provide accommodation to police personnel. He expressed confidence that, before 2029, Chandigarh Police would rank first in the country in terms of residential satisfaction among police personnel.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that the Opposition has been losing elections for the past 15 years and has now found a new way in the form of a mock Parliament. He said that if their approach continues to be characterised by spreading falsehoods, creating disorder and negativity, disrupting the functioning of Parliament, and taking parliamentary issues to the streets to create a ruckus, they will once again have to sit in the Opposition for the next five years.

Shri Amit Shah said that, on the one hand, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is steering the country towards rapid progress and development. Article 370 has been abrogated, Naxalism has been eliminated, and Triple Talaq has been abolished. He said that by December 31, 2029, the entire country, including Punjab, will be made drug-free.

Shri Amit Shah said that, on the one hand, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is steering the country towards rapid progress and development. Article 370 has been abrogated, Naxalism has been eliminated, and Triple Talaq has been abolished. He said that by December 31, 2029, the entire country, including Punjab, will be made drug-free. He said that Prime Minister Modi is also driving the creation of world-class infrastructure across the country. The largest cricket stadium, the highest over-bridge and the longest bridge are being built in India today. Infrastructure projects worth ₹11 lakh crore are underway. He said that electricity and toilets have reached every poor household, every poor family has been brought into the banking system through bank accounts, and every poor person is receiving five kilograms of free food grains per month. Schools are being opened for children, while opposition leaders are disrupting the functioning of Parliament to prevent women from getting 33 per cent reservation. He asserted that providing 33 per cent reservation to the women of India is the firm resolve of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the government. The people of the country are closely observing all these developments and are well aware of who is making the country secure and developed, who is promoting innovation, who has introduced the New Education Policy, and who is making the country economically prosperous.

 

*****

2331297.title: Union Minister for Railways Flags Off Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express Train
2331297.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Union Minister for Railways Flags Off Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express Train
Union Ministers Pralhad Joshi, H. D. Kumaraswamy, Minister of State for Railways V. Somanna and Other Dignitaries Also Join Flag-off Ceremony
New Vande Bharat Sleeper Express to Enhance Connectivity Between Bengaluru and Mumbai, Connecting India's IT and Startup Capital with Its Financial Capital: Sh. Ashwini Vaishnaw
Modern Overnight Rail Connectivity to Benefit Professionals, Entrepreneurs, Students, Traders and Tourists
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw today flagged off the SMVT Bengaluru-Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express in the presence of Union Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister Shri H. D. Kumaraswamy, Minister of State for Railways Shri V. Somanna, Minister of State Sushri Shobha Karandlaje and other dignitaries. The flag-off ceremony marks an important step towards strengthening modern overnight rail connectivity between two of India's leading metropolitan and economic centres.

Hon’ble Minister of Railways Shri @AshwiniVaishnaw, along with other dignitaries, flagged off the Bengaluru–Mumbai #VandeBharat_Sleeper train. https://t.co/2Gro8cQO5B

— Ministry of Railways (@RailMinIndia) November 1, 2026

The introduction of this next-generation sleeper train will provide passengers with an additional modern, comfortable and efficient travel option between Bengaluru and Mumbai. The service is expected to benefit professionals, entrepreneurs, business travellers, students, traders and tourists while strengthening connectivity across important regional centres in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.

Following the introduction of Vande Bharat Sleeper services on the Howrah-Guwahati corridor in January 2026, and the flagging off of the Varanasi-New Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper train yesterday, the Bengaluru-Mumbai service further expands the network of modern overnight rail travel and reinforces Indian Railways' commitment to passenger-centric mobility.

Highlighting the introduction of the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express, Shri Vaishnaw said that the service would connect Bengaluru, the country's IT and startup capital, with Mumbai, its financial capital. The train will run via Anantapur and Guntakal in Andhra Pradesh; Raichur, Yadgir and Kalaburagi in Karnataka; and Solapur, Pune and Kalyan in Maharashtra, providing improved overnight connectivity to several parts of North Karnataka that previously lacked access to premium, world-class train services. He also announced that the next Vande Bharat Sleeper service for Karnataka would originate from Bengaluru, connect the northern parts of the state towards the Hubballi region and proceed towards Pune and Mumbai.

The Union Minister further announced that Vande Bharat services between Bengaluru and Mangaluru are expected to commence within the next few weeks, following the completion of electrification and successful testing on the route. The service will strengthen connectivity between Bengaluru and coastal Karnataka. He emphasised that the new service would provide faster, more comfortable and world-class rail connectivity to the region. He also highlighted the importance of modern railway infrastructure, technology-driven improvements and the expansion of high-speed services in strengthening passenger connectivity and supporting the economic development of Karnataka.

The Union Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw highlighted the expansion of high-speed rail connectivity in Karnataka and the development of new railway corridors to strengthen regional connectivity and promote economic integration. Highlighting the expected reduction in travel time, he stated that the Bengaluru-Chennai journey would take just 73 minutes, while Bengaluru-Hyderabad connectivity would be covered in approximately 2 hours and 10 minutes.

Union Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Railways in strengthening railway connectivity across Karnataka, particularly in North Karnataka. He highlighted the increased allocation of funds for railway infrastructure development and appreciated the significant progress made in railway development works in Karnataka. Shri Joshi emphasized that this robust investment has driven both infrastructure expansion and safety enhancements, pointing out that accident rates have plummeted from 135 to 16 following the rollout of the Kavach protection system, with a clear institutional target of achieving zero accidents. He also welcomed the introduction of new Vande Bharat services and the announcement of additional high-speed rail corridors, stating that these initiatives would improve passenger connectivity, enhance regional development and provide better access to modern rail services across Karnataka.

Union Minister Shri H. D. Kumaraswamy welcomed the introduction of the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper service, the proposed Vande Bharat connectivity between Bengaluru and Mangaluru, and the planned rail connectivity linking Bengaluru with Pune. He noted that these initiatives would benefit not only the people of Karnataka but also the large number of migrant workers and families from states such as West Bengal, Assam and Bihar residing in Bengaluru, while improving passenger convenience and regional connectivity.

Union Minister of State for Railways Shri V. Somanna mentioned the significant transformation of railway infrastructure in Karnataka, with emphasis on expediting long-pending projects, strengthening rail connectivity and improving passenger amenities across the state. He highlighted that railway infrastructure development works worth approximately ₹52,000 crore are underway in the State. He appreciated the efforts of the Railway Minister in restoring train services, accelerating the construction of railway overbridges and underbridges, and modernising railway stations across Bengaluru, district headquarters and other important centres.

Connecting Two Major Economic and Commercial Centres

The new Vande Bharat Sleeper Express will establish an important overnight rail link between Bengaluru, a leading hub for information technology, innovation, education and entrepreneurship, and Mumbai, the country's financial and commercial capital.

Both metropolitan centres witness substantial movement of professionals, entrepreneurs, students, business travellers and families. The new service will offer passengers an additional convenient travel option, enabling them to undertake long-distance journeys overnight and reach their destination the following day.

The train will connect important stations along its route, including Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Yadgir, Wadi, Kalaburagi, Solapur, Pune and Kalyan. This will strengthen connectivity across parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra, providing improved access to important commercial, educational and regional centres.

The train will depart SMVT Bengaluru at 19:45 hours and arrive at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Mumbai, at 11:55 hours the following day. In the return direction, it will depart CSMT at 20:10 hours and reach SMVT Bengaluru at 12:00 hours the next day. The service will operate six days a week, except Monday in the Bengaluru-originating direction and Tuesday in the Mumbai-originating direction.

The overnight schedule will allow passengers to make more effective use of their daytime while travelling comfortably between the two metropolitan centres. Passengers from cities and towns along the route will also benefit from an additional modern rail travel option.

The flag-off of the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express marks another important milestone in Indian Railways' ongoing efforts to transform passenger transportation through modern infrastructure, advanced technology and improved connectivity. Indian Railways remains committed to developing a modern, efficient, safe and passenger-centric transportation network that supports India's economic growth and connects metropolitan centres with emerging regional hubs.

*****

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj

2331287.title: National Zoological Park marks 67th Foundation Day with Creative Outreach Activity and Bird Walk
2331287.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2331287.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Zoological Park marks 67th Foundation Day with Creative Outreach Activity and Bird Walk
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi

The National Zoological Park (NZP), New Delhi, celebrated its 67th Foundation Day on 01.11.2026 with an engaging doodle activity for visitors, reaffirming its commitment to wildlife conservation, biodiversity awareness and environmental education. The activity received an enthusiastic response, with approximately 1,500 visitors appreciating and participating in the initiative. It provided an interactive and creative platform, particularly for children and families, to express their ideas and connect with the importance of protecting wildlife and nature.

On the occasion, Dr. Sanjeet Kumar, Director (NZP) highlighted, “The 67th Foundation Day is an important milestone in the Park’s journey and an occasion to renew our commitment to wildlife conservation, animal welfare, biodiversity protection and public engagement. A modern zoo is not merely a place to see animals; it is a centre for conservation, learning, research and inspiration. Every visitor, especially every child can become an ambassador for nature through informed and responsible choices”. He invited citizens to connect with the National Zoological Park, learn about rich biodiversity and join in protecting wildlife and the natural world for future generations.

As part of its ongoing efforts to encourage public participation in biodiversity monitoring and wildlife conservation, the National Zoological Park organised the 19th edition of ‘Sunday Bird Walk @ NZP’ today, from 7:30 AM to 10:30 AM. The walk was conducted under the expert guidance of Dr. Paritosh Ahmed, Ornithologist, with the support of dedicated volunteers.

A total of 18 participants, including bird enthusiasts, nature lovers, students, wildlife photographers and citizens interested in biodiversity, took part in the programme. During the walk, participants recorded 46 bird species and observed more than 500 individual birds in the designated area. The observations contributed to field-level biodiversity documentation and provided participants with a practical opportunity to engage in citizen science. The expert shared insights into bird ecology, behaviour and conservation, highlighting the role of birds in maintaining ecological balance including through natural pest control and their value as indicators of ecosystem health.

Addressing the participants, Director (NZP) emphasised that nature walks strengthen field-identification skills, deepen understanding of ecological relationships and food webs, support biodiversity documentation and foster a lasting appreciation of wildlife conservation. To ensure meaningful learning and effective participation, each Sunday Bird Walk is limited to 20–25 participants. Prior registration is mandatory, and places are allotted on a first-come, first-served basis. The registration form remains open from Monday to Friday each week. The link is available on the official website of the National Zoological Park and through the NZP Saathi mobile application.

2331238.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE BALIDAN SHATABDI SAMAROH OF SWAMI SHRADDHANAND JI AT KURUKSHETRA
2331238.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE BALIDAN SHATABDI SAMAROH OF SWAMI SHRADDHANAND JI AT KURUKSHETRA
SWAMI SHRADDHANAND JI’S LIFE JOURNEY AND SACRIFICE ARE A SOURCE OF INSPIRATION FOR ALL: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu graced Balidan Shatabdi Samaroh of Swami Shraddhanand Ji at Gurukul, Kurukshetra, Haryana today (November 1, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President paid her tribute to Swami Shraddhanand Ji on the 100th anniversary of his martyrdom. She said that his life journey from Munshiram to Mahatma Munshiram and eventually to Swami Shraddhanand is deeply inspiring.

The President said that Swami Shraddhanand Ji had dedicated his life to the service of the Vedas and the upliftment of society. His life journey and sacrifice are a source of inspiration for all of us. 

The President said that Swami Shraddhanand Ji was a strong advocate of social unity. In an address delivered from the platform of the Jama Masjid in Delhi, he conveyed a message of mutual goodwill and national unity.

The President said that Swami Shraddhanand Ji believed that eradicating the stigma of untouchability and uplifting the Dalits were the most essential steps for the progress of India. In his view, the evil practice of untouchability was contrary to the core principles of the Vedic tradition.

The President said that Swami Shraddhanand Ji revived and strengthened the Gurukul system of education. This breathed new life into the stream of Indian education and culture. He made tireless efforts to revive the ancient Aryan system of education, a cause championed by Maharshi Dayanand Saraswati, the founder of the Arya Samaj.

The President said that the Centenary Year of Swami Shraddhanand Ji’s martyrdom serves as an opportunity to draw lessons from his inspiring life, his educational and social philosophy, and his dedication and sacrifice for the nation.

The President said that as we are moving towards the goal of a Viksit Bharat by the year 2047, it is of utmost importance that our citizens take pride in India’s rich cultural heritage while embracing modern knowledge, science, technology, innovation, and entrepreneurship. She expressed confidence that, drawing inspiration from the life of Swami Shraddhanand Ji, the youth of our country will contribute to building an educated, self-reliant, harmonious, and empowered India.

2331230.title: Coal India Marks 51 Glorious Years with Record-Breaking Performance in October 2026
2331230.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
Coal India Marks 51 Glorious Years with Record-Breaking Performance in October 2026
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi

Coal India Limited (CIL) under the Ministry of Coal, the country’s leading coal producer, marked its 51st Foundation Day on 1st November 2026 on a remarkable note, registering a series of record-breaking achievements during October 2026. The company recorded its highest-ever monthly coal production and total coal supply, while also achieving the highest-ever monthly supply to the power sector.

During October 2026, CIL achieved a highest-ever total coal supply of 70.3 Million Tonnes (MT) in any month, surpassing the previous record of 69.4 MT achieved in March 2026. This represents a year-on-year growth of 19%.

Coal supply to the power sector also reached a new milestone, with CIL recording its highest-ever monthly supply of 57.1 MT to the power sector. The previous record stood at 56.5 MT, achieved in May 2024. The supply to the power sector registered a year-on-year growth of 19%.

The company also achieved a significant milestone in coal production, recording its highest-ever production of 67.2 MT during the month of October. This surpassed the previous record of 62.47 MT achieved in October 2024 and represents a year-on-year growth of 19%.

In another major achievement, railway coal evacuation witnessed record performance, with daily rake loading for the power sector reaching 310 rakes, the highest-ever achieved in any month. This surpassed the previous record of 302.8 rakes per day achieved in March 2025.

These remarkable achievements assume special significance as Coal India celebrates 51 glorious years of its existence and embarks on its 52nd year of service to the nation. Established on 1st November 1975, Coal India has witnessed several transformations and overcome numerous challenges over the past five decades, moving forward with unity, determination and collective resolve.

From an annual coal production of 79 MT in its first year of operations, Coal India has recorded sustained growth over the decades, increasing its production to 768 MT in FY 2025–26—representing an almost tenfold increase over the past five decades. The production target for FY 2026–27 has been fixed at 815 MT.

The record performance during October 2026 reflects Coal India’s continued focus on enhancing production, strengthening coal evacuation and ensuring adequate and reliable coal supplies to meet the country’s growing energy requirements.

As Coal India enters its 52nd year, the company remains committed to building upon its legacy of growth and transformation and contributing to India’s energy security and national development.

THE PEOPLE OF HARYANA HAVE MADE MEANINGFUL CONTRIBUTIONS IN DIVERSE FIELDS, RANGING FROM THE FREEDOM STRUGGLE TO SOCIAL CHANGE, DEMOCRACY, LITERATURE, AND SCIENCE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU

2331224.title: Shri Kiren Rijiju, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs, attends the raising of 108 Stupas in Bhutan
2331224.body_html:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
Shri Kiren Rijiju, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs, attends the raising of 108 Stupas in Bhutan
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju represented Government of India at the ceremony for raising and consecration of 108 Stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan, led by His Majesty The King of Bhutan on 01 November 2026. Shri Rijiju’s presence at the 108 Stupas event is an expression of shared spiritual and cultural ties, and the close friendship between the peoples of India and Bhutan.


        The 108 Stupas project was conceived by His Majesty The King of Bhutan who also steered its implementation. In a single day, thousands of volunteers erected 108 Stupas, each 15 metres tall and separated by 108 metres on an 11.7 kilometre stretch along the Aie (Mau) River within Gelephu Mindfulness City near the border with Assam. The project aims to showcase Gelephu Mindfulness City as a prominent center of Vajrayana Buddhism, while simultaneously representing the values and culture of the Bhutanese people.           

His Majesty The King of Bhutan, Prime Minister of Bhutan and Minister Shri Rijiju offered prayers at the Stupa No.76, dedicated by His Majesty The King of Bhutan to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for his commitment and steadfast support to the Gelephu Mindfulness City. Shri Rijiju conveyed gratitude on behalf of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to His Majesty The King of Bhutan for the gesture of dedicating a Stupa as part of the Project.

During the visit to Bhutan from 31 October – 2 November 2026, Shri Rijiju received an audience with His Majesty The King of Bhutan, Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck and met with the Prime Minister of Bhutan, Dasho Tshering Tobgay. The two sides appreciated the special friendship between the two nations and the healthy trend in bilateral cooperation in diverse areas such as development cooperation, trade, energy, investment, connectivity and cultural connections. Shri Rijiju reaffirmed India’s support for the visionary project of Gelephu Mindfulness City and its role in development of neighbouring areas in India together with Bhutan.

2331222.title: PM to Inaugurate Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 on 2nd November
2331222.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
PM to Inaugurate Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 on 2nd November
Theme of Summit - ‘Invest. Innovate. Inspire.’
Summit to Witness Participation from Over 130 Countries, 9 Country Partners and 40 Ministers
13 States and UTs to Showcase Renewable Energy Potential and Investment Opportunities
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 on 2 November at around 4:30 PM at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

The four-day Summit will be held from 2 to 5 November 2026. The theme of the Summit  is ‘Invest. Innovate. Inspire.’

Bharat RE 2026 will attract participants from over 130 countries, including more than 40 Ministers, along with policymakers, investors, financial institutions and industry leaders. It will serve as a global platform for clean energy investment, industry engagement and technology partnerships. Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom will participate as Country Partners.

Thirteen States and Union Territories - Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal - will showcase their renewable energy potential, investment opportunities and manufacturing capabilities.

The Summit will be held alongside the 9th Session of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen (ICGH). While Bharat RE will focus on investment, industry and technology partnerships across the clean energy sector, the ISA Assembly will advance international cooperation in solar energy, including finance and institutional capacity. The ICGH will focus on green hydrogen technologies, investment and scale-up. Together, these three platforms will strengthen international cooperation and accelerate clean energy deployment.

Building on the legacy of RE-INVEST, India's flagship renewable energy investment summit, Bharat RE 2026 will provide an expanded platform for global engagement across the clean energy sector. The Summit will also host plenary sessions, ministerial discussions, CEO roundtables and country and state sessions, alongside business-to-business, business-to-government and government-to-government engagements to promote investment, partnerships and project development.  The Expo will feature over 400 exhibitors showcasing advanced technologies, Indian manufacturing capabilities and clean energy solutions across solar and wind power, green hydrogen, energy storage and other emerging areas.

2331212.title: AIR CHIEF MARSHAL ASHUTOSH DIXIT ASSUMES CHARGE AS THE 29TH CHIEF OF THE AIR STAFF; UNVEILS 'VAYU' AS GUIDING VISION FOR THE INDIAN AIR FORCE
2331212.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
AIR CHIEF MARSHAL ASHUTOSH DIXIT ASSUMES CHARGE AS THE 29TH CHIEF OF THE AIR STAFF; UNVEILS 'VAYU' AS GUIDING VISION FOR THE INDIAN AIR FORCE
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit PVSM AVSM VM VSM, as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff of the Indian Air Force, on 01 November 2026, commenced his tenure by paying homage at the National War Memorial to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in service of the Nation. This was followed by a ceremonial Guard of Honour at Air Force Station New Delhi.

An Experimental Test Pilot and Qualified Flying Instructor, Air Chief Marshal Dixit has over 3,500 hours of flying experience. He has held several key operational and strategic appointments, including Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC), HQ IDS, Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Central Air Command, and Vice Chief of the Air Staff.

Chief in his opening address, outlined his vision and priorities for the Indian Air Force, the Chief of the Air Staff coined the guiding theme ‘VAYU', articulating four distinct pillars that will shape the IAF's future trajectory.

V - Vigilance, Victory and Readiness: Maintaining the highest state of operational preparedness across all formations, while restoring combat strength to sanctioned levels.

A - Aatmanirbharta: Accelerating indigenous capabilities across platforms, sensors weapons and technologies, with a focus on operational self-reliance and sustained combat capability.           

Y - Yukti: Harnessing ingenuity and innovation in doctrine, technology and operational procedures, including Al-enabled command and control, counter-     drone capabilities, resilience and emerging operational domains.

U - Unity of Effort: Strengthening jointness with the Army, Navy and national agencies, in consonance with the national vision of JAI - Jointness, Aatmanirbharta and Innovation.

Through the 'VAYU' vision, the Chief of the Air Staff has articulated a clear direction for an operationally ready, technologically advanced, self-reliant and seamlessly integrated Indian Air Force, committed to safeguarding the nation's interests and deterring conflict through credible air power.
