2330834.title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Positions IIPA’s Nationwide Outreach for Inclusive Capacity Building in Governance
2330834.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2330834.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Positions IIPA’s Nationwide Outreach for Inclusive Capacity Building in Governance
Union Minister emphasises taking IIPA’s activities beyond the national capital through stronger Regional and Local Branches
Dr. Jitendra Singh addresses IIPA’s 72nd Annual General Body Meeting in the presence of Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan
Digital learning, online courses and private-sector collaboration to widen access to capacity building: Dr. Jitendra Singh
IIPA membership reaches 11,611, with expanded participation of young professionals and recent graduates, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 3:16PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh has emphasised nationwide outreach by the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA) as a key priority for ensuring inclusive capacity building in governance.

Stressing the need to move beyond the national capital, he said that expanding IIPA’s geographical reach would help make its learning resources, academic activities and professional networks accessible to a wider community.

Addressing IIPA’s 72nd Annual General Body Meeting, Dr. Jitendra Singh, Chairman of the IIPA Executive Council, spoke in the presence of the Vice President of India and President of IIPA, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, along with senior officials, members of the Institute’s governing bodies and representatives of its academic and administrative community.

Referring to IIPA’s efforts to extend its activities beyond the national capital, the Minister said that this experience had proved motivating. He emphasised the importance of building on this momentum and strengthening the Institute’s presence across the country so that capacity-building opportunities in public administration are not confined to Delhi but reach officials and professionals in different regions.

Dr. Jitendra Singh stressed the need to further strengthen IIPA’s Regional and Local Branches and use them as important channels for wider participation, professional engagement and the dissemination of knowledge. A stronger regional presence would help the Institute connect more effectively with public administration professionals and extend its academic and capacity-building activities to a broader geographical base.

The Minister also referred to the broadening of IIPA’s membership framework, including opportunities for younger professionals and recent graduates to become part of the Institute. With its membership reaching 11,611, IIPA has an opportunity to engage a wider and more diverse community, bringing together experienced administrators, young professionals, researchers and others interested in public administration.

Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the role of digital learning and online courses in widening access to knowledge and training. He also stressed the importance of collaboration with the private sector and exploring different ways of making learning resources available to a larger audience. Such efforts can complement the Institute’s physical presence and help expand participation in capacity-building programmes.

Recalling the legacy of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and the role of the civil services in nation-building, the Minister spoke about IIPA’s institutional journey since its establishment in 1954. He emphasised the continuing relevance of strengthening public administration through learning, research and professional development as India advances towards the vision of Viksit Bharat.

IIPA’s work during 2025–26 included the completion of 45 research projects, with 13 studies ongoing. The Institute also conducted 130 training programmes and related academic activities, including 35 programmes for State Government officials serving at the state, district and local levels.

As of March 31, 2026, IIPA had 26 Regional Branches and 43 Local Branches across the country. Strengthening this network and expanding nationwide outreach remain important to extending the Institute’s reach and making capacity building more inclusive.

The Annual General Body Meeting reviewed the Institute’s activities and priorities, with discussions centred on strengthening its contribution to public administration, widening participation and enhancing the reach of its academic and capacity-building initiatives in line with the broader vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

2330835.title: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs Concludes Special Campaign 6.0 with Focus on Swachhata, Record Management and Digital Governance
2330835.body_html:
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs Concludes Special Campaign 6.0 with Focus on Swachhata, Record Management and Digital Governance
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs (MoPA) has successfully concluded its participation in Special Campaign 6.0 for institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency, conducted from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The campaign focused on improving workplace cleanliness, strengthening record management, reviewing pending matters and promoting efficient and sustainable administrative practices.

The campaign, steered by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Government of India, aims to institutionalise Swachhata in government offices and enhance administrative efficiency through systematic record management, timely disposal of pending matters and improved utilisation of office space.

During the preparatory phase, the Ministry identified targets relating to record management, cleanliness and disposal of obsolete materials. The implementation phase witnessed focused efforts towards achieving the identified targets and improving the overall efficiency of office functioning.

Key Achievements under Special Campaign 6.0

Record Management: The Ministry reviewed all identified physical files and e-files as part of the campaign. A total of 134 physical files were identified for review among which 58 were identified for weeding out and have been weeded out, while 200 e-files were reviewed and 117 e-files were closed. These measures have contributed to systematic record management and streamlined administrative processes.

Cleanliness and Workplace Improvement: The campaign reinforced the importance of maintaining clean, organised and efficient workplaces. Cleanliness and workplace management remained important focus areas, with emphasis on sustaining Swachhata as an integral part of routine office functioning.

Inspections were conducted by senior officers under the leadership of the Secretary and the Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs to assess sanitation and cleanliness standards across Sections/Offices of the Ministry

Digital and Paperless Governance: The Ministry continues to promote digital and paperless functioning through various e-governance platforms, including e-Office, e-HRMS, Consultative Committee Management System, Sub-ordinate Legislation Management System, National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA), OAMS and the National Youth Parliament Portal. These platforms facilitate streamlined administrative processes, reduce dependence on physical records and promote transparency and efficiency.

The National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA), a flagship initiative of the Ministry, continues to support paperless functioning of State Legislatures, contributing to efficient legislative processes and environmentally sustainable governance.

Special Campaign 6.0 has further reinforced the Ministry’s commitment to systematic record management, digital transformation and a clean and organised work environment. The Ministry will continue to sustain these efforts beyond the campaign period and integrate Swachhata, efficiency and sustainable practices into its day-to-day functioning.

2330823.title: Government of India extends Customs Duty Exemption on Cotton imports up to 31st December 2026
2330823.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
Government of India extends Customs Duty Exemption on Cotton imports up to 31st December 2026
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 2:38PM by PIB Delhi

Keeping in view the raw material requirements of domestic textile industry, Government of India has extended the existing customs duty exemption on cotton imports until 31st December 2026.

The extension has been notified by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, vide Notification No. 35/2026-Customs dated 30th October 2026. Through this amendment, the existing exemption, which was available until 31st October 2026, has been extended by two months, up to 31st December 2026.

The Government of India remains conscious of the need to balance the requirements of the textile industry with the interests of domestic cotton farmers, while promoting the sustainable and long-term growth of the entire cotton and textile value chain. The decision aims to augment the availability of cotton for the domestic textile sector, ensure the availability of cotton at competitive prices, support domestic manufacturing, address specialised cotton requirements and support value addition across the textile and apparel value chain.

The measure is expected to provide greater flexibility to textile and apparel manufacturers in meeting their raw material requirements, help ease input cost pressures, support Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), and strengthen the competitiveness of Indian textiles in domestic and international markets.

The extension is expected to facilitate uninterrupted availability of raw materials, improve operational flexibility for the textile industry and promote greater value addition across the cotton-based textile and apparel sector.

The Ministry of Textiles welcomes and appreciates the decision of the Ministry of Finance and remains committed to promoting a competitive, resilient and globally integrated textile sector, advancing value addition and employment generation, and fostering the long-term growth of the entire textile value chain.

2330810.body_html:

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah Flags off ‘Run for Unity’ in New Delhi on 'Rashtriya Ekta Diwas’on the occasion of 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah also administered the Unity Pledge to the countrymen on the occasion of ‘Rahstriya Ekta Diwas’
Today, Prime Minister Modi Ji will take the salute of the parade of police forces from across the country from the same place and deliver the
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 2:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah flagged off the 'Run for Unity' in New Delhi today, organized on the occasion of 'Rashtriya Ekta Diwas'—marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. On this occasion, Union Home Minister also administered the 'Unity Pledge' to the citizens of the country. Several dignitaries were present at the event, including Delhi Lieutenant Governor Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Chief Minister of Delhi Smt. Rekha Gupta, and Union Ministers of State for Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai and Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar.

In his address on this occasion, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that ever since Shri Narendra Modi became the Prime Minister of the country, we have been observing the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel as 'Rashtriya Ekta Diwas'. Today marks the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Sahab. He was a great personality who not only transformed the history of India but also shaped its very geography. By undertaking the arduous task of uniting numerous princely states and royal domains, Sardar Sahab created the map of the unified India we see today. He said that Sardar Sahab not only made successful efforts toward the geographical, political, and cultural integration of India but also brought the nation together, binding it into a single, cohesive entity.

Shri Amit Shah said that when the country attained independence, the world predicted that India would disintegrate. In just 1,218 days following independence, Sardar Patel accomplished what many deemed impossible by forging a united India. Today, the India envisioned by Sardar Patel stands proudly before the world.

Union Home Minister said that on March 31st this year, the country got rid of Naxalism and is now progressing on the path to becoming a drug-free nation. He emphasized that the creation of a drug-free India is the foundational step toward the Prime Minister Modi’s vision of a 'Viksit Bharat'. He said that significant milestones have been achieved during Prime Minister Modi’s tenure—such as the abrogation of Article 370, which permanently integrated Kashmir into India; the eradication of Naxalism; and the implementation of a unified tax system. Shri Shah said that the realization of a drug-free India would be the most significant achievement of all—one that would profoundly benefit the nation's youth and its future.

Shri Amit Shah said that the linguistic, cultural, and traditional diversity of our country is not our weakness, but strength. He said that this was the message of Sardar Patel, and it is the path we must continue to follow. Our linguistic, cultural, and religious diversity is our power. Through dialogue, trust, and an inclusive mindset, we have built a shared national identity over the past 80 years. While our languages, attire, cultural beliefs, and religions may differ, our nation has always remained united.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple served as an experience of civilizational and national resurgence. It was Sardar Patel who envisioned the construction of the Somnath Temple. Today, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the initiatives of 'Make in India' and 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' are guiding us toward attaining a top position among the world's economies.

Shri Amit Shah said that Sardar Sahab did not get the recognition he deserved for his contributions for many years. The opposition always attempted to erase the memory of Sardar Sahab, but just as the light of the sun cannot be concealed, his legacy could not be suppressed. He said that when Shri Narendra Modi was the Chief Minister of Gujarat, he commissioned the 'Statue of Unity'—a towering monument—thereby presenting the stature of Sardar Sahab’s great personality to the entire nation. Shri Shah said that today, from that very location, Prime Minister Modi will take the salute at a parade of police forces from across the country, conveying a message of national unity.

2330789.title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS GAYATRI PARIVAR’S CONTRIBUTIONS TO INDIA'S SPIRITUAL RENAISSANCE, SOCIAL TRANSFORMATION AND NATION-BUILDING
2330789.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS GAYATRI PARIVAR’S CONTRIBUTIONS TO INDIA'S SPIRITUAL RENAISSANCE, SOCIAL TRANSFORMATION AND NATION-BUILDING
LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS UPON GAYATRI PARIWAR TO CARRY FORWARD IDEALS OF DEVELOPMENT, RIGHTEOUSNESS AND NATION-BUILDING
MATA BHAGWATI DEVI JI'S LIFE OF PENANCE, COMPASSION AND SERVICE INSPIRED A TRANSFORMATIVE MOVEMENT FOR WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND SOCIAL REFORM: LOK SABHA SPEAKER.
AKHAND JYOTI CONTINUES TO ILLUMINATE LIVES THROUGH SPIRITUAL AWAKENING, VALUE-BASED EDUCATION AND CHARACTER-BUILDING: SHRI OM BIRLA.
LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES CENTENARY CELEBRATION, ORGANISED BY GAYATRI PARIVAR IN NEW DELHI
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, 31 October 2026: Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today paid rich tributes to the revered spiritual luminaries Acharya Shri Ram Sharma Ji and Mata Bhagwati Devi Ji at the Shatabdi Samaroh 2026, recalling their invaluable contributions to India's spiritual renaissance, social transformation and nation-building. He observed that the centenary celebration was not merely an occasion to commemorate the past, but a celebration of a creative movement that had transformed countless lives across the country.

Paying homage to Acharya Shri Ram Sharma Ji during his address at the centenary celebration organised by Gayatri Parivar in New Delhi, Shri Birla said that through Akhand Jyoti, he had spread the light of spirituality across the country and inspired people with the ideals of individual development, family development, social development and nation-building. His inspiring resolve, “We will change, and the era will change”, had become a guiding principle for people in India and across the world. Through the Gayatri Mantra and yajna, Acharya Ji connected people with spiritual consciousness and paved the way for inner purity and spiritual awakening.

Recalling his personal association with the Gayatri Parivar, Shri Birla said that he had witnessed the transformative influence of Acharya Ji's spiritual philosophy even in remote villages and hamlets, where it had helped people overcome difficult circumstances, superstition and harmful social practices. The movement had not only brought about a change in people's social lives but had also contributed to their personal growth, character-building and a deeper sense of responsibility towards society and the nation.

Paying his respectful homage to Mata Bhagwati Devi Ji, the Lok Sabha Speaker highlighted her extraordinary life of maternal affection, compassion, penance, dedication and service. He said that her contribution went far beyond spiritual awakening, as she spearheaded a significant movement for social transformation and women's empowerment at a time when women across the country faced numerous social challenges and restrictive practices. He observed that Mata Ji inspired women to pursue education, develop self-confidence and become self-reliant. Her life and teachings demonstrated that the development of a woman's personality within a household lays the foundation for the progress of the entire family and society. Her maternal affection and compassionate guidance transformed the lives of countless women and gave a new impetus to their social and spiritual empowerment. An environment rooted in spiritual awareness and Indian values, he said, played an important role in nurturing positive attitudes, strengthening families and building a progressive society.

Shri Birla appreciated the Gayatri Parivar's sustained efforts to take India's spiritual heritage, cultural wisdom and value-based philosophy to different parts of the world. He noted that the organisation, through its work in several countries, had been advancing the ideals of individual, family and social development in keeping with contemporary needs. He also appreciated the institution's commitment to education rooted in spirituality, culture and Indian values.

Referring to the university established by Acharya Ji, the Lok Sabha Speaker said that its emphasis on spirituality, cultural values and character-building from the early stages of education was commendable.

He expressed appreciation for the institution's initiatives in value-based education, women's awakening and empowerment, and social reform. He also lauded Dr. Chinmaya Pandya for taking India's spiritual traditions and cultural values to the world while simultaneously familiarising people with developments in science and technology. Emphasising the relevance of spirituality in the contemporary world, Shri Birla said that at a time when people in several countries were experiencing stress and depression, the message of inner peace, spiritual strength and a purposeful life had become increasingly significant. The Gayatri Parivar's spiritual centre, he observed, provided people with peace of mind, self-confidence, determination and a sense of direction in life. Shri Birla called upon the Gayatri Pariwar to continue carrying the light of Akhand Jyoti to every village and every section of society. He emphasised that this mission must continue until the life of the last person in society was touched by positive transformation. The ideals of spirituality, religion, culture, character-building and nation-building, he said, must remain central to this endeavour.

Expressing confidence in the continued contribution of the Gayatri Parivar, Shri Birla said that the spiritual energy and consciousness inspired by Acharya Shri Ram Sharma Ji and Mata Bhagwati Devi Ji would continue to illuminate lives and strengthen the foundations of a harmonious, enlightened and developed society.

2330752.title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda administers Rashtriya Ekta Diwas pledge to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
2330752.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2330752.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda administers Rashtriya Ekta Diwas pledge to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 11:36AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Shri J.P. Nadda, today administered the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) pledge to officers and officials of both the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers at a ceremony held at Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi. The observance commemorated the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, whose contributions to the integration and unity of the nation remain an enduring inspiration.

The ceremony was attended by Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Department of Health and Family Welfare; Shri Rajat Kumar Mishra, Secretary, Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers; Shri Tejveer Singh, Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers; Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research and Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR); Dr. Lovneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services (Dte.GHS) and Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal, CEO, National Health Authority (NHA) along with other senior officers and officials of both the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers.

The pledge-taking ceremony reaffirmed the collective commitment of officers and officials towards upholding the unity, integrity and security of the nation. Rashtriya Ekta Diwas is observed every year on 31st October to honour the legacy of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and reiterate the importance of national unity and solidarity.

The observance served as an occasion to renew the commitment to the ideals of unity, integrity and national cohesion, which continue to guide the country's journey towards a developed and united India.

2330737.title: Prime Minister visits CCIC Pavilion at Bharat Parv 2026 in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat
2330737.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
Prime Minister visits CCIC Pavilion at Bharat Parv 2026 in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat
CCIC Showcases India’s Rich Handloom and Handicraft Heritage, Highlighting Its Efforts to Empower Artisans and Weavers and Promote ‘Vocal for Local’ and ‘Local to Global’
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 10:48AM by PIB Delhi

Central Cottage Industries Corporation of India Ltd. (CCIC), a Government of India enterprise under the Ministry of Textiles, is participating in the ongoing Bharat Parv 2026 being held at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, Gujarat. It was a proud and memorable moment for CCIC when the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India visited the CCIC Pavilion on 30 October 2026 at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia. The visit provided an opportunity for CCIC to showcase its rich legacy, its longstanding association with artisans & weavers, and its continued efforts towards promoting India’s traditional handloom and handicraft heritage.

CCIC Pavilion presents the Corporation’s journey of empowering artisans and weavers by providing them with better market access and sustainable livelihood opportunities. Through its initiatives, CCIC is actively contributing to the vision of “Vocal for Local” and taking “Local to Global”, by connecting India’s traditional craftsmanship with wider domestic and international markets.

Shri Bimal Gopalachari, Managing Director, CCIC, along with officials of the Corporation, artisans and weavers, were present at the Pavilion. The Pavilion showcases the exceptional skills and craftsmanship of artisans from different parts of the country, including artisans from Gujarat demonstrating traditional artwork using Agate stones and semi-precious stones and intricate Appliqué work.

CCIC is celebrates the rich and diverse heritage of Indian handloom and handicrafts, bringing together exceptional artistry, creativity and craftsmanship from across the country and showcases a wide range of traditional and handcrafted products that reflect India’s vibrant cultural legacy and the timeless beauty of its indigenous art forms.

The exhibition will remain open for visitors up to 15 November 2026 at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, Gujarat

2330728.title: ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ awarded to 490 personnel of various States/UTs/CAPFs/CPOs for the year 2026
2330728.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ awarded to 490 personnel of various States/UTs/CAPFs/CPOs for the year 2026
‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ recognizes excellent work, promotes high professional standards and boosts the morale of the concerned officials/officers
Initiated under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ will boost the morale of all police personnel
‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ is announced on 31st of October every year on the occasion of Birth Anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 9:55AM by PIB Delhi

The ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ has been awarded to 490 personnel of various States/Union Territories (UTs)/Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs)/Central Police Organisations (CPOs) for the year 2026. The medal is given to recognize excellent work, promote high professional standards and boost the morale of the concerned official/officer.

Initiated under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ will boost the morale of all police personnel.

The “Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak” has been instituted vide Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India Notification dated 1st February, 2024. The Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak is conferred on members of the Police Forces, Security Organization, Intelligence Wing/Branch/Special Branch of State/Union Territories/Central Police Organizations(CPOs)/Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs)/National Security Guard/Assam Rifles; and Forensic Science (Central/State/Union Territories) throughout the Indian Union in consideration for excellence in Operations, outstanding service in Investigation, exceptional performance, indomitable & daring intelligence service, meritorious work done by Serving Government Scientists in the field of  Forensic Science.

The medal is announced on 31st of October every year, on the occasion of Birth Anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

The list of awardees is available on MHA website - https://www.mha.gov.in

2330727.title: India’s Social Security Coverage
2330727.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
India’s Social Security Coverage
Strengthening Worker Protection
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 9:46AM by PIB Delhi

India’s social security framework has expanded through wider EPFO coverage, digital reforms and welfare initiatives. EPFO provides provident fund savings, pension and insurance benefits to eligible members. The increase in the mandatory coverage wage ceiling from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 is expected to bring over 51 lakh additional employees within its ambit. Digital initiatives aim to simplify registration, withdrawals and claim settlement. Beyond EPFO, initiatives such as e-Shram, and schemes like PM-SYM and the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana extend support to unorganised workers and vulnerable groups. These measures strengthen access to social protection across employment categories and stages of life.  

 

Social Security as a Pillar of Worker Protection

As economies evolve, employment patterns and sources of livelihood continue to change. The expansion of informal, gig and platform-based work, along with variations in income and employment continuity, makes social security increasingly important for workers and their families. Social security provides protection against income loss and other contingencies across different stages of life. It also strengthens financial security during retirement and periods of vulnerability.

India has significantly expanded the reach of social protection in recent years. Social protection coverage increased from 19% in 2015 to 68.4% in 2026. This expansion has brought more than one billion people within the social protection framework.  

For Indian workers, social security provides financial security beyond their working years. The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) plays an important role by administering provident fund, pension and insurance schemes for eligible workers. It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment and one of the world’s largest social security institutions. Its schemes help workers build retirement savings, access pension benefits and secure financial support for their families.

 

Three Pillars of EPFO-led Social Security

EPFO social security architecture includes provident fund savings, pension benefits and insurance protection.

  • Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 (EPF)
    The new EPF 2026 introduced under the Social Security Code, 2020 (Code) replaced the erstwhile Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme, 2026. The EPF 2026 enables members to build retirement savings through contributions and accrued interest. It also permits partial withdrawals for specified purposes, including housing, higher education, marriage and medical treatment, subject to prescribed conditions.

 

  • Employees’ Pension Scheme, 2026 (EPS)
    The new EPS 2026 under the Code replaced the erstwhile Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995. The EPS 2026 provides monthly pension benefits to eligible members on superannuation, retirement or disability. It also provides pension benefits to eligible dependents of deceased members, including spouses, children and other eligible family members.

 

  • Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 2026 (EDLI)
    The new EDLI 2026 under the Code replaced the erstwhile Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976 and provides insurance protection to eligible EPF members in the event of death while in service. The scheme offers insurance benefits of up to ₹7 lakh, without requiring members to pay a separate insurance premium.

Expanding EPFO Coverage Across the Workforce

Over the years, EPFO has expanded its reach alongside India’s growing formal workforce. Its progress is reflected in wider membership, institutional coverage and pension support.

EPFO’s contributing membership has increased significantly over the period. Contributing members rose from 3.49 crore in 2014-15 to approximately 7.98 crore (as on 16 September, 2026). This represents an increase of approximately 4.49 crore contributing members over the period.

As of September 2026, 7.68 lakh establishments are contributing to EPFO. This provides a broad institutional base for extending social security coverage to eligible workers.

Pension support has expanded alongside membership. EPFO paid pensions to 51.04 lakh pensioners during 2014-15. Till September 2026, around 82 lakh pensioners are receiving pension benefits. This represents an increase of over 31 lakh pensioners.

The scale of social security benefits has also grown substantially. 1.30 crore claims were settled during 2014-15. In the last one-year period (as of October, 2026), EPFO settled 6.42 crore claims. This reflects the increasing scale of services delivered to EPFO members and beneficiaries.

Strengthening EPFO through Digital and Service Reforms

EPFO is strengthening social security delivery through wider coverage, simplified claim settlement and digitalisation. Reforms also focus on improving compliance, reducing administrative procedures and facilitating access to provident fund and pension services.

 

Wage Ceiling Revision

Extending Coverage: The wage ceiling for mandatory EPFO coverage was last revised in September 2014, from ₹6,500 to ₹15,000 per month. In September 2026, a further increase to ₹25,000 per month was approved. The revision is expected to extend mandatory coverage to over 51 lakh additional employees. It reflects changes in wage levels and the expansion of formal employment over the intervening period. The revised ceiling broadens the pool of employees eligible for mandatory coverage, subject to applicable statutory provisions.  

Streamlining PF Withdrawals and Accelerating Claim Settlement

Simplified Partial Withdrawal Rules: EPFO has consolidated 13 provisions governing partial withdrawals into three categories: Essential Needs, Housing Needs and Special Circumstances. Essential Needs cover expenses related to illness, education and marriage. This categorisation simplifies the withdrawal framework, facilitating easier access to provident fund savings for eligible members.

Liberalised Withdrawal Limits: Employees can make partial withdrawals from their PF savings to meet specific financial needs during their working years. This allows them to access savings without withdrawing the entire accumulated balance.

EPFO has simplified these provisions by allowing up to 10 withdrawals for education and 5 for marriage. Earlier, both purposes shared a combined limit of 3 partial withdrawals. The revised framework, introduced in October 2025also permits eligible members to withdraw up to 75% of their PF balance. This includes employee and employer contributions, subject to applicable conditions. The minimum service requirement has been standardised at 12 months.

Automated Claim Settlement: EPFO increased the auto-settlement limit for eligible advance claims to ₹5 lakh. This enables faster processing of eligible withdrawals without manual intervention.

Simplified Bank Verification: EPFO removed the requirement to upload cheque-leaf images or attested bank passbooks for eligible online claims. This reduces the paperwork and simplifies the claim process.

Strengthening Compliance and Ease of Doing Business

VISHWAS, 2026: The scheme facilitates one-time settlement of eligible disputes involving damages or penalties under the EPF & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, and the Code on Social Security, 2020. It reduces litigation and encourages voluntary compliance through a digital, time-bound process. The scheme covers cases involving challenged damage or penalty orders, pending or partial recovery, issued notices awaiting final orders, and cases where notices are yet to be issued.

  • Eligible pre-14 June 2024 defaults attract reduced monthly damage rates of 0.25%, 0.50% or 1%, depending on the delay period.
  • Employers must pay applicable statutory interest and undertake not to pursue further appeals on settled disputes.
  • The scheme covers cases at different stages, subject to exclusions for fraud, misappropriation, deliberate falsification and fully recovered damages. Applications are submitted online through the EPFO Employer Portal.

AMNESTY, 2026: It is a one-time scheme launched by the EPFO to help establishments regularise their provident fund PF trusts. It covers trusts recognised under the Income Tax Act, 1961, but lacking formal exemption under the EPF & MP Act, 1952, or the Code on Social Security, 2020. The scheme is open until 28 December 2026.

  • Eligible establishments can obtain exemption retrospectively, from the trust’s establishment up to the prescribed cut-off date. The scheme also waives specified minimum employee strength and fund requirements.
  • Eligible trusts must have deposited statutory contributions and credited interest to members’ accounts at rates equal to or higher than the applicable EPF rate. Subject to these conditions, proceedings initiated solely because the formal exemption was missing will be withdrawn, and no new proceedings will be initiated on this ground.

Simplifying Registration with Digital Access  

Automatic Registration: Since February 2020, eligible public and private limited companies and One Person Companies can avail the facility of automatic EPFO registration through the Ministry of Corporate Affairs portal. This facility operates through the SPICe+ and AGILE-PRO forms.  This form combines various services like PAN/TAN/Director Identification Number/GSTN, etc.

Self-Generation of Universal Account Numbers (UAN): Since November 2019, workers have been able to generate their UAN independently. This facility supports enrolment in EPFO’s social-security schemes. In April 2025, EPFO introduced UAN generation and activation through Aadhaar-based Face Authentication Technology. Available through the UMANG mobile application, this facility enables contactless and secure digital access.  As of October 2026, 1.74 crore self-generated UAN have been reported. In addition to this, EPFO transactions on the Umang Application since January 2017 till 21 October are ~709 crore, reflecting the scale of digital access to EPFO services.

The UAN is a unique, permanent number assigned to an EPFO member, linking their provident fund accounts across different establishments. It facilitates the portability of provident fund accumulations when members change jobs, subject to verification of their details in the UAN database by the employer.

 

Simplified Aadhaar Seeding: Since August 2025, EPFO members have been able to seed or correct Aadhaar details through the UAN Member Portal. Employers can approve requests directly when Aadhaar and UAN profile details match. Mismatched details can be referred online to the EPFO office for rectification. If the employer is unavailable, members can seek assistance through the concerned EPFO office’s Public Relations Officer.

Digital Transformation of EPFO Services

Centralised Pension Payment System (CPPS): CPPS enables pension disbursement through any bank branch across India. Pensioners can receive their pensions without transferring Pension Payment Orders (PPOs) between offices when changing locations or bank branches. This benefits specially the pensioners who move to their hometown after retirement. In addition, the system also supports pensioners by reducing the need to visit the branch for any verification at the time of commencement of pension.

Doorstep Digital Life Certificate Services: EPFO has partnered with India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) to provide doorstep Digital Life Certificate services to EPS pensioners. EPFO bears the cost of ₹50 per certificate, making the service free for pensioners. The initiative particularly benefits elderly pensioners in rural and remote areas. It supports timely pension continuity, faster initiation of family pensions and improved accuracy under CPPS.

Redesigned EPFO Website: On 1 November 2025, EPFO launched its redesigned website at epfo.gov.in. The mobile-responsive portal provides a unified interface for employees, employers and pensioners. It offers easier access to passbooks, claim forms, pension services, profile updates and scheme information. Separate login options and the “EPFO and You” section help users locate services quickly. YouTube videos explain services such as checking PF balances, applying for advances, submitting pension applications, filing Electronic Challan-cum-Returns (ECR), registering establishments and activating UANs. The shorter domain and improved navigation simplify access across devices.

EPFO 3.0 - Core Banking-Based Transformation: EPFO 3.0 modernises services through industry-standard core banking capabilities.

  • It integrates a core banking solution with cloud-native, API-first and microservices-based modules for account management, enterprise resource planning, compliance and customer services. Its phased implementation is designed to ensure secure, scalable and uninterrupted services.
  • The initiative reduces paperwork, accelerates claims and provides a unified platform for member services.
  • Risk-validated claims are designed for automatic processing without manual intervention, potentially reducing settlement time from up to 20 days to under 3 days.
  • Planned capabilities include instant withdrawals, multilingual self-service and seamless payroll-linked contributions. The framework is intended to support EPFO’s services for over 30 crore members.  

Beyond EPFO: India's Wider Social-Security Framework

India’s social security framework extends beyond EPFO through multiple schemes and institutional mechanisms supporting vulnerable groups and workers across employment categories. These initiatives combine social assistance, pension support, statutory protections and digital platforms to widen access to social security.

Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana     

The Yojana provides social assistance to eligible elderly persons, widows, persons with disabilities and bereaved families. It has been revised from the existing National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) in October, 2026. The scheme will continue from 2026–27 to 2030–31. The following are the benefits offered by the sub-schemes under NSAP:

  • The disability pension scheme provides monthly assistance of ₹375 to beneficiaries aged below 80 years and ₹625 to those aged 80 years and above. The benchmark disability threshold has been reduced from 80% to 40%, and the minimum age criterion has been removed, extending eligibility from birth. 
  • The old age pension scheme grants a monthly pension of ₹200 to persons aged 60-79 years and ₹500 to those aged 80 years and above.
  • The widow pension scheme offers a monthly pension of ₹300 to widows aged 40-79 years and ₹500 to those aged 80 years and above.
  • The family benefit scheme provides one-time financial assistance of ₹20,000 to eligible households upon the death of the primary breadwinner aged 18-59 years.

Code on Social Security, 2020

It consolidates nine existing central labour laws relating to social security into a unified legislative framework. The code provides for social security benefits covering provident fund, pension, insurance, maternity benefits, gratuity and other forms of worker protection. Its provisions extend to organised and unorganised workers, including gig and platform workers.

The Code provides for gratuity to eligible fixed-term employees on a proportionate basis after one year of service, subject to applicable conditions. It also recognises gig and platform workers within the social security framework and provides for schemes for their welfare, supported by a social security fund.

Women-centric provisions include maternity benefits of up to 26 weeks for eligible women, the option of work from home where the nature of work permits and crèche facilities in establishments meeting prescribed conditions. The Code also provides for digital and simplified compliance mechanisms to facilitate implementation and access to social security benefits.

e-Shram: An Integrated Platform for Unorganised Workers

Launched in August 2021, e-Shram created India’s first Aadhaar-seeded National Database of Unorganised Workers. Each registered worker receives a UAN. The portal recorded 31.89 crore registrations as of August 2026. The e-Shram One-Stop Solution, launched in October 2024, integrates 15 social security and welfare schemes. It also connects workers with the National Career Service for jobs, Skill India Digital Hub for skilling and apprenticeship, and myScheme for identifying eligible government schemes.

Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM)

PM-SYM is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for eligible unorganised workers aged 18–40 years, with monthly incomes of up to ₹15,000. It provides a minimum assured pension of ₹3,000 per month after attaining 60 years of age, subject to prescribed conditions. Monthly contributions range from ₹55 to ₹200, depending on the age of enrolment, with an equal contribution from the Central Government. The scheme supports old-age income security for workers in the unorganised sector, which contributes around 50% of India's GDP.

Towards Universal Social Security

India’s social security framework continues to expand through wider EPFO coverage, digital service delivery and reforms in labour welfare. Initiatives across provident fund, pensions, insurance and social assistance support workers across formal and informal employment. Simplified compliance and technology-enabled platforms are further strengthening access to benefits. Together, these measures contribute to a more inclusive and accessible social security system.

2330702.title: Government Ensures Continuity of Telecom Connectivity amid Cyclone Arnab
2330702.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Government Ensures Continuity of Telecom Connectivity amid Cyclone Arnab
Telecom restoration efforts underway in affected districts through coordinated action by telecom service providers
Intra-Circle Roaming operational across affected districts of Andhra Pradesh; 11 Cell on Wheels deployed to support connectivity
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 10:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), in coordination with Telecom Service Providers (TSPs), is undertaking restoration efforts and monitoring the telecom network situation to ensure the continuity of essential communication services in the affected areas, after Cyclone Arnab hit along the coast of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. Widespread heavy rainfall, flash floods, tree falls and power infrastructure disruptions affected telecom services across parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and adjoining regions.

Significant progress has been achieved in restoring network connectivity across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, with particular focus on resolving power supply disruptions and restoring optical fibre connectivity. Emergency connectivity arrangements, including ICR and COW deployments, are being maintained to facilitate uninterrupted communication for citizens and support relief and restoration activities in the affected regions.

In Andhra Pradesh, overall telecom network availability has reached 99.18 percent. Among the affected districts, network availability stands at 98.5 per cent in West Godavari, 91.96 per cent in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema. Commercial power supply disruptions and localised Optical Fibre Cable (OFC) cuts are the primary factors affecting network operations. Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) remains operational across affected districts to facilitate connectivity for subscribers, irrespective of their service provider. Additionally, 11 Cell on Wheels (COWs) have been deployed to strengthen emergency communication services.

In Odisha, following Cyclone ARNAB, the telecom network situation in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts has been gradually improving with the easing of rainfall and receding of floodwaters. Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) have initiated restoration work at affected sites, resulting in progressive improvement in network connectivity and a reduction in service disruptions. All TSPs are making sustained efforts on a priority basis to restore the remaining affected sites and ensure early normalisation of telecom services and uninterrupted connectivity for the public.

What is ICR & how to use it:

Intra Circle Roaming (ICR) is a telecom arrangement where a mobile subscriber connects to another operator’s (TSP’s) network within the same telecom circle (region). This allows users to access mobile services even if their own operator (TSP) has no coverage in that specific area. It plays a critical role during natural disasters when mobile infrastructure is damaged.

During the time of disaster, if mobile infrastructure is damaged in a region, DoT issues instructions to Telecom Service Providers to implement ICR.

To ensure ICR works:

  • Keep "Automatic Network Selection" enabled in your phone settings.
  • If automatic connection fails;
  • Go to Settings > Mobile Networks > Network Operators
  • Manually select another available network

2330687.title: BOOKS ARE POWERFUL INSTRUMENTS OF TRANSFORMING LIVES AND BRINGING POSITIVE CHANGE IN SOCIETY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
2330687.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
BOOKS ARE POWERFUL INSTRUMENTS OF TRANSFORMING LIVES AND BRINGING POSITIVE CHANGE IN SOCIETY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
TECHNOLOGY CAN PROVIDE INFORMATION, BUT TRUE KNOWLEDGE COMES FROM BOOKS AND LIFE EXPERIENCES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
INDIA'S DEMOCRACY IS ITS GREATEST STRENGTH, UNITING THE NATION AMID EXTRAORDINARY DIVERSITY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LANGUAGES DO NOT DIVIDE US; THEY CONNECT PEOPLE AND STRENGTHEN OUR CULTURAL BONDS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESS INAUGURAL CEREMONY OF THE 29TH KOCHI INTERNATIONAL BOOK FESTIVAL IN KERALAM
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 9:37PM by PIB Delhi

 Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasised that books are not merely sources of information but powerful instruments of transforming lives, broadening perspectives and inspiring positive change in society. He observed that while technology has made information readily accessible, true knowledge and wisdom come from books and life experiences. Stressing that there is no substitute for books, he said that reading not only enriches individuals but also cultivates curiosity, sensitivity and the ability to understand life from different perspectives.

Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the 29th Kochi International Book Festival in Kochi, Shri Birla emphasised the importance of cultivating reading habits and inspiring others to read. He observed that books preserve generations of wisdom and experience, inspire and guide individuals and foster discipline, determination and a sense of purpose.

Drawing a distinction between information and knowledge, Shri Birla observed that digital technology has enhanced access to information, but books and human experiences remain vital for deeper understanding and sensitivity. Emphasising lifelong learning, he highlighted curiosity as essential to acquiring knowledge and noted that books inspire hope, resilience and the pursuit of constructive goals.

Highlighting India's extraordinary diversity, Shri Birla said that the country's varied languages, religions, traditions, perspectives and ways of life constitute its unique strength. He observed that despite these differences, India remains united, and democracy is the greatest force binding the nation together. Shri Birla emphasised that democracy teaches people to respect differing opinions and ideologies and to live together in harmony. He further stressed that while opinions may differ, all citizens must stand united when it comes to the interests of the nation.

Speaking on the role of language and literature in promoting national unity, Shri Birla observed that languages connect rather than divide people. He highlighted the contribution of India's rich linguistic traditions, including Malayalam, Kannada and Telugu, in preserving and promoting the country's cultural, spiritual and intellectual heritage. He noted that writers have taken India's history, values and democratic ideals to the world, while digital translation has further expanded literature's reach across linguistic boundaries.

Appreciating Keralam's contributions to education, literature, science and technology, Shri Birla highlighted its distinction as India's first fully literate State. He observed that education has enabled Keralites to excel in India and abroad, while praising the State's traditions of service and sacrifice, particularly the contribution of its women to nursing and healthcare worldwide. Recalling Shri P. N. Panicker's pioneering contribution to Keralam's library movement, he observed that libraries and reading habits had transformed literacy and socio-economic development. He highlighted the Kerala Granthasala movement's role in spreading knowledge and appreciated Keralam's sustained efforts to promote reading through 'Vayana Dinam' or Reading Day, observed on 19 June.

Shri Birla commended the organisers of the Kochi International Book Festival for bringing together literary stakeholders and promoting literature. He observed that such festivals encourage intellectual exchange, nurture reading habits and provide access to diverse ideas. He called for greater efforts to take Kerala's rich literary, spiritual and cultural heritage to India and the world through books and translations. He congratulated the organisers and expressed hope that the Kochi International Book Festival would continue to expand its reach, inspire new generations of readers and contribute to building a more knowledgeable, sensitive and enlightened society.

Former ISRO Chairman Dr. S. Somanath, Chairman of the International Book Festival Shri Madhu S. Nair, Shri Prakash Babu, Sahitya Akademi Secretary Dr. Varun Gulati, several distinguished guests, literary figures and book enthusiasts were present on the occasion.

केरलम की समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक एवं बौद्धिक परंपरा की साक्षी नगरी कोच्चि में 29वें कोच्चि अंतर्राष्ट्रीय पुस्तक महोत्सव के उद्घाटन समारोह में सम्मिलित होकर उपस्थित जनसमुदाय को संबोधित किया। पुस्तकें किसी सभ्यता की स्मृति, समाज की चेतना और मानवता के अनुभवों की अमूल्य धरोहर हैं। वे ज्ञान के प्रकाश से व्यक्ति का परिष्कार करती हैं और राष्ट्र की वैचारिक नींव को सुदृढ़ बनाती हैं। विगत 28 वर्षों से यह महोत्सव साहित्य, विचारों के मुक्त आदान-प्रदान तथा भारतीय भाषाओं और नवोदित लेखकों को प्रोत्साहन देने का महत्वपूर्ण मंच बना हुआ है। साहित्य लोकतंत्र की आत्मा को संवेदना, विवेक और स्वतंत्र चिंतन से समृद्ध करता है। Artificial Intelligence एवं Digital Technology के इस युग में हमें प्रौद्योगिकी को साहित्य का सहयोगी बनाकर ज्ञान और अपनी भाषायी विरासत को नई पीढ़ियों तक पहुँचाना होगा। युवाओं से आग्रह है कि त्वरित सूचनाओं के दौर में पुस्तकों के गहन अध्ययन की परंपरा को जीवंत रखें, क्योंकि पुस्तकें ही विचारों को गहराई और जीवन को व्यापक दृष्टि प्रदान करती हैं। विश्वास है कि ऐसे आयोजन ‘वसुधैव कुटुंबकम्’ की भावना को साकार करते हुए विकसित भारत की बौद्धिक एवं सांस्कृतिक चेतना को नई ऊँचाइयाँ प्रदान करेंगे।

2330634.title: Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Chairs Chintan Shivir on Digitisation of Trade
2330634.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Chairs Chintan Shivir on Digitisation of Trade
Discussions Focus on Empowering Kirana Retailers through Digital Procurement and Supply-Chain Efficiency
DigiDukaan Connects Over 21,000 Retailers with More Than 450 Brands Across Three Cities
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 8:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal chaired the Bharat Commerce Chintan Shivir, a high-level CEO Roundtable convened by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The roundtable brought together over 40 leaders from leading Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) companies to deliberate on a shared roadmap for strengthening and digitising India's General Trade ecosystem through ONDC DigiDukaan.

Speaking at the roundtable, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal said, “ONDC’s DigiDukaan shows that when open digital infrastructure is built around the needs of the small retailer, adoption follows. Let this become another case study where the world can learn from India. By making procurement simpler and more transparent while strengthening our distributors, we can help kiranas free up working capital and grow. I invite the FMCG industry to work together and take this to every corner of Bharat.”

Shri Amardeep Singh Bhatia, Secretary, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) said, “Open digital infrastructure has a critical role to play in accelerating the digitalisation of India’s retail ecosystem, particularly its vast network of kirana stores. ONDC’s DigiDukaan is an important step in this direction, demonstrating how an open, interoperable network can enable neighbourhood retailers to access digital procurement opportunities and participate more effectively in the evolving digital economy. By bringing together retailers, FMCG companies and distributors on a common network, DPIIT along with ONDC is helping build a more connected and efficient General Trade ecosystem, creating a pathway for digitalisation to reach kiranas at scale.”

The discussions focused on strengthening and re-empowering the General Trade ecosystem, which remains central to India's retail economy and supports the livelihoods of millions of neighbourhood retailers. Participants emphasised the need for greater institutional commitment from FMCG companies, distributors and industry stakeholders to accelerate digital procurement, improve supply-chain efficiency and enhance the competitiveness of kirana stores. The initiative seeks to bring industry stakeholders together through common digital infrastructure, shared services and commercially sustainable models.

Senior representatives from Hindustan Unilever (HUL), Coca-Cola India, ITC, P&G, Marico, CavinKare, Pidilite, Britannia, Adani Wilmar, LT Foods, Anmol Industries, Haldiram's, Emami, Veeba and Nilon's participated in the roundtable, along with representatives from logistics providers, technology partners and ONDC network participants.

ONDC DigiDukaan addresses procurement by digitising kiranas as buyers. Through a single digital interface, retailers can discover and order products across multiple brands, distributors and wholesalers, with greater visibility into pricing, trade schemes and product availability. The initiative is designed to strengthen existing distribution relationships rather than replace them, while creating a common digital foundation through which retailers can eventually access shared logistics, formal credit and other services. This approach seeks to reduce the complexity and cost of participation across the General Trade value chain.

The roundtable deliberated on five key areas for strengthening the General Trade ecosystem. These included developing a common digital identity for kirana retailers to enable seamless engagement with multiple brands, distributors and service providers; creating shared logistics and micro-warehousing infrastructure to improve distributor reach and facilitate reliable next-day replenishment, including in areas beyond existing delivery routes; and expanding access to formal credit through financing solutions linked to digital procurement and transaction activity to improve access to working capital and reduce dependence on informal distributor credit.

Discussions also focused on simplifying technology integration through plug-and-play Distributor Management System (DMS) connectors, standardised catalogues and common digital interfaces to reduce onboarding complexity and encourage wider industry participation. Participants further deliberated on realigning commercial incentives for FMCG companies, sales teams, distributors and channel partners to make digital ordering, wider retail coverage and sustained retailer adoption commercially beneficial across the value chain.

DigiDukaan has connected over 21,000 retailers with more than 450 brands across Hyderabad, Jaipur and Mumbai as of September 2026, compared with over 12,000 retailers in the previous quarter. In Hyderabad, more than 16,000 retailers have been onboarded, with monthly repeat ordering rates of 73–78%. An initial ONDC retailer study also found that 40% of surveyed retailers reported lower inventory holdings for products procured through DigiDukaan, indicating the potential for improved working capital efficiency.

The National Traders' Welfare Board (NTWB), under the chairmanship of Shri Sunil J. Singhi, has been working closely with ONDC to accelerate the adoption of DigiDukaan among kirana retailers. The collaboration focuses on mobilising local trade associations, strengthening retailer participation and enabling small businesses to benefit from digital procurement and more efficient distribution networks.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, ONDC, Shri Vibhor Jain, said, “Digital adoption for the distributor fraternity has been developing - billing, printing, order placement are largely online. But retailers, most of which are mom-and-pop shops, still run on pen, paper and memory. DigiDukaan is ONDC's effort to build digital infrastructure for India's General Trade ecosystem in retail. We are digitising kiranas as buyers, while strengthening the existing distributor network rather than replacing it.”

DigiDukaan is building an expanding network of FMCG brands, technology providers and logistics partners. Leading FMCG companies, including HUL, Marico, Colgate-Palmolive, Emami and Amul, are participating through their distribution networks, while ITC, Tata Consumer Products and Britannia are at various stages of integration or discussion. On the technology front, Paytm for Business, Qwipo and Mulltiply.ai are live on the network, while DMS and technology providers, including Bizom, Botree, QuIDPe and ENS, are progressing towards integration. Logistics and warehousing partners, including ElasticRun, Shiprocket, India Post and Moeving, are also part of the expanding ecosystem, supporting seamless procurement, wider distributor reach and faster replenishment for kirana retailers.

As part of its next phase, ONDC is focusing on deepening brand and distributor participation in Mumbai, particularly North Mumbai, while strengthening operations across existing markets.

The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is building open digital commerce infrastructure in India through a network model aimed at reducing entry barriers and improving access for businesses. The network has enabled over 500 million transactions to date, with retail as its core focus area. It seeks to create digital networks that improve efficiency, lower costs and unlock opportunities for businesses, gig workers, small retailers and consumers.

ONDC-enabled retail initiatives include DigiDukaan, which has onboarded over 21,000 retailers for business-to-business (B2B) procurement digitisation, and Amazing India, which focuses on enabling products from kisans, karigars, cooperatives and other micro-producers to become e-commerce-ready and reach wider markets.

Other initiatives include public transport services, facilitating over 5 lakh metro and bus journeys daily through more than 40 consumer applications; logistics infrastructure used by over 80,000 merchants and 30+ small and micro fleet operators; and more than 1,000 tourism experiences, including 170 Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) monuments and 29 museums, available on the network. ONDC has also enabled low-ticket investment and credit solutions aimed at expanding financial access, with a majority of investors coming from Tier-2 cities and beyond.

***

2330630.title: 14th International Tourism Mart Concludes Its Official Sessions with Regional Tourism Ministers’ Meeting
2330630.body_html:
Ministry of Tourism
14th International Tourism Mart Concludes Its Official Sessions with Regional Tourism Ministers’ Meeting
Regional Tourism Ministers deliberate on tourism development, digital initiatives, live events economy and tourist facilitation in the North East
43 international buyers from 22 countries, 42 domestic buyers and 81 sellers participate in the Mart
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 8:02PM by PIB Delhi

The 14th International Tourism Mart (ITM), organised by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in association with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and other North Eastern States, successfully concluded its main sessions today in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. The Mart is being organised from 29 to 31 October 2026, which brought together domestic and international tourism stakeholders to showcase the tourism potential of the North Eastern Region, strengthen business partnerships and promote sustainable and experience-based tourism.

The Mart witnessed participation of 43 international buyers from 22 countries, 42 domestic buyers from 16 States and Union Territories and 81 sellers, along with media representatives, influencers and tourism stakeholders. The participating countries included Australia, Belarus, Bhutan, Egypt, France, Germany, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Malaysia, the Philippines, Poland, Russia, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The Mart’s deliberations concluded with the Regional Meeting of Tourism Ministers of the North Eastern States, held on 30 October 2026 under the chairmanship of Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. The meeting brought together Tourism Ministers and senior officials from the North Eastern States to discuss tourism development priorities, regional cooperation, emerging tourism opportunities and measures to improve tourist facilitation across the region.

During the meeting, thematic presentations were made to the Tourism Ministers on Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 and the National Digital Tourism Stack (NDTS). The presentation on Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 focused on the Mission for Redistribution of Tourism Demand and Promotion of Lesser-Known Destinations, aimed at promoting tourism-ready destinations as alternatives to popular tourist centres. The presentation on NDTS highlighted the development of a common digital tourism ecosystem to improve the discoverability of tourism experiences, enable online bookings and enhance market access for local tourism service providers, including guides, homestays and tourism entrepreneurs.

Presentations were also made on the Live Concert Economy and Restricted Area Permit (RAP)/Protected Area Permit (PAP) requirements in the North Eastern Region. The discussions on the live events economy highlighted the potential of music concerts, cultural festivals and other events to attract tourists, encourage longer stays and generate opportunities for local businesses. The presentation on RAP/PAP requirements focused on improving tourist facilitation through simplified application procedures, greater clarity on permit requirements and timely processing, while taking into account security considerations. Tourism Ministers from the eight North Eastern States also shared their views and suggestions on tourism development priorities and regional cooperation.

A major component of the International Tourism Mart was the structured business-to-business (B2B) meetings, which provided a platform for direct engagement between domestic and international buyers and tourism sellers. A total number of 1580 B2B meetings were held, facilitating opportunities for developing new tourism itineraries, establishing commercial partnerships and promoting tourism products and experiences across the North Eastern States.

Earlier, during the technical sessions, Shri Suman Billa, Additional Secretary and Director General, Ministry of Tourism, delivered the keynote address highlighting India’s significant growth in domestic tourism, with Domestic Tourist Visits increasing from 1.32 billion in 2014 to 4.34 billion in 2025, registering a CAGR of approximately 11%. He noted that the tourism sector supports 89 million jobs and contributes 5.22% to the national GDP. Highlighting improvements in connectivity, he stated that the number of airports in the North Eastern

Region has increased from 9 in 2014 to 17, while the national highway network has expanded from 10,905 km to 16,207 km. He also underscored the region’s investment potential and opportunities for community-led tourism growth, particularly through homestays, adventure, eco, wellness and experiential tourism.

The technical sessions also featured presentations by all eight North Eastern States—Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura—showcasing their tourism attractions, emerging destinations and tourism circuits.

The Mart was inaugurated on 29 October 2026 in the presence of Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Tourism and Culture; Shri Suresh Gopi, Union Minister of State for Tourism and Petroleum & Natural Gas; Shri Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh; Shri Prem Singh Tamang, Chief Minister of Sikkim; and other dignitaries. Addressing the inaugural session, Shri Shekhawat emphasised the importance of translating the region’s tourism potential into sustainable business opportunities and livelihoods for local communities.

The Mart also showcased the rich cultural and natural heritage of the North Eastern Region through the North East Bazaar, featuring traditional handicrafts, handlooms, textiles and regional products, along with cultural programmes highlighting the traditions of the region. Curated visits for delegates and media representatives included Tawang Monastery, Tawang War Memorial and Urgelling Gompa.

On the last day, technical visits to Buddha Park, PTSO Lake and Shernup Village are scheduled for 31 October 2026. Post-Mart familiarisation (FAM) tours for international delegates will commence from Guwahati on 1 November 2026, providing opportunities to experience tourism destinations and products across the North Eastern Region.

The 14th edition marked the return of the International Tourism Mart to Tawang after 13 years, following the second edition held here in 2013. The Mart reaffirmed the commitment to strengthening tourism partnerships, promoting lesser-known destinations and positioning the North Eastern Region as a leading destination for sustainable and experience-based tourism.

2330620.title: INS TARKASH CALLS AT PORT LOUIS, MAURITIUS
2330620.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INS TARKASH CALLS AT PORT LOUIS, MAURITIUS
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship Tarkash arrived at Port Louis, Mauritius, on 30 Oct 2026, as part of her ongoing operational deployment to the Southern Indian Ocean Region. The port call reflects the close maritime partnership between India and Mauritius and provides an opportunity to further strengthen bilateral naval cooperation through professional interactions, joint activities and cultural exchanges.

During the port call, the ship’s crew will undertake a series of engagements with personnel of the Mauritius Coast Guard, including joint training activities aimed at sharing operational experiences and Best Practices, enhancing interoperability and strengthening coordination between the two maritime forces. Cultural exchanges and community outreach activities will also form part of the visit, providing opportunities for interaction between the personnel of the two countries and fostering closer people-to-people ties.

INS Tarkash will also participate in events commemorating the 192nd Aapravasi Diwas of Mauritius on 02 Nov 2026. The annual observance commemorates the arrival of the first batch of indentured labourers from India at Aapravasi Ghat, Port Louis, on 02 Nov 1834. The day honours the historical legacy, sacrifices and contributions of these labourers, whose descendants now constitute a significant part of the Mauritian population and have contributed to the island nation's cultural and economic development. The participation of INS Tarkash in the commemorative events underscores the deep-rooted historical and cultural connections between the two countries.

The port call is an important manifestation of India's enduring partnership with Mauritius, underpinned by shared historical links, cultural affinity and mutual trust. It also highlights the Indian Navy's continued engagement with friendly maritime nations in the Indian Ocean Region, contributing to maritime cooperation, regional security and stability. Through such deployments and engagements, the Indian Navy continues to strengthen maritime partnerships and advance the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

2330618.title: 46 ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ Programmes Held Across 21 States/UTs to Promote Electoral Awareness Among Youth
2330618.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2330618.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
46 ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ Programmes Held Across 21 States/UTs to Promote Electoral Awareness Among Youth
6,688 youth participate in programmes across the country on Oct 30; nationwide campaign aims to cover 500 universities, colleges & institutions by Nov 5
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 7:51PM by PIB Delhi

A total of 6,688 youth participated in 46 editions of ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ organised across 21 States and Union Territories today by Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), under the Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. The nationwide campaign, being conducted from 26 October to 5 November 2026, aims to reach 500 universities, colleges and institutions across the country.

The initiative seeks to promote electoral awareness among young people, particularly first-time voters, and encourage their informed participation in the democratic process. It aims to familiarise them with voting rights, electoral procedures and civic responsibilities, while providing a platform to interact with elected representatives, Youth Icons and other distinguished personalities on democratic participation and their role in nation-building.

 

 

The programmes conducted today covered a wide geographical spread, extending from Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh in the north to Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Nagaland and Sikkim in the North-East, and reaching States across eastern, central, western and southern India, including Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. As of 30.10.2026, a total of 96 Yuva Samvads have been conducted across 27 States and Union Territories, engaging 18,475 youth and 97 Youth Icons.

In Punjab, Yuva Samvads across Faridkot, Fatehgarh Sahib, Gurdaspur and Moga today featured interactions with Youth Icons Master Saiyam Mazumder, International Rugby Player Ms. Amandeep Kaur, Shri Divjot Singh and Shri Shashikesh Kumar. The discussions highlighted informed democratic participation, responsible citizenship and the role of youth in strengthening democratic institutions.

In Jammu and Kashmir, Yuva Samvads in Doda and Poonch featured interactive discussions on electoral awareness, civic responsibility and youth participation in governance. Lacrosse athlete Ms. Abhilove Kour interacted with students in Poonch, while participants in Doda actively raised questions and shared their perspectives on the importance of first-time voters and responsible citizenship.

In Madhya Pradesh, programmes in Chhatarpur and Gwalior featured interactions with elected representatives on youth leadership and the vision of Viksit Bharat. Gwalior also witnessed a presentation by Youth Icon Shri Vikram Baghel, inspiring sports stories and the Loktantrik Shapath. In Khandwa (East Nimar), young participants actively engaged with elected representatives during the interaction.

In Champa, Chhattisgarh, Member of Parliament from Janjgir-Champa Smt Kamlesh Jangde interacted with young participants and encouraged their involvement in democratic processes and nation-building. The programme also featured a yoga and meditation session under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, focusing on stress management, mental well-being and healthy lifestyles.

Yuva Samvaads in other States also featured activities promoting civic awareness, youth participation and nation-building. In Chamoli, Uttarakhand, 200 youth participated in a Youth Dialogue Programme in Gopeshwar. In Vaishali, Bihar, participants took the Loktantrik Shapath, reaffirming their commitment to responsible citizenship. In Rajasthan, programmes in Bundi and Dausa focused on voter awareness and promoting a drug-free lifestyle, with a street play on the importance of voting organised in Dausa. In Uttar Pradesh, Lakhimpur Kheri hosted a Nasha Mukt awareness session and a lecture on Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD), while activities in Shrawasti included youth mobilisation for a drug-free India and a Neighbourhood Youth Parliament.

In Madurai, Tamil Nadu, the Yuva Samvad featured a Parliament-style discussion on the Women’s Reservation Bill, providing young participants an opportunity to deliberate on women's representation and inclusive governance.

With 96 programmes conducted across 27 States and Union Territories so far, the campaign continues to engage young people through discussions, interactions with public representatives and Youth Icons, and activities promoting democratic awareness, responsible citizenship and youth leadership.
