The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Adoni - Mantralayam and Hyderabad nearby areas , during the month of September 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 1. Hyderabad 63 Kms, Hotspot locations –2 and walk test 21.5Km, during 15th-16th September 2026 in AP LSA. 2.Kurnool District Adoni-Mantralayam and nearby areas 201.8Kms, Hotspot locations – 6, during 17th-18th September 2026 in AP LSA.   2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instance occurred during the calls.

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 1323/37685 for Airtel, 8339/35351 for BSNL, 633/36991 for RJIL and 4155/37273 for VIL. The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having Limited service out of the total samples collected, was 0/37685 for Airtel, 140/35351 for BSNL, 0/36991 for RJIL and 6/37273 for VIL. 2330383.title: Vice-President calls for holistic rural development to realise Viksit Bharat 2047; graces Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute
2330383.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President calls for holistic rural development to realise Viksit Bharat 2047; graces Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute
“India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 must begin with empowered villages”: Vice-President
Gandhian ideals of self-reliance and social service remain vital for building a developed India: Vice-President
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 3:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today graced the Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute (Deemed to be University) in Dindigul, Tamil Nadu. He conferred gold medals on meritorious students and extended his congratulations and best wishes to all the graduating students.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute (Deemed to be University), Dindigul, Tamil Nadu, today, and conferred gold medals on meritorious students. Emphasising that Viksit Bharat 2047 begins with developed villages, he highlighted the transformative progress in rural infrastructure and basic amenities over the past twelve years and called for ensuring greater opportunities and a dignified life for every rural citizen. Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, Chancellor Dr. K. M. Annamalai, Vice-Chancellor Dr. N. Panchanatham and other dignitaries were present.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 30, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President emphasised that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 can be realised only through the holistic development of villages. He stated that the real strength of Indialies in its villages and that rural development must remain a fundamental pillar of national development.

He stressed that the objective should not necessarily be to transform every village into a town, but to ensure that rural citizens have access to quality infrastructure, essential public services, livelihood opportunities and a dignified standard of living comparable to those available in urban areas.

Recalling the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi, the Vice-President said that the history of Gandhigram was closely intertwined with Gandhian philosophy. He recalled that Dr. G. Ramachandran and Dr. T. S. Soundaram Ramachandran, inspired by Mahatma Gandhi’s ideals, established the institution with the vision of promoting rural education, development and social transformation.

Highlighting the enduring power of truth and non-violence, he observed that Mahatma Gandhi had challenged the might of the British Empire through these principles and led India to freedom. Gandhian values, he said, continue to offer guidance to society and the nation.

Referring to India’s development journey over the past twelve years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President highlighted significant progress in rural housing, drinking water, electricity, roads, sanitation, agriculture and digital connectivity.

He noted that, approximately 25 crore people moved out of multidimensional poverty between 2014 and 2023. He observed that various development and welfare initiatives had contributed to improving the quality of life of millions of people.

Emphasising the importance of connectivity, he said that villages must be linked to towns and cities through improved road and transport infrastructure so that opportunities in education, healthcare, markets and employment reach rural communities.

He also underlined the impact of the Swachh Bharat Mission in creating greater awareness about cleanliness. Referring to improvements in the cleanliness of public spaces, he stressed that cleanliness was not merely the responsibility of the government but a collective responsibility of every citizen.

Stating that farmers’ welfare was directly linked to the country’s food security, he highlighted the importance of supporting the farming community. He referred to the PM-KISAN scheme, under which eligible farmer families receive financial assistance of ₹6,000 annually in three instalments directly into their bank accounts.

The Vice-President observed that Artificial Intelligence, automation and digital technologies were rapidly transforming the world and changing the nature of employment. He urged students to equip themselves with emerging technologies while developing creativity, problem-solving abilities and an entrepreneurial outlook.

He encouraged them to become job creators rather than merely job seekers. Referring to the contemporary relevance of Mahatma Gandhi’s philosophy of Swadeshi, he said that promoting domestic manufacturing, indigenous technologies, local industries and innovations by young Indians represented the modern expression of Swadeshi.

The Vice-President called upon the graduating students to use their education and skills not merely for personal advancement but also for the welfare of society. He urged them to make Gandhian values of simplicity, self-reliance, social responsibility and service the guiding principles of their lives.

He also urged students to stay away from drugs and substance abuse and become ambassadors of a drug-free society by creating awareness among their friends, families and communities.

Congratulating Gandhigram Rural Institute on completing fifty years of its journey as a deemed-to-be university, the Vice-President expressed confidence that it would continue to emerge as a leading centre for sustainable rural development, inclusive growth and innovative research.

On the occasion, the Vice-President conferred Honorary Doctorates (Honoris Causa) on three distinguished personalities in recognition of their outstanding contributions in their respective fields: Thavathiru Kundrakudi Ponnambala Adigalar, renowned spiritual leader and Tamil scholar; Shri S. Nambi Narayanan, former senior aerospace scientist of ISRO; and Professor S. S. M. Sundaram, distinguished academician.

At the 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute ( Deemed to be University), Dindigul, Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan conferred Honorary Doctorates (Honoris Causa) on Thavathiru Kundrakudi Ponnambala Adigalar, renowned spiritual and Tamil scholar; Shri S. Nambi Narayanan, former senior aerospace scientist of ISRO; and Professor S. S. M. Sundaram, distinguished academician, in recognition of their valuable contributions to spirituality, Tamil scholarship, science and education.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 30, 2026

As part of efforts to strengthen the institution’s academic and infrastructure facilities, the Vice-President inaugurated two new buildings, the Examination and Seminar Halls and the Pushpkunj Heritage Building.

During the Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Gandhigram Rural Institute, Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated two new buildings and laid the foundation stones for three new projects, including a 30-classroom academic complex. He also released the book “Inclusivity of India’s Ageing Population” and unveiled the Golden Jubilee Commemorative Postage Stamp and Postal Cover, marking a significant milestone in the institution’s journey.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 30, 2026

He also digitally laid the foundation stones for three projects: a 22 kV Power House and Control Room, an Academic Building for the School of Education, and an Academic Building Complex comprising 30 classrooms.

The Vice-President released the book “Inclusivity of India’s Ageing Population”. He also unveiled a Golden Jubilee Commemorative Postage Stamp and Postal Cover, marking an important milestone in the institution’s journey.

The Governor of Tamil Nadu, Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar; Chancellor, Dr. K. M. Annamalai; Vice-Chancellor, Dr. N. Panchanatham; Registrar, Dr. K. Marimuthu; faculty members, researchers, students, parents and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

2330371.title: India to Host ICAR- CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 in New Delhi from April 12–17; Over 5,000 Delegates Expected to participate
2330371.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
India to Host ICAR- CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 in New Delhi from April 12–17; Over 5,000 Delegates Expected to participate
CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 to Showcase India's Agricultural Transformation and Global Research Partnerships
CGIAR and ICAR to bring their work in India closer together around national priorities: Dr M L Jat
India to Promote South-South Cooperation and Share Agricultural Innovations with Global South: Dr. M. L. Jat
India–CGIAR Partnership Demonstrates the Transformative Power of Science and Technology: Dr. Ismahane Elouafi
Science, Technology and Global Partnerships Have Transformed India's Agricultural Landscape: Dr. Himanshu Pathak
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 2:29PM by PIB Delhi

CGIAR and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) today announced that New Delhi will host CGIAR Science and Partnership Week from 12th  to 17th April 2027. The event is organized by ICAR, of the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India, and CGIAR.

 

The week will bring researchers, farmers, governments, startups and businesses from around the world to New Delhi. Together, they will look at the innovations already reaching farmers and where more work is needed to reach many more.

India is a natural host. ICAR leads one of the world’s largest national agricultural research systems, and its scientists have worked with CGIAR for more than 50 years. Ten CGIAR research centers now work in India, on crops, water, livestock, fish, nutrition, and policy.

India’s agricultural science also reaches well beyond its borders. A groundnut sample from India, conserved and shared by ICRISAT, contributed to varieties now grown in Malawi, Uganda, Mozambique, and Zambia. Hyderabad’s Center of Excellence for South–South Cooperation in Agriculture shares proven farming innovations across Asia, Africa, and Latin America.

 

Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR highlighted the longstanding partnership between India and CGIAR, which has played a significant role in strengthening agricultural research and development in the country for over five decades.

 

He noted that CGIAR, an international agricultural research partnership comprising 15 research centres working across more than 100 countries, has contributed significantly to global agricultural advancement. Its collaboration with India, particularly through ICAR, has supported important developments in crop improvement, natural resource management, food security and agricultural productivity

Referring to India's agricultural transformation since the Green Revolution, Dr. Jat highlighted how collaboration with international research institutions, including CIMMYT, IRRI and ICRISAT, contributed to strengthening India's food production capabilities. From a food-deficit nation dependent on imports, India has emerged as a major food-producing and exporting country.

He emphasised that the CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 will provide an important platform to strengthen international cooperation and facilitate the exchange of scientific knowledge, technologies and best practices.

Dr. Jat stated that India's priority would be to promote South-South cooperation and share its successful agricultural innovations with the Global South, particularly African countries. He highlighted India's progress in climate-resilient agriculture, digital agriculture and AgriStack, agricultural mechanisation, millets, natural farming and sustainable agricultural practices as areas offering considerable opportunities for international collaboration.

He further noted that the event would deliberate on emerging priorities across the agri-food value chain, including climate resilience, water management, soil health, public-private partnerships, startups, youth and women's participation, and the role of media in communicating agricultural science and innovations.

Dr. Ismahane Elouafi, Executive Managing Director, CGIAR, emphasised that the upcoming event would celebrate the achievements of this longstanding partnership while developing a forward-looking agenda for the next 50 years of agricultural cooperation. She highlighted that India has shown what strong national science can achieve at scale. Seed and knowledge from India already help farmers in Africa and Asia. In April, we want to build on that exchange and consider together where science can do more, she added.

She also underscored the importance of recognising the contribution of science and scientists in improving human well-being and strengthening food systems. Referring to the successful first edition held in Nairobi, Kenya, in April 2025, she expressed confidence that the India edition would further strengthen global partnerships and bring together stakeholders to develop solutions for emerging agricultural challenges.

Dr. Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT  says “India's agricultural journey from a food-deficit nation to a major food-producing and exporting country reflects the transformative power of science, technology and international partnerships. Through CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027, we aim to showcase India's agricultural achievements, share our innovations with the world and learn from global advancements to co-create solutions for the emerging challenges of agriculture and food systems.”

The first CGIAR Science Week took place in Nairobi, Kenya, in April 2025, where CGIAR launched its current research portfolio. The New Delhi edition will focus on how we move from science to impact and how partnership can advance South–South cooperation. It will also explore how agricultural research and innovation can contribute to India’s vision for 2047.

The program and speakers will be announced in the coming months.

2330361.title: Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare is conducting Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5 from 1st to 30th November, 2026
2330361.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2330361.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare is conducting Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5 from 1st to 30th November, 2026
Camps to be held at 2000 Districts/Cities across the country, Largest ever DLC Campaign
Promotion of Digital Empowerment of Pensioners using Face Authentication technology
Saturation model adopted to achieve 2.30 crore DLCs with 1.50 crore Face Authenticated DLCs
19 Banks, 785 District Post offices, 56 Welfare Associations, MeitY & UIDAI  teams, CGDA, Railways, DoT, EPFO, State Governments to collaborate in the month-long campaign
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi

Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare will be conducting the 5th Nation-wide Digital Life Certificate campaign in 2000 cities/ Districts across India from November 1-30, 2026. The department has notified the guidelines through O.M. dated 13th August, 2026. This is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken.

A Whole of Government approach will be adopted through coordination with Pension Disbursing Banks, India Post Payments Bank, Pensioners’ Welfare Associations, CGDA, DoT, Railways, EPFO, State Governments, UIDAI & MeitY with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country.

The focus is majorly on promoting Face Authentication Technology. Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and UIDAI will provide technical support during this Campaign. Face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used on Android as well as iOS, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.

DD, AIR and PIB teams are actively geared up to provide full support to this campaign for Audio, Visual and Print publicity. Outreach efforts will be further complemented by SMSs, tweets (#DLCCampaign5), Jingles and Short films to spread awareness about the campaign.

The Campaign will be conducted in an ‘Utsav’ mode by offering a bouquet of services such as such as Health Check-ups, Aadhar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services will be provided to pensioners where required. Grievance officers will handle grievances regarding DLCs with an immediate resolution approach.

The campaign will be monitored by senior officials from DoPPW who will carry out on-ground reviews in identified states. Mega Camps will be held by stakeholders in areas having high concentration of pensioners and these Mega Camps will be attended by Senior officials from DPPW.

2330346.title: 19th India–BLEU Joint Economic Commission Session Held in Luxembourg to Strengthen Trade and Economic Cooperation
2330346.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
19th India–BLEU Joint Economic Commission Session Held in Luxembourg to Strengthen Trade and Economic Cooperation
Discussions Cover Key Sectors, Including Logistics, Renewable Energy, FinTech, Healthcare and Agro-Food Processing
India–BLEU JEC Explores Opportunities to Deepen Cooperation in Aerospace, Research, Innovation and Higher Education
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi

The 19th Session of the India–Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Joint Economic Commission (JEC) was held in Luxembourg on 29 October 2026. The meeting provided a platform for India, Belgium and Luxembourg to review bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss opportunities to further strengthen economic cooperation across key sectors.

The JEC was co-chaired by Commerce Secretary, Government of India, Shri Rajesh Agrawal; Director-General for Geo-Economy and Economic Diplomacy, Belgian Federal Public Service Foreign Affairs, Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation, H.E. Mr. Filip Vanden Bulcke; and Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, Defence, Development Cooperation and Foreign Trade, Luxembourg, H.E. Mr. Henri Schumacher.

The 19th Session reviewed existing trade and investment relations between India, Belgium and Luxembourg and deliberated on ways to enhance economic engagement, facilitate trade and investment flows, and strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

The discussions covered a broad range of priority sectors, including logistics, with a focus on air connectivity and ports, renewable energy and clean technology, financial services and FinTech, digital transformation and information and communication technology (ICT), healthcare and life sciences, Ayurveda and traditional medicine, and the agro and food processing industry.

The meeting resolved to explore opportunities to deepen cooperation in aerospace, research and innovation, higher education and skill development. Market-related issues were also discussed with a view to addressing trade concerns, facilitating market access and identifying opportunities to further strengthen economic ties.

The JEC provided an opportunity for the three sides to exchange views on their economic priorities, review sectoral cooperation and identify avenues for enhancing business engagement and investment partnerships. The discussions reaffirmed the importance of sustained dialogue and cooperation in advancing mutually beneficial economic relations between India, Belgium and Luxembourg.

Following the JEC session, Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal interacted with CEOs of Luxembourg-based companies during a business interaction. He highlighted India's strong economic growth and investment potential and underscored opportunities for collaboration in financial services, advanced manufacturing, logistics, clean energy, digital technologies, healthcare, and research and innovation. He encouraged Luxembourg companies to explore long-term investments, technology partnerships and opportunities to integrate with Indian firms to serve global value chains.

2330320.title: FIRST TRAINING SQUADRON OF THE INDIAN NAVY DEPARTS COLOMBO, SRI LANKA
2330320.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
FIRST TRAINING SQUADRON OF THE INDIAN NAVY DEPARTS COLOMBO, SRI LANKA
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi

Ships of the First Training Squadron (1TS) of the Indian Navy, comprising INS Tir, INS Sujata and ICGS Sarathi, departed Colombo, Sri Lanka, on 29 Oct 2026, marking the conclusion of a successful port call. The visit featured bilateral engagements between the Indian Navy (IN) and the Sri Lanka Navy (SLN), reinforcing defence cooperation and the maritime partnership between the two nations.

During the port call, the Senior Officer, 1TS, accompanied by the Commanding Officers of the ships, called on the Commander, Western Naval Area, Sri Lanka Navy. The interaction reaffirmed the close bilateral ties and the shared commitment of both navies to enhancing maritime cooperation.

As part of the professional engagements, sea trainees of 1TS visited the Naval and Maritime Academy (NMA), Trincomalee, and interacted with their Sri Lankan counterparts. In a reciprocal engagement, SLN cadets from NMA visited the 1TS ships and gained insights into the squadron’s training facilities and activities. These interactions provided opportunities for the exchange of experiences and fostered professional camaraderie among the trainees of both navies.

As part of its community outreach initiatives, Indian Navy personnel participated in a beach clean-up activity, promoting environmental sustainability. The ships were also opened to visitors, including members of the local community and the Indian diaspora, providing an opportunity to interact with the crew and gain an insight into the Indian Navy’s training and operational activities.

On departure from Colombo, the ships of 1TS undertook a Passage Exercise (PASSEX) with SLNS Nandimithra. The exercise facilitated coordinated maritime manoeuvres and enhanced operational coordination and interoperability between the two maritime forces.

The visit underscored the enduring maritime partnership between India and Sri Lanka and reaffirmed their shared commitment to regional maritime cooperation and capacity building, in line with the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

2330310.title: DRI busts a big clandestine synthetic drug manufacturing laboratory in Uttar Pradesh; seizes approx. 1,100 kg drugs and precursor chemicals; two arrested
2330310.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI busts a big clandestine synthetic drug manufacturing laboratory in Uttar Pradesh; seizes approx. 1,100 kg drugs and precursor chemicals; two arrested
Intelligence-led joint operation uncovers a fully functional illicit drug manufacturing facility in a remote village in Jalaun district
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 11:05AM by PIB Delhi

In a major crackdown on illicit synthetic drug manufacturing in the country, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) busted a big clandestine drug manufacturing laboratory operating in a remote village in Jalaun district, Uttar Pradesh. The operation led to the massive seizure of approximately 1,100 kg drugs and precursor chemicals, along with manufacturing equipment. Two persons have been arrested in connection with the case.

Acting on specific intelligence, a large team of DRI officers, with operational assistance from UP ATS, launched a coordinated operation at the suspected premises in the early hours of 29th October 2026.
The search of the premises revealed a well-established and functional laboratory for the manufacture of synthetic drugs, resulting into huge seizure of approximately 184 kg semi-prepared drugs, along with around 582 kg precursor chemicals and associated equipment used in the manufacturing process.

In swift follow-up action, searches at the residential premises of the accused led to the recovery of around 15.4 kg finished methaqualone, along with around 153 kg chemicals and a machine used in the manufacturing process. A further search at the premises of another accused resulted in another huge seizure of around 168 kg precursor chemicals. Two persons associated with the clandestine manufacturing facility were arrested under the provisions of NDPS Act,1985.

The recovery of huge quantities of finished drugs, semi-prepared material, precursor chemicals and manufacturing equipment indicates the existence of an organised illicit drug manufacturing operation. The operation has dealt a significant blow to the illicit drug manufacturing ecosystem by dismantling a large clandestine production facility, removing substantial quantities of drugs and precursor chemicals from the illicit supply chain, and preventing the manufacture of further quantities of synthetic drugs.

DRI remains committed to dismantling clandestine drug manufacturing networks, disrupting the supply chains that sustain illicit drug production, to combat the trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.

2330300.title: Holy Relics of Lord Buddha to be Exposed for Public Veneration in Arunachal Pradesh from 31 October to 21 November 2026
2330300.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Holy Relics of Lord Buddha to be Exposed for Public Veneration in Arunachal Pradesh from 31 October to 21 November 2026
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, to participate in the inaugural ceremony at Tawang on 31 October 2026
Sacred Piprahwa Relics from the National Museum, New Delhi, to be taken to Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai, reflecting Arunachal Pradesh's rich Buddhist traditions
Special Indian Air Force aircraft and helicopter arrangements planned for the safe and dignified transportation of the Holy Relics
Exhibition on the discovery and repatriation of the Piprahwa heritage to accompany the exposition at all three locations
International conference on “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond” to bring together monks, scholars and delegates from India and six other countries
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 10:35AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC) and the National Museum, New Delhi, is organising an exposition of the Holy Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha in Arunachal Pradesh from 31 October to 21 November 2026. The exposition will cover three important centres of Buddhist faith and heritage—Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai, providing devotees and members of the public an opportunity to pay homage to the Sacred Relics.

Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, is scheduled to participate in the inaugural ceremony at the historic Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) on 31 October 2026. The programme will be attended by distinguished representatives of the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, venerable members of the Buddhist Sangha, representatives of Buddhist institutions, devotees and other dignitaries.

The exposition is being organised in recognition of the deep spiritual significance of the Holy Relics and Arunachal Pradesh's distinctive place in India's Buddhist cultural landscape. It also reflects the Government of India's continuing commitment to the protection, preservation and dissemination of the country's Buddhist heritage, and to strengthening cultural and spiritual connections with Buddhist communities in India and abroad.

Tawang Monastery

 

Ceremonial Movement and Inauguration at Tawang

The Holy Relics, presently preserved at the National Museum, New Delhi, will commence their sacred journey with ceremonial observances at the Museum on the night of 30 October 2026. They will thereafter be taken to Air Force Station Palam for onward transportation to Arunachal Pradesh.

As per the proposed movement itinerary, the Holy Relics are scheduled to depart from Palam in the early hours of 31 October 2026 by a special Indian Air Force aircraft and reach Air Force Station Borjhar, Guwahati, before being transported by helicopter to Tawang.

Upon arrival, the Holy Relics will be received with due religious ceremony and reverence. They will thereafter be taken to Tawang Monastery for installation and the inaugural ceremony, scheduled between 10:00 AM and 11:30 AM on 31 October 2026.

A further inaugural function, together with the opening of the associated exposition and exhibition, is scheduled for 1 November 2026, with the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, as the Chief Guest.

The occasion coincides with the observance of Lhabab Düchen, a significant festival in the Tibetan Buddhist tradition commemorating the Buddha's descent from the heavenly realm. The exposition will thus bring together religious observance, cultural heritage and public participation in a spiritually meaningful setting.

The movement and installation of the Holy Relics are being planned with particular attention to their sanctity, security and conservation requirements. The Ministry of Culture is coordinating with the Ministry of Defence, Indian Air Force, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, National Museum and other concerned agencies for the necessary operational arrangements.

Bomdila Monastery

 

Exposition Schedule: Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai

The Holy Relics will be available for public darshan at the following locations:

Dates

Venue

Programme

31 October 2026

Gaden Namgyal Lhatse, Tawang Monastery

Arrival, ceremonial reception and inaugural ceremony

1–7 November 2026

Tawang Monastery

Public darshan and exposition

8–13 November 2026

TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila

Public darshan and exposition

14–20 November 2026

Golden Pagoda, Namsai

Public darshan and exposition

21 November 2026

Namsai–Tezu–New Delhi

Ceremonial departure and return of the Holy Relics to the National Museum

 

On 8 November, the Holy Relics are scheduled to travel from Tawang to Rupa by helicopter and thereafter by road to Bomdila. The itinerary includes ceremonial reception at Upper Gompa before their installation at Lower Gompa, where the inaugural ceremony is scheduled between 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM.

On 14 November, the Holy Relics will be transported from Bomdila to Rupa by road and thereafter by helicopter to Nalung Helipad, Namsai. They will be taken to the Golden Pagoda, where the installation and inaugural ceremony are scheduled between 11:00 AM and 12:00 noon.

Following the conclusion of public darshan at Namsai, the Holy Relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026, via Tezu Airport and Air Force Station Palam.

The timings and movement arrangements will remain subject to operational, weather and security considerations.

Namsai Pagoda

 

Sacred Piprahwa Relics: An Extraordinary Archaeological and Spiritual Heritage

The Holy Relics being taken to Arunachal Pradesh originate from Piprahwa in present-day Siddharthnagar district, Uttar Pradesh, an archaeological site associated with ancient Kapilavastu and the Shakya tradition of Lord Buddha.

Piprahwa occupies a prominent place in the archaeological history of Buddhism. In 1898, William Claxton Peppé excavated a stupa at the site and discovered reliquaries containing bone fragments and precious objects, bringing international attention to the historical and religious significance of the discovery.

Subsequently, the Archaeological Survey of India conducted further excavations between 1971 and 1977, under the supervision of archaeologist Shri K. M. Srivastava. Excavations at deeper levels revealed two additional reliquary caskets containing ancient bone relics traditionally associated with Lord Buddha.

The larger casket contained 12 sacred bone fragments, while the smaller casket contained 10, making a total of 22 sacred relics recovered during these excavations. Of these, 20 are preserved at the National Museum, New Delhi, and two at the Indian Museum, Kolkata.

The relics, comprising ancient osteological material, are regarded as exceptionally rare and are accorded profound religious reverence by Buddhist communities. Their historical and archaeological importance is accompanied by a deep spiritual significance rooted in the long-established Buddhist tradition of relic veneration.

Following the Mahāparinirvāṇa of Lord Buddha at Kushinagar, the tradition of enshrining His corporeal relics in stupas developed into an important expression of Buddhist devotion. Over the centuries, these sacred sites became centres of pilgrimage, religious learning and cultural exchange.

The present exposition offers devotees an opportunity to connect with this ancient spiritual tradition while also drawing attention to the importance of preserving archaeological and religious heritage for future generations.

Arunachal Pradesh: A Meeting Place of Buddhist Traditions

Arunachal Pradesh occupies a distinctive position in the Buddhist cultural geography of India. Its monasteries, religious institutions and living traditions reflect historical connections with the wider Himalayan region and other parts of Buddhist Asia.

The western and northern parts of the State, including Tawang and West Kameng, are particularly associated with the Mahāyāna and Vajrayāna traditions of Himalayan Buddhism.

Tawang Monastery, also known as Gaden Namgyal Lhatse, is an important centre of monastic learning, religious practice and cultural continuity. The monasteries of Bomdila similarly sustain the spiritual and artistic traditions of the region.

In eastern Arunachal Pradesh, particularly Namsai and adjoining areas, the Theravāda traditions followed by the Tai Khamti and other Buddhist communities represent another important dimension of India's diverse Buddhist heritage.

The exposition across Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai will therefore bring the Holy Relics to communities representing different Buddhist traditions, reflecting the diversity and shared spiritual foundations of Buddhism within the State.

Beyond its religious significance, the initiative is expected to strengthen awareness of Arunachal Pradesh's Buddhist heritage, encourage cultural exchange and promote the universal values of peace, compassion, non-violence and harmony associated with the teachings of Lord Buddha.

Government of India's Continuing Commitment to Buddhist Heritage

Under the leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has undertaken initiatives for the conservation, protection, promotion and international dissemination of India's Buddhist heritage.

These efforts include the preservation of Buddhist monuments and sacred objects, development of pilgrimage infrastructure, support for Buddhist scholarship and cultural exchanges, recovery of important heritage objects and organisation of international expositions of Sacred Relics.

The Government's approach recognises the importance of safeguarding India's civilisational inheritance while strengthening the cultural and spiritual relationships that connect India with Buddhist communities across the world.

A significant recent development was the return to India in 2025 of the Piprahwa jewel collection, associated with the historic 1898 discovery. Following the proposed international auction of the collection, the Ministry of Culture undertook efforts that contributed to its return after approximately 127 years.

The homecoming of these precious objects marked an important development in the preservation and recovery of India's cultural heritage and renewed public interest in the history of Piprahwa and the early Buddhist tradition.

The Government of India's initiatives also reflect the broader principle of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”, emphasising the complementary importance of development and preservation of heritage.

International Expositions: Strengthening India's Buddhist Cultural Connections

India has a longstanding tradition of sharing its sacred Buddhist heritage through international relic expositions, enabling devotees abroad to participate in public veneration and reinforcing historical bonds of friendship.

Over the decades, Government of India-supported expositions have taken place in countries including Sri Lanka, Mongolia, Singapore, the Republic of Korea and Thailand.

In recent years, such initiatives have continued to strengthen cultural diplomacy and people-to-people relations.

In 2022, the exposition of the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha in Mongolia reaffirmed the longstanding Buddhist connections between India and Mongolia.

In 2024, the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha, together with the relics of His two principal disciples, Arahant Sariputta and Arahant Mahamoggallana, were taken to Thailand for public veneration at Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Ubon Ratchathani and Krabi. The exposition witnessed participation by millions of devotees.

In 2025, the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha were taken to Vietnam during the Vesak celebrations, attracting widespread public participation. Expositions were also undertaken in Kalmykia, Russia, and Bhutan, further strengthening India's spiritual and cultural ties with Buddhist communities in these regions.

In February 2026, the sacred Devnimori Relics were taken to Sri Lanka for public veneration, reflecting the enduring Buddhist relationship between the two countries.

In May 2026, the exposition of the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha in Ladakh provided devotees and monastic communities of the Himalayan region an important opportunity for collective prayer and reverence.

Subsequently, during May–June 2026, the Holy Relics of Arahant Sariputta and Arahant Mahamoggallana from Sanchi were taken to Mongolia for a special exposition at the Gandan Tegchenling Monastery in Ulaanbaatar.

These initiatives demonstrate India's commitment to sharing its Buddhist heritage in a spirit of mutual respect, cultural understanding and spiritual fellowship.

The exposition in Arunachal Pradesh represents another important step in this continuing engagement, bringing the sacred heritage preserved at the National Museum closer to Buddhist communities in India's northeastern Himalayan region.

Special Exhibition: “Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa”

As an important accompanying initiative, the International Buddhist Confederation will organise an exhibition titled “Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery” at Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai.

The exhibition will present the historical and spiritual significance of Buddhist relic veneration, beginning with the life and teachings of Siddhartha Gautama and the development of the tradition of enshrining Sacred Relics following His Mahāparinirvāṇa.

It will trace the archaeological discoveries at Piprahwa, including the excavation undertaken by William Claxton Peppé in 1898 and the subsequent investigations by the Archaeological Survey of India.

The exhibition will also examine the historical journey of the Piprahwa jewels, their association with the Peppé family collection, the proposed international auction in 2025 and the subsequent efforts that led to their return to India.

Through this narrative, visitors will gain an understanding of the relationship between archaeological research, religious traditions, heritage preservation and the recovery of culturally significant objects.

The exhibition is expected to serve as an important educational and cultural component of the exposition, particularly for students, scholars, young visitors and members of the public interested in India's Buddhist history.

International Conference on “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond”

The International Buddhist Confederation, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, will also organise an international conference titled “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond” at the Kalawangpo Convention Hall, Tawang, on 2 November 2026.

The conference is expected to bring together venerable monks, Buddhist scholars and delegates from India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia and Germany.

It will provide a platform for scholarly dialogue on the historical transmission of Buddhist teachings, the evolution of monastic institutions, the preservation of Buddhist knowledge traditions and the contemporary relevance of Buddhist philosophy and ethical principles.

The deliberations will be organised around three broad themes:

1. Carrying Forward the Buddha's Legacy after Mahāparinirvāṇa

This theme will examine the continuity of Buddhist teachings and practices following the Mahāparinirvāṇa of Lord Buddha. Discussions will cover the Four Noble Truths as a living heritage, conservation and material culture, the evolution of religious institutions, international engagement through Sacred Relic expositions and Buddhism's contribution to shared cultural traditions.

2. Historical and Doctrinal Continuity of Buddhism

This theme will focus on the intergenerational transmission of Buddhist textual and monastic lineages, with particular reference to Arunachal Pradesh. It will also explore the plurality of Buddhist schools, shared doctrinal foundations, language and interpretation, pedagogical traditions, and the preservation of Buddhist ideas through art and cultural expression.

3. Buddhism and Right Livelihood

The third theme will explore the contemporary relevance of Buddhist ethical teachings, including connections between the intellectual traditions of Nalanda and modern academia, cultural tourism and pilgrimage, skill development, sustainable livelihoods, and the relationship between Buddhism, globalisation and consumerism.

The conference will highlight Arunachal Pradesh's importance as a living centre of Buddhist heritage, where diverse traditions have been sustained through monastic institutions, community practices and cultural exchange.

It will also provide an opportunity to examine how Buddhist thought and ethical principles can contribute to contemporary discussions on education, sustainability, cultural preservation and peaceful coexistence.

Institutional Coordination and Public Facilitation

The exposition is being undertaken through coordinated efforts of the Ministry of Culture, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, National Museum, International Buddhist Confederation and other concerned institutions.

The National Museum, New Delhi, as the nodal agency, is responsible for the technical and conservation aspects of the Holy Relics, including their secure handling, transportation, installation and safe return.

The Government of Arunachal Pradesh is coordinating arrangements at the respective venues, including security, reception, infrastructure, crowd management, medical facilities, sanitation, local transportation and public facilitation.

The International Buddhist Confederation is facilitating religious coordination, participation of venerable monks, associated cultural and scholarly programmes, the Piprahwa exhibition and the international conference.

The Ministry of Defence and the Indian Air Force have been approached for the requisite aircraft and helicopter support for movement of the Holy Relics, taking into account the challenging terrain and operational requirements of Arunachal Pradesh.

Media coverage and public outreach are being coordinated with the concerned agencies to disseminate information regarding the exposition and associated programmes.

The arrangements are intended to ensure that public veneration is conducted in an orderly, secure and dignified manner, while maintaining the highest standards of religious sanctity and conservation.

A Shared Message of Peace, Compassion and Harmony

The exposition of the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha in Arunachal Pradesh represents an important occasion for spiritual reflection, cultural participation and the celebration of India's Buddhist heritage.

By bringing the Sacred Relics to Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai, the initiative will provide devotees from different Buddhist traditions an opportunity to participate in public veneration and reaffirm their shared spiritual inheritance.

The accompanying exhibition and international conference will further enrich the occasion by connecting religious devotion with historical understanding, scholarship and cultural exchange.

The exposition also carries a message of wider significance. The teachings of Lord Buddha—compassion, non-violence, wisdom, moderation and peaceful coexistence continue to offer valuable guidance to humanity in an increasingly interconnected world.

Through the preservation of sacred heritage and its responsible dissemination, the Government of India seeks to strengthen cultural understanding, encourage people-to-people connections and promote the enduring message of peace and harmony associated with Bhagwan Buddha.

The exposition will conclude on 21 November 2026 with the ceremonial return of the Holy Relics to the National Museum, New Delhi.

2330299.title: Government notifies National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers and Gig & Platform Workers under the Labour Codes
2330299.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Government notifies National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers and Gig & Platform Workers under the Labour Codes
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 10:29AM by PIB Delhi

In a landmark step toward ensuring comprehensive social security for India's massive informal workforce, the Ministry of Labour & Employment has notified the official constitution of the National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers and Gig & Platform Workers. Established under the statutory framework of the Code on Social Security, these Boards mark a historic shift by integrating digital gig and platform professionals into India's formal welfare architecture.

The Boards will be presided over by the Union Minister for Labour & Employment and comprise representatives from Central and State Governments, prominent aggregator companies, employers, civil society organizations, workers' unions and gig & platform Associations. The Boards are mandated to design, monitor, and recommend targeted welfare schemes to bridge the social security gap for millions of gig & platform workers alongside traditional unorganised workers.

The National Social Security Boards shall meet at least thrice a year and shall observe rules of procedure relating to the transaction of business at its meetings, as prescribed by the Central Government.

The National Social Security Boards shall perform the following functions, namely:-

(a) recommend to the Central Government for framing suitable schemes for different sections of unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers;

(b) advise the Central Government on such matters arising out of the administration of this Code as may be referred to it;

(c) monitor such social welfare schemes for unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers as are administered by the Central Government,

(d) review the record keeping functions performed at the State level;

(e) review the expenditure from the fund and account; and

(f) undertake other functions as are assigned to it by the Central Government from time to time.

2330291.title: Fisheries Sector Looks Beyond Production: Fish Value Addition Enterprises and Mobile Marketing Set to Transform High-Value India’s Blue Economy
2330291.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2330291.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Fisheries Sector Looks Beyond Production: Fish Value Addition Enterprises and Mobile Marketing Set to Transform High-Value India’s Blue Economy
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 7:55AM by PIB Delhi

India’s fisheries sector is evolving from a production-focused activity into a dynamic, technology-driven and value-oriented pillar of the national economy. It plays a vital role in strengthening food and nutritional security, generating employment, supporting rural livelihoods and contributing to export earnings.

The fisheries ecosystem has witnessed significant transformation through value addition, cold-chain development, modern processing, mobile fish marketing and start-up-led innovation. Enterprises are increasingly adopting Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, blockchain, drone technology, smart cold-chain systems and precision aquaculture to improve traceability, productivity, quality assurance and post-harvest management. Together, these interventions are reducing losses, enhancing profitability and strengthening the fisheries value chain.

Value addition is emerging as a critical lever in reshaping India’s fisheries sector from a primary production activity into a diversified and market-oriented enterprise. By enabling fish and fishery products to be processed, packaged, branded and made available in ready-to-cook or ready-to-eat formats, it allows producers to secure better prices while responding to changing consumer preferences in domestic and export markets. More importantly, value addition helps reduce post-harvest losses, extend shelf life and improve quality standards across the supply chain. It also opens new avenues of employment and entrepreneurship, particularly for fishers, fish farmers, women’s groups, youth, cooperatives and small enterprises engaged in processing, packaging, cold-chain logistics, marketing and retail. In doing so, value addition strengthens market linkages, enhances incomes and positions the fisheries sector to compete more effectively in the growing market for safe, convenient and high-quality seafood.

This shift towards value-addition has been supported by a series of public investments and targeted policy interventions aimed at strengthening the sector from production to markets. Since 2015, the Government of India has significantly stepped-up public investment in the fisheries sector, committing Rs. 39,272 crore through key schemes and programmes such as the Blue Revolution Scheme, Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Samridhi Sah Yojana (PM-MKSSY) and Kisan Credit Card (KCC). These interventions are aimed at expanding infrastructure, strengthening production and post-harvest systems, and creating employment and livelihood opportunities for 74.66 lakh fishers and fish farmers across the country.

A parallel focus has been placed on strengthening transportation and logistics networks, with 46,500 facilities, including fish transportation systems, retail and wholesale fish markets, kiosks, feed mills, ice plants, cold storages and value-added enterprise units, added with an investment of Rs. 3,393.85 crore. In addition, five modern and smart fish markets are under development, integrating advanced IT systems, green technologies and logistics supply chains, and are expected to generate 15,900 employment opportunities.

Alongside infrastructure and logistics, the availability of quality raw material is equally critical for sustaining premium fish value chains. As India looks to expand value addition around premium fish products, ensuring a steady supply of quality raw material has become increasingly important. In this direction, the Department has taken up genetic improvement initiatives to develop fish varieties with faster growth, improved disease resistance, better resilience and higher productivity. The effort is expected to support the availability of high-value species such as trout, shrimp, catla, rohu, tilapia, pangasius, seabass and scampi for domestic consumption, processing and export-oriented markets. By strengthening the production base for such species, genetic improvement can complement value-added enterprises, improve farm-level returns and help India move up the fisheries value chain.

For these gains to reach small producers, institutional models that can aggregate production and improve access to markets are becoming increasingly important. The push towards value addition in fisheries is also being anchored in collective enterprise models that can help small fishers and fish farmers overcome constraints of scale, capital and market access. The Department has supported the formation of 2,195 Fisheries Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) enabling producers to aggregate output, pool resources and participate more effectively in processing, branding and marketing activities. Several of these organisations have also been integrated with the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), widening their access to digital markets and improving prospects for fair price realisation. Under PM-MKSSY, 5,500 fisheries cooperatives are being strengthened to function as FFPOs in collaboration with intermediary agencies such as NCDC, NAFED, SFAC and NERAMAC. By building collective bargaining power and linking producer groups with modern value chains, these institutions are expected to support a more inclusive transition towards value-added fisheries enterprises.

The emphasis on value addition is also creating a stronger platform for women’s participation in post-harvest activities and fisheries-based enterprises. Women have emerged as a vital force in India’s fisheries sector, particularly in post-harvest operations and small-scale enterprises, where value addition has opened new avenues for income generation and entrepreneurship. Their empowerment has been prioritised under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), under which projects worth more than Rs. 4,155 crore, with a central share of Rs. 1,572 crore have been approved over the last five years for the benefit of more than 1.28 lakh women beneficiaries. This support has enabled women to participate in diverse such as fish drying, preparation of fish pickles and papad, smoked fish products, fish powder, and packaging and retailing. Mobile fish vending units and micro‑processing enterprises are generating sustainable livelihoods for women across coastal, inland, and northeastern states, while also strengthening nutritional security by expanding access to affordable, protein‑rich food.

India’s fisheries sector is increasingly moving beyond production towards a value-chain-driven and technology-enabled ecosystem, supported by investments in processing, logistics, cold-chain infrastructure, digital platforms and entrepreneurship. With the convergence of PMMSY, PM-MKSSY, FIDF and KCC, the sector is better positioned to reduce post-harvest losses, expand value-added seafood exports, improve fisher incomes, promote women-led enterprises and generate rural employment. The future of Indian fisheries will depend not merely on producing more fish, but on building resilient, market-oriented value chains that connect fishers and fish farmers with consumers through innovation, mobility, processing and sustainable market development.

2330284.title: Clarification on the Process of Strategic Restructuring of the IDBI Bank Ltd.
2330284.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Clarification on the Process of Strategic Restructuring of the IDBI Bank Ltd.
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 9:54PM by PIB Delhi

The first or initial bid round was conducted in the financial year 2025-26 by DIPAM as per its internal practices, which are in the nature of indicative guidelines and not hidebound rules or regulations. The foreword itself states that the procedure suggested is not to be construed as a rigid, legal framework, which may require due adaptation/ modification in the best interest of successful execution of the transaction in a time bound manner. Given the complex nature of strategic transactions, the indicative guidelines give flexibility to ensure cost and time spent in lengthy processes is not wasted.

The press note dated 14.10.2026 clearly explains that there is no a-priori benchmark for bidding. The bidders do their own valuation and submit their bids in a confidential manner. Independent agencies are hired to do a fair valuation of the enterprise contemporaneously, which is then used as a comparator to assess the reasonableness of the bids submitted. The bid discovered price and the comparative valuation can, therefore, be above or below each other.

To handle this situation, provision is ex-ante built into Para 5.3.6(iii) the RFP: “In the event the Financial Bid of the Highest Bidder is lower than the reserve price, the Gol will decide the further course of action and the QIPs shall not subsequently question any decision taken by the Gol in this regard.”

There is no procedure prescribed to handle this situation internally within DIPAM and special powers have been delegated to the Core Group of Secretaries on Disinvestment (CGD) by the Cabinet Committee of Economic Affairs (CCEA) for this purpose. In its meeting dated August 16, 2017, while approving the Note titled ‘Procedure and Mechanism for Strategic Disinvestment - Delegation Thereof’, the CCEA has empowered the CGD to remove all difficulties, including deviations from procedure, to ensure effective implementation of the strategic disinvestment transactions approved by the CCEA. The abstract of the decision is as follows:

“8.1 Approval of the CCEA is solicited in case of strategic disinvestment...(ii) for empowering the CGD to take policy decisions with regard to procedural issues and to consider deviations as necessary from time to time for (the) effective implementation of decisions of CCEA”. Decision: Approved in the CCEA Meeting dated August 16th, 2017.

In due exercise of these powers, the procedure for the second or the best offer round was determined by the CGD itself. The reserve price was neither decreased, nor increased, and the first round itself became functus officio after the initial bids were not approved. 

The entire valuation methodology was reviewed by the CGD in April, 2026 before the invitation of best offer bids.  Since the comparator used for valuation has to be contemporaneous with the bids received, and 31st March, 2026 closing financial accounts were released in the public domain in end-April, the independent valuation agencies had started working on the revised valuations in May, 2026 itself. The process remained double blind because the bidder did not know the valuation and the valuators did not see the bids. It is only the CGD which gets to see a complete picture and compares the bids with fair valuations to take a final call on the reasonableness of the bids submitted.

The valuation was carried out by two different advisers, independent of each other, using independent and distinct methodologies. The Business Valuation is always done through the Transaction Adviser as per the protocol, who, given the complex nature of this transaction, further appointed professional experts trained in the Market Multiple Method. To explain briefly, the Market Multiple method is of two sub-types: the Comparable Company Method and the Comparable Transaction Method. Since suitable comparable transaction were not available, comparable companies’ method was used, which in this case were all the listed public sector banks. It is pertinent to mention here that the IDBI was a government ‘owned’ banking company till 2019, but became a government ‘controlled’ banking company after the LIC acquired majority stakes in 2019. Since there is no specific regulatory protocol for this situation, the RBI started treating it as a private bank only for regulatory purposes, even though the ownership stayed overwhelmingly with the LIC and the GoI, and the market investors continued to value it as a public sector entity. 

The Asset Valuer also used robust and time-tested methodologies, including additional value for disputed tax demands, which were indemnified as a common demand of the qualified bidders to nudge the bid offer upwards. This remains a low probability event and revenue neutral for the government, as only the additional tax demand, if paid at all, will be eligible for reimbursement. The potential liability that could arise on this account was only Rs. 627 crores while the bid discovered price increased by Rs 3,917 crores enhancing the value of the transaction for the GoI and the LIC.

The details of the volatile stock price of the narrowly traded IDBI stock and why it was discarded are well explained in the press note date 14.10.2026. The GoI and the LIC retain residual shareholdings to get further benefit from the upside that is expected from the value enhancement following strategic restructuring of the IDBI Bank going forward in future.

2330281.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Greater FTA Utilisation by Telangana
2330281.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Greater FTA Utilisation by Telangana
Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Pharma Innovation, Global GI Exports and Ease of Doing Business to Drive Telangana’s Growth
India’s FTAs Provide Preferential Market Access to 76% of Global GDP: Shri Piyush Goyal
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 9:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, today highlighted India’s growing trade partnerships, policy stability and investment opportunities while addressing the curtain raiser of the Invest Telangana Global Summit in New Delhi. Congratulating the Chief Minister of Telangana, Shri A. Revanth Reddy, on convening the summit, Shri Goyal said the State’s ambition to become a $3 trillion economy by 2047 was achievable through collective efforts by the Central Government, State Government, industry, investors and citizens.

Shri Goyal said India’s existing trade agreements had provided preferential market access to a global GDP of $70 trillion, including $10 trillion through agreements finalised more than a decade ago and an additional $60 trillion through the nine recently finalised agreements. With negotiations underway for another eight bilateral or multilateral agreements, which he said would add a further $15 trillion, India would have preferential market access covering approximately 76 per cent of the global GDP of $115 trillion.

He noted that the IMF had projected global trade growth of barely 1.9 per cent amid global challenges. Against this backdrop, India set a target of $1 trillion in exports, aiming for 15 per cent growth in the current year. He said the target reflected the collective conviction of exporters, industry associations and businesses to surpass conventional forecasts.

Highlighting India’s economic performance, Shri Goyal said the country had moved from the “Fragile Five” a decade ago to the world’s fifth-largest economy and the fastest-growing large economy. He cited growth of 7.7 per cent in the previous year and 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of the current year, expressing the expectation that growth would remain above 7 per cent in the quarter ending September. He also referred to the IMF’s recent assessment of stronger-than-expected economic performance and its expectation that India would continue to be the fastest-growing large economy in the current and following year.

The Minister acknowledged global uncertainties arising from conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. He said India continued to demonstrate resilience amid these challenges and highlighted upgrades to India’s credit rating by multiple international rating agencies, including the Japanese Credit Rating Agency (JCR), which upgraded India’s rating for the first time in over 35 years.

The Minister said India offered investors stable policies, open borders, supply chain resilience and the assurance that the rule of law would protect their interests. He highlighted that, over the preceding four and a half years, India had negotiated and finalised nine free trade agreements or bilateral trade agreements, opening opportunities for Indian businesses in 38 developed countries. He said these countries offered complementary capabilities, including advanced equipment, modern technologies, high-tech devices and graphics processing units (GPUs) required by Indian industry.

Referring to Telangana’s historical trading traditions, Shri Goyal recalled the Motupalli Abhaya Shasana, a maritime charter issued in 1244 by Kakatiya ruler, Ganapati Deva, which promoted stability and predictability in trade. He drew parallels with the present, noting that investors continue to seek certainty and continuity in policy.

Emphasising the collective responsibility towards Viksit Bharat 2047, Shri Goyal said the country’s journey towards shared prosperity required the collective drive and energy of 1.4 billion Indians. He said the commitment and capabilities of Telangana’s skilled, qualified and youthful population could help the State set new benchmarks for growth and development.

Referring to Telangana’s aspiration to grow from an economy of approximately $200 billion to $3 trillion by 2047, he welcomed the target set by the state government.

“Impossible doesn’t exist in my dictionary,” Shri Goyal said, acknowledging that achieving the target would require considerable collective effort. He said the Central Government, State Government, businesses, investors, farmers, fishermen, technical manpower, scientists, innovators, startups, women entrepreneurs and officials would all have to contribute to the State’s development.

Shri Goyal said Telangana is well positioned to contribute to the Viksit Bharat vision through its pharmaceutical industry, aerospace and defence capabilities, value-added agriculture, food processing, research and development, innovation and services sector. He also highlighted the opportunities presented by global capability centres, design and innovation, and the State’s talent in artificial intelligence and quantum computing.

Emphasising that every contribution mattered to economic development, the Minister referred to the dispatch of 2.5 metric tonnes of GI-tagged Tandur red gram from Hyderabad to Australia, leveraging the India-Australia free trade agreement. He said such exports demonstrated how trade agreements could create opportunities not only for large industries but also for farmers and smaller producers.

Shri Goyal emphasised that every contribution, big or small, was important to India’s development journey. He highlighted the role of farmers, entrepreneurs, MSMEs and other stakeholders in collectively advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

The Minister reiterated the Central Government’s commitment to Telangana’s development and referred to projects launched or supported in the State. He mentioned the foundation stone for the Zaheerabad Industrial Smart City, which he said would provide plug-and-play industrial land for automobiles, food processing, machinery and electrical equipment. He also referred to the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park in Warangal, describing it as the first fully functional PM MITRA park, and highlighted its alignment with the 5F vision of “farm to fibre, fibre to factory, factory to fashion, and fashion to foreign”.

Calling for closer coordination between the Centre and the States, Shri Goyal said Telangana’s development vision for 2047 was aligned with the national vision of Viksit Bharat articulated by Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi.

Outlining six suggestions for the way forward, Shri Goyal proposed that Telangana identify its 50 leading export products across goods and services and map markets offering preferential access under existing FTAs. He also suggested setting up FTA help desks in every district to help MSMEs, farmers and startups make the most of these agreements.

He called for taking GI-tagged products such as Tandur red gram, Chatpata chilli and Nizamabad turmeric to global markets, stressing the need for traceability, packaging and branding to help farmers secure a premium for their produce.

Shri Goyal suggested moving Telangana’s pharmaceutical industry up the value chain by strengthening domestic capabilities in key starting materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), investing in innovation, and moving beyond generics towards high-value branded and innovative pharmaceutical products, biosimilars and biotechnology.

Identifying opportunities in space, aerospace, aircraft components, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), defence, electronics, artificial intelligence, quantum computing and machine learning, he called for developing precision engineering and tooling capabilities, establishing advanced testing facilities and partnering with leading global institutions in science, technology and manufacturing.

He also proposed stronger linkages between industry, academia and government to advance research and development and skilling, helping prepare the workforce for future industrial and technological requirements.

Finally, Shri Goyal suggested accelerating ease-of-doing-business reforms through the decriminalisation of minor offences, reduced compliance burdens, simplified procedures and time-bound single-window clearances. Referring to the Centre’s efforts in this direction, he encouraged Telangana to consider similar measures to simplify business operations and citizens’ lives, thereby strengthening ease of living across the State.

Concluding his address, Shri Goyal invoked the symbolism of Diwali, saying that light spreads one diya at a time. He said every investment, export, new job and startup would bring Telangana and the whole nation closer to the shared vision of a developed and prosperous nation by 2047. Inviting investors from India and across the world to explore Telangana’s opportunities, he called for enduring partnerships that generate employment and contribute to the prosperity of the people of Telangana and India.

***

2330273.title: 14th International Tourism Mart Inaugurated in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
2330273.body_html:
Ministry of Tourism
14th International Tourism Mart Inaugurated in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
Union Tourism Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat calls for transforming North East’s tourism potential into business opportunities and sustainable livelihood
Ministry of Tourism emphasises sustainable tourism, improved connectivity and livelihood opportunities for local communities
Domestic tourist visits to North Eastern States increase from 95.65 lakh in 2019 to 1.51 crore in 2025
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 9:22PM by PIB Delhi

The 14th edition of the International Tourism Mart (ITM), organised by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in association with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and other North Eastern States, commenced today at Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. The three-day Mart, being held from 29 to 31 October 2026, aims to showcase the tourism potential of the eight North Eastern States and strengthen business engagement with domestic and international tourism markets.

The inaugural session was held in the presence of Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Tourism and Culture; Shri Suresh Gopi, Union Minister of State for Tourism and Petroleum & Natural Gas; Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education and Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER); Shri Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh; and Shri Prem Singh Tamang, Chief Minister of Sikkim. Tourism Ministers from the North Eastern States, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, international and domestic tourism stakeholders and representatives of the travel industry were also present. Addressing the inaugural session, Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat emphasised that the International Tourism Mart has evolved beyond a promotional platform into an important avenue for tourism partnerships and business opportunities. He stated, “ITM is not merely a tourism marketplace; it is a platform for building partnerships, generating business opportunities and creating a shared vision for the growth of tourism in the North East Region.”

Highlighting the immense potential of the region, the Minister said that its rich biodiversity, cultural heritage, spiritual traditions and natural landscapes offer distinctive opportunities for adventure, nature-based and experiential tourism. He particularly emphasised the potential of adventure tourism, music festivals and concert tourism to attract new visitor segments, encourage longer stays and generate economic opportunities for local communities. He also called for developing tourism experiences with appropriate safety standards, community participation and environmental safeguards.

The Minister highlighted the Government’s continued focus on improving connectivity, tourism infrastructure and destination experiences in the North Eastern Region. He also underlined the Ministry’s support for tourism promotion through domestic and international travel fairs, festivals, digital platforms and familiarisation visits, along with skill development initiatives to create employment opportunities for local youth.

Earlier, addressing a press conference, Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat highlighted that the 14th International Tourism Mart has brought together 43 international buyers from 22 countries, the highest-ever international buyer participation at ITM, along with 42 domestic buyers from 16 States and Union Territories and 81 sellers. He emphasised that hosting the Mart in Tawang would bring greater attention to lesser-known destinations in the North Eastern Region and showcase their tourism potential to domestic and international markets. Highlighting the growth of tourism in the region, he noted that domestic tourist visits to the eight North Eastern States increased from 95.65 lakh in 2019 to 1.51 crore in 2025, registering a growth of approximately 58%.

The Minister also highlighted the Government’s continued focus on strengthening tourism infrastructure and connectivity in the region. He informed that 16 projects worth ₹1,309 crore have been sanctioned under Swadesh Darshan 1.0, 17 projects worth ₹564 crore under Swadesh Darshan 2.0, nine projects worth ₹139 crore under Challenge Based Destination Development, nine projects worth ₹790 crore under SASCI and nine projects worth ₹258 crore under PRASHAD. Additionally, the Ministry has supported ten tourism routes in the North Eastern Region under the Regional Connectivity Scheme–UDAN. He reiterated the Government’s commitment to promoting sustainable tourism, improving visitor experiences and creating livelihood opportunities for local communities.

During the inaugural session, Union Minister of State for Tourism Shri Suresh Gopi highlighted the opportunities for developing innovative tourism products, including cultural, adventure, festival and community-based experiences. He also emphasised the importance of the Ministry’s initiatives, Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 and the National Digital Tourism Stack, in promoting lesser-known destinations and improving digital visibility and market access for local tourism service providers.

The inaugural session also featured addresses by Shri Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh; Shri Prem Singh Tamang, Chief Minister of Sikkim; and Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education and DoNER.

As part of the programme, the North East Bazaar was inaugurated, showcasing traditional handicrafts, handlooms and other cultural offerings of the region. A cultural programme highlighting the rich traditions of the North Eastern States was also organised.

The Mart will feature tourism presentations by all eight North Eastern States and structured B2B meetings. A Regional Meeting of Tourism Ministers of the North Eastern States will be held on 30 October 2026 to deliberate on tourism development, regional cooperation, tourist facilitation and emerging tourism opportunities.

The 14th edition marks the return of the International Tourism Mart to Tawang after 13 years, following the second edition held here in 2013. The event seeks to strengthen tourism partnerships, promote lesser-known destinations and position the North Eastern Region as a leading destination for sustainable and experience-based tourism.
