2329137.title: ‘Opportunity for Shared Commitment to Improve Future of Our Cities’: Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Opens ARISE Cities Forum 2026
2329137.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
‘Opportunity for Shared Commitment to Improve Future of Our Cities’: Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Opens ARISE Cities Forum 2026
Second edition of the forum brings together 200+ delegates from 50+ cities across 18+ countries representing the Global South.
Discussions must lead to practical actions that cities can adopt, says MoS.
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi

The second edition of the ARISE Cities Forum opened today at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi today. The two-day Forum is being organised by ICLEI South Asia, in collaboration with the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), with support from the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India.

Themed “From Bharat to Antalya — Commit. Implement. Deliver,” the Forum features 3 technical plenaries and 14 technical sessions, focusing on the experiences of local governments from the Global South region in advancing urban resilience, sustainability, and equitable and low-carbon development. The discussions feed into the Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals 2026, which will be adopted on 28 October, 2026 at the forum and presented at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye.

The Inaugural Ceremony of the Forum was graced by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India; Shoko Ishikawa, Country Representative, UN Women India; Dr Debolina Kundu, Director, National Institute of Urban Affairs; Gino Van Begin, Secretary General, ICLEI; and Emani Kumar, Deputy Secretary General, ICLEI and Executive Director, ICLEI South Asia.

Also present were Adv. Minimol V.K, Hon’ble Mayor of Kochi, India; Ismail Rafeeq, Hon’ble Mayor of Fuvahmulah, Maldives; Bhola Pokhrel, Hon’ble Mayor of Karjanha, Nepal; and Thinley Namgay, Hon’ble Mayor of Samdrup Jongkhar, Bhutan, representing urban leadership from across South Asia.

Appreciating the progress made since the first edition of the Forum, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Tokhan Sahu called for collective efforts to develop sustainable cities to fulfil India’s climate commitments and realise the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. “From resolve to planning, from planning to implementation, and from implementation to results—that should be our way of working. Our goal is to build cities where development reaches every section of society and creates better opportunities for future generations,” he said.

Calling for gender-responsive and inclusive urban development, Country Representative, UN Women India Shoko Ishikawa stated, “Drawing on the lessons gained from our initiatives in India, there are three priorities: integrate gender equality into urban planning, climate policies and investments; invest in urban infrastructure and services that strengthen women's safety, mobility and economic participation; and institutionalise women's leadership and accountability in urban climate action.” She added that UN Women looks forward to working with the ARISE Cities Forum to carry this agenda forward so that women and girls help shape the cities of tomorrow.

Director of the National Institute of Urban Affairs, Dr Debolina Kundu, noted that the theme of this year's Forum, "From Bharat to Antalya – Commit, Implement, Deliver," reflects the urgency of moving from climate commitments to action. “As we look towards COP31, it is important that the experiences, priorities and solutions emerging from our cities find a stronger place in national and global climate conversations,” she remarked.

Secretary General of ICLEI, Gino Van Begin, also spoke of the potential of urban local governments, stating, “Cities are developing innovative solutions, building functioning partnerships and demonstrating pathways towards more resilient, inclusive and sustainable futures. Their experiences and priorities must have a stronger voice in global processes such as the UNFCCC COPs, and this is what the ARISE Cities Forum aims to achieve.”

Emphasising the purpose of the Forum, Deputy Secretary General, ICLEI and Executive Director, ICLEI South Asia, Emani Kumar said, “The ARISE Cities Forum aims to amplify voices from the Global South so they are heard ‘from Bharat to Antalya’. We will carry the Delhi Declaration, a key outcome of our collective efforts and a shared call for stronger local climate action, to the global stage at COP31 to make sure that the perspectives and priorities of our cities and urban stakeholders are heard loud and clear.”

 

Advancing sustainable, equitable and resilient cities Across the Global South: Takeaways from Day 1 of the ARISE Cities Forum 2026

Day 1 of the ARISE Cities Forum 2026 featured 2 Plenary sessions and 8 technical sessions. The discussions, featuring high-level representatives from city governments, state-level bodies, embassies, UN agencies, development institutions, and experts, spanned topics such as

 

  • the need for strengthening multilevel action to translate global climate commitments into measurable action on the ground,
  • climate-resilient water management and sustainable energy transition in cities,
  • advancing urban biodiversity and nature-positive cities,
  • positioning entertainment and culture as an actionable lever for systemic urban resilience,
  • building resilient coastal cities and communities, and
  • integrating public health and child- and youth-focused initiatives with climate-resilient urban planning.

 

The winners of the Youth for Climate Hackathon 2.0 were also felicitated with the Ritu Thakur Memorial Award on Day 1 of the Forum. The Hackathon invited solutions on ‘Action-Oriented Transition: Translating Resilient, Scalable, and Inclusive Solutions for Circular Cities’ by young innovators from countries in South Asia.

A Memorandum of Understanding was also exchanged between Global Buildings Performance Network (GBPN) and ICLEI South Asia.

 

Launches on Day 1 of the ARISE Cities Forum

 

The Inaugural and technical sessions on 27 October also featured the launch of the following:

  • The Centre for Sustainable Urban Mobility and Integrated Transportation (SUMMIT)
  • Investing in Climate Resilient Cities - State-Level Project Pipelines: Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh & Telangana reports
  • Embedding Gender Equity and Responsive Transport - A Compendium of Case Studies for Gender and Mobility in India
  • A Compendium of Case Studies for Mobilising Funds to Enable Integrated Planning and Infrastructure Development
  • Policy Framework for Gender Equality in Public Bus Transport Systems
  • Guidelines on Canal Restoration using Nature-based Solutions
  • Poster for the ‘Early Action for Children’s Health (EACH): Towards Heat Resilience and Clean Air’ project in collaboration with UNICEF India
  • ICLEI South Asia’s Annual Report for 2025–26

 

Looking ahead to COP31

The Forum will continue on 28 October, with one Plenary, six technical sessions, and the Closing Ceremony, where the Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals 2026 will be adopted and handed over to Samed Ağırbaş, COP31 Climate Champion and President of the Zero Waste Foundation. The Declaration will mark a key milestone in carrying the ARISE Cities Forum’s collective commitments and urban priorities forward to COP31 in Antalya, strengthening the presence of cities from the Global South on the global climate stage.

For more information on the ARISE Cities Forum 2026 and its agenda, please visit: https://arisecitiesforum.org/

2329132.title: DPIIT Launches 6th Edition of National Startup Awards to Recognise Innovation and Entrepreneurship
2329132.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
DPIIT Launches 6th Edition of National Startup Awards to Recognise Innovation and Entrepreneurship
National Startup Awards 6.0 to Recognise Startups Across 20 Sectoral and 3 Special Categories, Introduces 12 New Sectors
National Startup Awards 6.0 Introduces Student Innovator Award, Offers ₹25 Lakh Cash Prize Across Eligible Categories
Applications for National Startup Awards 6.0 Open from 27 October to 20 November 2026
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, has launched the 6th Edition of the National Startup Awards (NSA 6.0) under the Startup India initiative to recognise innovation and entrepreneurship and strengthen India’s startup ecosystem.

The year 2026 marks the completion of ten years of the Startup India initiative, launched in January 2016 to build a strong, inclusive and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem in the country. Since its inception in 2019, the National Startup Awards have emerged as a flagship initiative under Startup India, providing a national platform to recognise entrepreneurial excellence and showcase innovative solutions addressing critical challenges across sectors.

The National Startup Awards recognise startups demonstrating outstanding performance in innovation, scalability, sustainability and socio-economic impact. Building upon the success of the previous five editions, NSA 6.0 seeks to strengthen India’s startup ecosystem by encouraging innovation-led entrepreneurship, fostering inclusive participation and promoting globally competitive startups.

NSA 6.0 will recognise innovation, entrepreneurship and excellence across 20 sectoral categories and three special award categories, reflecting India’s evolving startup ecosystem, emerging technologies and national development priorities. This edition introduces 12 new sectoral categories: Biomanufacturing; Consumer Industries; Defence & Security; Rural Economy, Traditional Industries & Livelihoods; Education & Skilling; Electronics, Semiconductors & Advanced Manufacturing; Sports, Fitness & Sports-Tech; Future Mobility & Automotive; Ocean & Blue Economy; Space-Tech, Drones & Aerospace; Telecom, Connectivity & Digital Infrastructure; and Travel, Tourism & Hospitality.

The three special award categories are Women-Led Startup of the Year, North-East Startup Excellence and the newly introduced Student Innovator / Aspiring Entrepreneur Award. Introduced for the first time, the student award aims to foster a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship among school and college students across all 36 States and Union Territories. It marks a step towards nurturing the next generation of innovators and entrepreneurs and expanding the reach of the National Startup Awards.

Winning startups across the 20 sectoral categories and the two startup-focused special categories will be eligible for a cash prize of ₹25 lakh per category, subject to the applicable award guidelines. The Student Innovator / Aspiring Entrepreneur Award will carry a total prize pool of ₹25 lakh across four sub-categories.

In addition to monetary recognition, the National Startup Awards seek to facilitate mentorship, investor engagement, market access, industry partnerships and enhanced visibility within India’s startup ecosystem.

NSA 6.0 aims to encourage participation from startups across States and Union Territories, including emerging entrepreneurial ecosystems in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities. DPIIT will engage Central Ministries and Departments, State and UT Governments, incubators, academic institutions, banks and financial institutions, Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), industry associations and other ecosystem stakeholders to support outreach, participation and evaluation under the awards.

Applications for NSA 6.0 open on 27 October 2026 and will remain open until 20 November 2026. Eligible startups and student innovators are encouraged to apply and showcase their innovations at the national level through the official Startup India portal at www.startupindia.gov.in.

Through the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards, DPIIT reaffirms the Government of India’s commitment to fostering an inclusive, innovation-driven and globally competitive startup ecosystem, while recognising entrepreneurial excellence and nurturing the next generation of innovators.

2329130.title: From Financial Hardship To Recovery: Mohan Lal’s Journey
2329130.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Hardship To Recovery: Mohan Lal’s Journey
Healthcare Support Through the NAMASTE Scheme and Ayushman Bharat–PM-JAY
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

Access to timely healthcare makes a life-changing difference, particularly for workers facing economic hardship.

The journey of Mohan Lal (name changed), a 65-year-old waste picker from Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, highlights how social protection and healthcare support can help vulnerable workers overcome serious medical challenges and move towards a healthier life.

Coming from a financially disadvantaged family, Mohan Lal spent most of his life working as a contractual sanitation worker and waste picker, earning between Rs 101 and Rs 250 per day. His modest income was barely sufficient to meet his family’s basic needs, leaving little scope for savings or unexpected expenses. When he was diagnosed with a serious heart blockage requiring specialised treatment, the high cost of medical care became a major concern for him and his family.

Enrolled under the Waste Pickers component of the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme, Mohan Lal received an Ayushman Card under Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY). This support enabled him to access treatment for his heart blockage at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, on 8 May 2026, with the full cost of his medical treatment covered.

Following successful treatment, Mohan Lal recovered and was able to return to work and resume supporting his family. Access to healthcare eased the financial burden associated with his medical emergency and helped him focus on recovery. The timely intervention also restored his confidence and provided renewed hope for the future.

Mohan Lal’s journey demonstrates the importance of accessible healthcare and social protection for waste pickers and other vulnerable workers. His recovery reflects how welfare initiatives can help reduce barriers to essential medical treatment, safeguard dignity and strengthen family well-being. His story stands as an encouraging example of how timely support can help individuals move beyond difficult circumstances and look towards the future with renewed confidence.

2329126.title: Special Campaign 6: Department of Posts Organises Dedicated One-day Nationwide Activities
2329126.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Special Campaign 6: Department of Posts Organises Dedicated One-day Nationwide Activities
Department of Posts Holds 1,861 Dak Chaupals
Cleanliness activities cover 55,952 sites; Resolves 9,007 Public Grievances
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications, organised 1,861 Dak Chaupals across the country on 23rd October 2026 as part of Special Campaign 6, strengthening citizen engagement and bringing postal and government services closer to the people. This dedicated one-day programme also witnessed cleanliness activities at approximately 55,952 sites nationwide and the resolution of 9,007 public grievances.

Undertaken in response to the initiative of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), the programme focused on citizen outreach, grievance redressal, cleanliness, environmental sustainability and improvement of postal infrastructure.

Dak Chaupals: Bringing Government Services to Citizens

Dak Chaupals served as platforms for direct interaction between postal officials and citizens, facilitating awareness of postal and citizen-centric services, addressing public grievances and obtaining feedback to improve service delivery.

Activities included awareness and facilitation of Postal Life Insurance (PLI) and Rural Postal Life Insurance (RPLI) schemes, promotion of accessible postal services and engagement with local communities. The resolution of   9,007 public grievances during the programme further reflects the Department’s commitment to responsive governance and timely redressal of citizens’ concerns.

Nationwide Cleanliness and Environmental Sustainability Drives

Special cleanliness drives were undertaken across post offices, including Branch Post Offices, mail offices and administrative establishments. Cleanliness activities covered 55,952 sites, contributing to cleaner surroundings and improved public spaces.

Postal Circles also undertook initiatives to promote environmental sustainability, including awareness campaigns on waste segregation, composting and responsible waste management. These activities encouraged community participation and reinforced the principles of Swachhata and environmental responsibility.

Infrastructure Improvement and Community Engagement

Postal establishments undertook initiatives to improve office infrastructure, enhance public-facing areas and ensure better utilisation of available space. Creative beautification, maintenance and other improvement activities contributed to cleaner and more welcoming postal establishments.

The dedicated one-day programme reflects the Department of Posts commitment to the objectives of Special Campaign 6, particularly institutionalising cleanliness, strengthening grievance redressal, improving citizen engagement and promoting sustainable practices.

The Department will continue to build on these initiatives to make postal establishments cleaner, more accessible and more responsive to citizens’ needs.

2329093.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2329093.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry Organises Health Check-up Camp and ‘Samvaad’ for Safai Mitras under Special Campaign 6.0
Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Shri Prataprao Jadhav Reviews Cleanliness at Ministry’s Offices, Visits Health Check-up Camp and Interacts with Safai Mitras
Health Screening and Medical Consultations Organised for Safai Mitras as Part of Kayakalp Activities under Special Campaign 6.0
‘Samvaad’ Programme Recognises Contributions of Safai Mitras and Reinforces the Importance of Sustaining a Culture of Cleanliness
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the ongoing Special Campaign 6.0, the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare organised a health check-up camp and a ‘Samvaad’ programme for Safai Mitras (sanitation workers) at Kartavya Bhawan-1. Conducted under the Ministry’s Kayakalp activities, the initiatives focused on promoting the health and well-being of Safai Mitras, recognising their contribution to maintaining hygienic workplaces and strengthening a culture of cleanliness.

Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare and Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav visited the health check-up camp and interacted with Safai Mitras. During the visit, he enquired about their health and well-being and expressed appreciation for their dedicated efforts in maintaining cleanliness and hygiene across the Ministry’s premises. Dr. L.G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, was also present.

As part of Special Campaign 6.0, Shri Jadhav also undertook a round of the Ministry’s office premises to take stock of cleanliness and hygiene. During the visit, he reviewed the cleanliness of the office premises and took stock of the upkeep of the working environment.

The health check-up camp provided Safai Mitras with essential health screening and consultation services, including Body Mass Index (BMI) assessment based on height and weight, blood pressure measurement, blood sugar testing and haemoglobin testing. General medicine consultations, basic eye check-ups and Ear, Nose and Throat (ENT) examinations were also conducted to assess their health status and facilitate early identification of potential health concerns.

As part of the Special Campaign 6.0 activities, the Ministry also organised a ‘Samvaad’ programme to acknowledge the important role of Safai Mitras in ensuring clean and hygienic workplaces. Joint Secretary Shri Elangbam Robert Singh interacted with the Safai Mitras and thanked them for their dedicated service. He emphasised the importance of making cleanliness an integral part of everyday life, maintaining hygienic surroundings and instilling these values in future generations. The programme also provided Safai Mitras with an opportunity to share their experiences, feedback and suggestions.

The initiatives under Special Campaign 6.0 underscored the Ministry’s commitment to promoting cleanliness alongside the health, dignity and well-being of those who play a vital role in maintaining hygienic workplaces. By bringing together cleanliness reviews, preventive healthcare, recognition and dialogue, the Ministry reinforced the importance of collective responsibility and sustained efforts towards a clean, healthy and inclusive working environment.

2329092.title: Workshop on Base Revision of State -level Index of Industrial Production during 28–30 October 2026 at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam
2329092.body_html:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Workshop on Base Revision of State -level Index of Industrial Production during 28–30 October 2026 at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) is convening a three Days Workshop on Base Revision of State-level Index of Industrial Production (IIP), at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam in collaboration with Department of Economics and Statistics (DES), Keralam during 28–30 October 2026.

The IIP is a key indicator of industrial performance, tracking changes in performance of industrial sector in economy. It is widely used by policymakers, economists, businesses and investors to assess trends in industrial activity and support informed decision-making. The index also serves as an important input in estimating overall economic growth.

MoSPI has updated the base year of the All-India IIP from 2011-12 to 2022-23. The base year is the reference year against which changes in production in later years are measured. A more recent base year helps the index reflect what India’s industries actually produce at present. The revised series incorporates several methodological improvements, including revision of the item basket and weights, updating of the factory panel, expansion of coverage to include activities such as Gas Supply, Water Supply, Sewerage and Waste Management and provision for factory substitution.

The State DES are responsible for compiling and disseminating the State-level IIP. As the nodal Ministry at the national level, the MoSPI provides technical guidance to States and Union Territories (UTs) to promote methodological uniformity and improve the quality and comparability of industrial statistics.

The three-day workshop will familiarise participating States and UTs with the proposed changes in the structure and methods of the revised IIP and help them finalise the list of items to be tracked and the factories that will report data. It will also provide a platform for discussions and feedback on the revisions to National Industrial Classification-2025 and National Product Classification.

Around 60 officials from MoSPI and the DESs of various States and UTs are expected to take part. Through this workshop, MoSPI aims to strengthen the quality, consistency and comparability of industrial statistics across the country.

2329091.title: Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Reviews Ongoing Construction Work For Permanent Premises At CRC Jammu
2329091.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Reviews Ongoing Construction Work For Permanent Premises At CRC Jammu
Emphasises Timely Completion of Infrastructure to Strengthen Rehabilitation, Skill Development and Empowerment Services for Divyangjan
Rs 24-Crore Facility to Expand Rehabilitation Services; Laboratories for Customised Artificial Limbs and Assistive Devices Planned
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, visited the construction site of the permanent premises of the Composite Regional Centre (CRC) for Skill Development, Rehabilitation & Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan), CRC Jammu, at Village Chak Jawala, Vijaypur in District Samba of Jammu Province in Jammu & Kashmir, to review the progress of the ongoing construction work.

Constructed at an estimated cost of around Rs 24 crore, the permanent premises are expected to significantly enhance the availability of rehabilitation and support services in the region, helping persons with disabilities lead more independent and dignified lives.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Virendra Kumar said that the permanent premises would strengthen CRC Jammu’s institutional capacity and expand access to rehabilitation, education and support services for persons with disabilities across the region. He noted that the Centre was currently operating on a limited scale in Jammu city and that the new facility would enable it to broaden its services.

The Hon’ble Minister was accompanied by senior officials of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, including Shri Rajeev Sharma, Joint Secretary, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan).

During the visit, Dr. Rohnika Sharma, Director, CRC Jammu, briefed the Hon’ble Minister on the progress of construction, the status of work completed so far and the activities remaining to be undertaken. She also apprised him of the infrastructure-related requirements and key aspects concerning the timely completion and operationalisation of the permanent premises.

Dr. Sharma also apprised the Union Minister of the infrastructure requirements and other aspects concerning timely completion of the project. Once operational, the facility is expected to support rehabilitation, special education, early intervention, skill development and empowerment initiatives for Divyangjan.

The visit provided an opportunity to assess the ongoing construction work and review the measures required to expedite the remaining activities.

The Hon’ble Minister emphasised the importance of timely completion of the project and the availability of appropriate infrastructure to facilitate the effective delivery of services to Divyangjan.

He added that the establishment of the permanent premises of CRC Jammu marks an important step towards strengthening rehabilitation services, special education, early intervention, skill development and empowerment initiatives for persons with disabilities in the Jammu region.

The Minister further said the Centre is intended to support the delivery of rehabilitation-related services and facilitate access to appropriate interventions and skill development opportunities for persons with disabilities.

Dr Kumar said the Centre would provide physiotherapy and specialised training for children with disabilities to help them become self-reliant. Training for parents and caregivers would also be facilitated so that they can better support children with disabilities.

He added that a Pradhan Mantri Divyasha Kendra would be established at the Centre to facilitate access to assistive devices. Disability-related courses, including B.Ed. and M.Ed. programmes, are also planned, which would create educational opportunities and enhance employment prospects for youth trained in disability rehabilitation and empowerment, he added.

The Minister said the laboratory facilities for the measurement, manufacture and fitting of customised artificial limbs and other assistive devices would be developed at the Centre. These facilities are expected to help beneficiaries perform daily activities with greater ease and independence, he added.

Emphasising inclusive development, Dr. Kumar said that empowering persons with disabilities was integral to the vision of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas’ and the goal of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. He observed that CRC Jammu would address the long-standing need for a comprehensive rehabilitation facility in the Jammu region, bringing disability-related services closer to beneficiaries, from children to senior citizens.

The Minister further said that supporting persons with disabilities would also strengthen their families and enable them to contribute more actively to society and the nation’s development.

The review reaffirmed the importance of completing the infrastructure project in a timely manner to strengthen the institutional capacity for providing rehabilitation and empowerment services to Divyangjan in Jammu & Kashmir.

It is pertinent to mention that CRC Jammu functions under the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, through Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Institute for Persons with Physical Disabilities (PDUNIPPD), New Delhi.

2329077.title: Government of India Introduces Concessional Local Pass for National Highway Users Living Near Fee Plazas
2329077.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
Government of India Introduces Concessional Local Pass for National Highway Users Living Near Fee Plazas
Eligible non-commercial vehicle owners residing within 20 km of a fee plaza can avail Concessional Local Pass for Rs. 1,500 per annum for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs. 3,000 per annum for fee plazas situated within these limits depending on the location of the plaza
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

In a major step to enhance ‘Ease of Living’ for citizens residing near National Highway Fee Plazas, the Government of India has introduced a ‘Concessional Local Pass’ for eligible non-commercial vehicle owners residing within 20 km of a National Highway fee plaza. The rule will come into effect from 01st November 2026.

The annual fee for the concessional Local Pass will be Rs.1,500 for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs.3,000 for toll plazas situated within these limits. 

Under the new provision, eligible non-commercial vehicle owners with a valid and functional FASTag, residing within 20 km range can choose between the existing monthly pass and the concessional Local Pass for commuting through a specific fee plaza. The pass will be valid only for that fee plaza and will not be transferable to any other plazas.

The concessional Local Pass will not be available on National Highways or Expressways where toll fee collection is based on a closed user-fee collection system. It will also not be issued where a service road or alternative road is available for use by commuters.

The Annual Local Pass will be available at eligible Toll Plazas wef 01.11.2026. The Annual Local Pass will also be available through Rajmargyatra App wef 01.12.2026.

The amendment has been notified through the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) (Fifth Amendment) Rules, 2026, under the powers conferred by the National Highways Act, 1956. The rates may be revised by the Central Government annually with revisions taking effect on 01st April.

With over 13 crore FASTags issued across the country, the new provision aims to provide an option for eligible residents living near toll plazas to make travel more economical and enhance Ease of Commuting for local residents.

2328924.title: AIIA Report Indicates Encouraging Improvements in Quality of Life and Cognitive Health Among Elderly in Faridabad
2328924.body_html:
AYUSH
AIIA Report Indicates Encouraging Improvements in Quality of Life and Cognitive Health Among Elderly in Faridabad
Community-based Ayurveda intervention records improvements in quality of life, Agnibala and bone mineral density; project report submitted to Expert Committee
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 2:43PM by PIB Delhi

The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, has reported encouraging findings from a community-based Ayurveda programme conducted in Faridabad district, Haryana, to promote the physical and mental health of elderly people. According to the project findings, improvements were recorded in quality of life, Agnibala and bone mineral density following the intervention. Positive changes were also observed in cognitive health assessments, along with improvements in selected biomarkers, including serotonin, acetylcholine, DHEA and vitamin D. The findings were presented at a workshop held at AIIA on October 24, and the project report was submitted to an expert committee.

Under its Public Health Initiative (PHI), AIIA screened 5,594 people aged 60–80 years in Faridabad district over three months and provided them with Ayurvedic medicines. In addition, under a separate component focused on dementia, 200 patients were screened and provided with Ayurveda-based medicines over four months. Titled “Community-Based Ayurveda Intervention for Promotion of Physical and Mental Health in Elderly Population of Faridabad District, Haryana State,” the project aimed to study the potential of community-level Ayurveda-based interventions and assess approaches to promoting healthy ageing.

The initial assessment identified several health challenges among the elderly participants. These included vision-related problems in 67.73% of participants, physical inactivity in 43.05% and reduced cognitive function in 6.85%. Other concerns included high blood pressure, elevated random blood glucose levels, reduced bone mineral density, constipation and sleep-related problems.

In the first component of the project, improvements in quality of life were recorded following a 60-day intervention. The total score on the World Health Organization Quality of Life (WHOQOL) assessment increased from 292.0 to 326.3. Improvements were also observed across all six parameters used to assess Agnibala, an Ayurvedic concept associated with digestive and metabolic strength. An improvement in bone mineral density was also recorded.

In the second component, which focused on cognitive health, the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores showed a shift towards normal levels. The 6-CIT assessment also indicated signs of improved cognitive performance. The quality-of-life score in this component increased from 277.4 to 364.2. Improvements were additionally recorded in the levels of serotonin, acetylcholine (ACh), dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and vitamin D.

These findings provide a basis for further investigation into the potential of community-based Ayurveda interventions. However, more extensive scientific evaluation, continued safety monitoring and further studies are necessary to validate the findings and establish the effectiveness and safety of these interventions.

Dr. Koustubha Upadhyaya, Advisor to the Ministry of Ayush, attended the workshop as the Chief Guest, while Prof. (Vaidya) Pradeep Kumar Prajapati, Director of AIIA, presided over the programme. Dr. Upadhyaya emphasised the importance of meaningful social engagement with elderly people to better understand their needs. He also highlighted the importance of encouraging older adults to participate in physical and mental activities. In addition, he underscored the need for greater investment in such initiatives to achieve better health outcomes.

Prof. (Vaidya) Prajapati appreciated the efforts of the Public Health Initiative team and stressed the importance of systematically studying experiences with community-based Ayurveda healthcare services and widely disseminating the findings. He also emphasised the need to extend such initiatives to a larger number of elderly people. The Director further emphasised the importance of the joint family system, highlighting its role in ensuring proper care, support, and emotional well-being of the elderly.

The workshop also featured contributions from Dr. Suneela Garg, Director Professor and Head of the Department of Community Medicine at Maulana Azad Medical College, New Delhi; Dr. Suman Ray, Senior Principal Scientist at the CSIR–National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (NIScPR); and Dr. Lokesh Singh Shekhawat, Professor of Psychiatry at Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital.

The occasion also witnessed the release of the book Holistic Approach for Healthy Aging. Other attendees included Prof. (Dr.) Manjusha Rajagopala, Dean (DU); Prof. (Dr.) Mahesh Vyas, Dean (Ph.D.); Prof. (Dr.) R. K. Yadav, Dean (PG); and Prof. (Dr.) Yogesh Badwe, Medical Superintendent, along with other faculty members of the institute.

The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, is an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India. The institute works to advance Ayurveda through education, research, clinical services and public health initiatives.

2328843.title: Industrial Settlements Benefit Over 10,900 Bihar Gramin Bank Employees, Securing Financial Benefits Worth Nearly ₹78 Crore
2328843.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Industrial Settlements Benefit Over 10,900 Bihar Gramin Bank Employees, Securing Financial Benefits Worth Nearly ₹78 Crore
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 12:24PM by PIB Delhi

Two industrial disputes involving the management of Bihar Gramin Bank and its employees’ organisations were amicably resolved on October 22 and 23, 2026, through conciliation efforts of the Assistant Labour Commissioner (Central), Patna, under the Office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India.

The settlements are expected to extend financial benefits amounting to approximately ₹77.69 crore to over 10,900 employees of Bihar Gramin Bank, including recurring annual benefits of approximately ₹9.02 crore under the settlement with the Bihar Gramin Bank Workers Organisation (BGBWO).

The first settlement, reached on October 22, 2026, between the Bihar Gramin Bank Adhikari Sangh, Patna, and the bank management, is expected to benefit around 8,400 employees, with financial benefits amounting to approximately ₹67.17 crore. The settlement addresses key employee demands, including payment of Performance Linked Incentive (PLI), officiating allowances, wage enhancement, enhancement of travel allowances, promotions and compassionate appointments.

The second settlement, reached on October 23, 2026, between the Bihar Gramin Bank Workers Organisation (BGBWO) and the bank management, is expected to benefit around 2,500 employees, with financial benefits amounting to approximately ₹10.52 crore, including recurring annual benefits of approximately ₹9.02 crore. This settlement addresses key demands relating to the effective implementation of the 12th Bipartite Settlement, enhancement of House Rent Allowance (HRA), increase in transport allowance for Divyang employees, payment of overtime, transparency in promotion processes and the formation of a Negotiating Council.

Both settlements were facilitated through constructive dialogue and the active participation and cooperation of the employees’ organisations and the bank management, helping resolve the disputes amicably and strengthen industrial harmony.

These successful conciliation efforts reflect the continued commitment of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) Organisation towards safeguarding employees’ interests, promoting fair labour practices and fostering harmonious industrial relations through effective conciliation and constructive dialogue.

****

2328842.title: DPIIT Advances Trust-Based Governance Through Startup Support, Regulatory Reforms and Digital Single-Window Clearances
2328842.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
DPIIT Advances Trust-Based Governance Through Startup Support, Regulatory Reforms and Digital Single-Window Clearances
Startup India Supports 2.5 Lakh+ Startups, Generating 25.42 Lakh+ Jobs Across 770+ Districts
Startup Credit Guarantees Reach ₹1,662 Crore as 63 Regulatory Reforms Strengthen the Startup Ecosystem
47,957 Compliances Reduced and 900 Legal Provisions Decriminalised to Ease Business Regulations Across India
Labour Law Consolidation and Licensing Reforms Simplify Compliance and Reduce Regulatory Burden on Businesses
India Records USD 843 Billion in FDI Over 12 Years as Investment Reforms Expand Automatic Route Across 17 Sectors
National Single Window System Simplifies Approvals Through Digital Integration, Automation and 22-Language Accessibility
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 12:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, has driven a sustained shift from a permission-based to a trust-based regulatory framework. Reforms across the startup ecosystem, compliance reduction, sectoral regulation, foreign direct investment and single-window clearances have reduced the regulatory burden on businesses and delivered measurable outcomes in business entry, employment, investment and digital service delivery.

DPIIT has recognised 2,50,046 startups, reporting over 25.42 lakh jobs across 770+ districts and 56 industries. Of these startups, 52% are from non-metro cities and 48% have at least one woman director. Annual recognitions increased from 34,200 in FY 2023-24 to 36,440 in FY 2024-25.

Under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme, ₹775.67 crore has been approved for 4,194 startups across 32 States/UTs through 244 incubators, including 2,147 women-led startups and 2,356 startups from Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Under the Fund of Funds for Startups, SIDBI has committed ₹12,623 crore to 166 Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), which have invested ₹28,254 crore in 1,475 startups.

The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups has guaranteed 532 loans worth ₹1,662.71 crore to startups employing 41,637 people. The guarantee cover per borrower has been doubled from ₹10 crore to ₹20 crore, while the annual fee has been reduced to 1% for 27 Champion Sectors.

A total of 63 regulatory reforms have been enabled, including the abolition of angel tax, harmonisation of long-term capital gains taxation for listed and unlisted shares, and permission for insurance companies, EPFO, superannuation funds and gratuity funds to invest in AIFs. Further, 4,467 startups hold the Section 80-IAC certificate of eligibility.

With prior-experience, prior-turnover and Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) requirements relaxed, the number of startups registered on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) has increased from 7,929 in January 2021 to 43,260. These startups have delivered 6.23 lakh orders worth ₹68,105 crore to public buyers. Dedicated startup policies have expanded from four States/UTs in 2016 to 32. In addition, 104 new incubators have been established across 17 States/UTs, while the TEJAS initiative covers 132 districts in 27 States/UTs.

A total of 47,957 compliances have been reduced across Central Ministries and States/UTs. Of these, 22,290 have been digitised, 16,141 simplified, 5,255 decriminalised and 4,271 eliminated. The Jan Vishwas Acts have decriminalised 900 provisions of Central laws, comprising 183 provisions across 42 Acts in 2023 and 717 provisions across 79 Acts in 2026.

States/UTs have implemented over 9,700 reforms across seven editions of the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP). The District BRAP extends 222 reforms to District Collectorates, Development Authorities and Urban Local Bodies.

Twenty-nine Central labour laws have been consolidated into four Labour Codes. The threshold for prior permission for lay-off or closure has been raised from 100 to 300 workers. The applicability threshold for factories has been increased from 10 to 20 workers for establishments using power and from 20 to 40 workers for those not using power. The threshold for contract-labour licensing has been raised from 20 to 50 workers. A 30-day compliance notice is now mandatory before legal action.

The validity of licences issued by the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) has been extended from five to ten years, reducing the need for renewals. All PESO modules have been digitised and integrated with the National Single Window System (NSWS), with online No Objection Certificates (NOCs) issued by District Authorities and fee relaxations provided for women and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). The Boilers Act, 2025, has replaced the colonial-era Boilers Act, 1923.

Seventeen sectors have moved to the automatic route for foreign direct investment (FDI). In the defence sector, the FDI limit under the automatic route has been raised from 49% to 74% for new industrial licences. The FDI limit in insurance was raised from 49% to 74% in 2021 and to 100% in 2026 for insurers investing their entire premium in India. The sector attracted approximately USD 8.79 billion in FDI from FY 2021-22 to FY 2024-25.

Up to 100% FDI is permitted under the automatic route in telecommunications, non-scheduled air transport services and ground handling in civil aviation, as well as satellite component manufacturing and broadcasting distribution.

India received USD 843 billion in FDI during FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, 169% higher than the USD 313 billion received in the preceding twelve years. The inflow reached an all-time high of USD 94.53 billion in FY 2025-26.

The National Single Window System (NSWS) has received 15,49,850 applications, registered 5,76,778 businesses and delivered over 8.5 lakh approvals. A total of 3,779 services are live on the platform, comprising 327 Central and 3,452 State services, compared with 142 Central approvals and 14 States/UTs at its soft launch in September 2021. The system has integrated 34 States/UTs and 32 Central Ministries/Departments, with 18 Central Ministries using NSWS.

The Know Your Approvals (KYA) module enables businesses to identify the Central and State approvals applicable to them at the outset, providing visibility of over 8,000 approvals. Of these, 2,825 approvals, comprising 592 Central and 2,233 State approvals, are integrated through KYA. To eliminate repetitive data entry, 89 common data fields now auto-populate across 285 approvals. The portal is available in 22 Indian languages, improving accessibility for entrepreneurs across regions.

NSWS is also being used to eliminate approval steps altogether. The Industrial Entrepreneur Memorandum (IEM) is now auto-generated using data drawn from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) and other databases, without requiring departmental approval. Similarly, e-B4 production visa sponsorship letters for foreign professionals are generated through API integration between NSWS and the Visa portal, without requiring approval from the concerned line Ministry.

States/UTs have been encouraged to establish and strengthen Single Window Systems (SWS) as integrated digital platforms providing businesses with a single point of access to regulatory approvals and compliances. The framework promotes features such as Single Sign-On, Single Business ID, Know Your Approvals, Common Application Forms, online payments, inspection management, applicant guidance, grievance redressal and real-time dashboards, supported by inter-departmental integration and end-to-end digital processing.

These initiatives aim to reduce procedural complexity, minimise physical touchpoints, improve transparency and ensure time-bound service delivery. Taken together, the reforms mark a steady transition towards simpler, digital and less burdensome regulation, enabling businesses to start, grow and invest with greater ease.

***

2328830.title: Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage
2328830.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage
Powering India's Industries Towards a Net Zero Future
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 11:42AM by PIB Delhi

CCUS is an important pathway for reducing emissions from hard-to-abate sectors. Carbon dioxide is increasingly being viewed not only as an emission, but also as a potential resource. CCUS can support India’s Net Zero by 2070 vision while strengthening industrial competitiveness and resource efficiency. The Government is fostering an ecosystem that brings together research institutions, public sector enterprises and private industry. This growing ecosystem spans operational projects, projects under execution and proposed initiatives across multiple States. These efforts are laying the foundation for indigenous CCUS capabilities, carbon utilisation and secure carbon storage.

 

CCUS Bridging the Gap in India’s Net Zero Journey

 India’s journey towards Net Zero by 2070 requires reducing emissions across its energy and industrial sectors. Renewable energy can significantly lower emissions, but some industrial processes cannot be easily electrified. These include processes requiring very high temperatures or carbon-based inputs. Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) offers an additional pathway for addressing such emissions. It involves capturing carbon dioxide from industrial sources before its release into the atmosphere. The captured carbon dioxide can then be utilised in productive applications or stored securely underground. CCUS can therefore complement renewable energy and support India’s transition towards a lower-carbon industrial economy.

NITI Aayog identifies CCUS as critical for decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors, including steel, cement, oil and gas, petrochemicals, chemicals and fertilisers. These industries contribute significantly to industrial emissions and face technological challenges in achieving deep decarbonisation. CCUS can help reduce emissions from existing facilities while supporting the continued production of essential goods. It can also create opportunities for developing new technologies, infrastructure and industrial capabilities in India. By connecting carbon capture with utilisation and secure storage, the approach can address emissions across multiple stages. CCUS can thus support India’s climate goals while maintaining industrial growth and economic development.

Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies

ESTIC-2026, the second edition of India’s Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave, is being held from 27–29 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Organised by the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), the conclave follows the theme “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies.” It advances emerging frontiers in science and technology, including energy technologies such as Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS). Spanning 12 thematic areas, ESTIC-2026 features plenary sessions, technical discussions and exhibitions. The conclave also promotes strategic collaborations in support of India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Read More on the agenda: ESTIC 2026

 

CCUS Process: From Capture to Storage

 

Step 1: Capturing Carbon Dioxide at the Source

The process begins at an industrial facility where carbon dioxide is generated. Capture systems separate carbon dioxide from gases released during fuel combustion or industrial processes. The captured gas is then purified, dried and compressed into a dense form before being transported or used.

Step 2: From Capture to Transport

Pipelines are commonly used to transport carbon dioxide over suitable distances. Ships and other transport modes can provide flexibility, especially for longer distances. The choice of transport depends on distance, volume, infrastructure and the destination. The carbon dioxide can then be sent to a utilisation facility or geological storage site.

Did You Know? A geological storage site is a secure, deep underground location used to permanently isolate captured CO₂. CO₂ geological storage (geo-storage) is a promising approach that can help to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

Step 3: Carbon Utilisation and Permanent Storage

At the final stage, captured carbon dioxide can either be put to productive use or stored permanently underground. It can be used in applications such as enhanced oil recovery, food and beverages, urea, green methanol and concrete. For permanent storage, carbon dioxide is injected deep underground into suitable geological formations, including depleted oil and gas reservoirs, deep saline aquifers and basaltic rock formations.

CCUS Hubs and Clusters Model

 

India’s CCUS framework envisages regional clusters and hubs connecting multiple carbon dioxide emitters with shared infrastructure. This model can integrate common systems for carbon dioxide transport, utilisation and storage. Captured carbon dioxide can be collected from multiple sources and transported through shared networks. It can then be directed to suitable utilisation facilities or geological storage sites. NITI Aayog identifies the hub and cluster approach as suitable for India. The model can create economies of scale, reduce infrastructure risks and connect carbon dioxide supply with potential demand.

 

The Department of Science and Technology’s CCUS Roadmap 2025 identifies potential industrial and geological regions for such clusters. These include the Gujarat coast, with its concentration of refineries and chemical industries. The Odisha–Jharkhand belt offers potential for clusters linked to steel and cement industries. Northeast India also presents opportunities linked to its oil and gas resources. Such regional clusters can bring together emitters, transport infrastructure, utilisation facilities and storage sites. This approach can help develop a coordinated CCUS ecosystem suited to India’s industrial landscape.

 

 

CCUS Advancing the Low Carbon Transition

 

India’s low-carbon transition requires solutions that combine economic growth with deeper emission reductions. CCUS addresses this gap by managing carbon dioxide at source and creating opportunities for its reuse. It complements renewable energy expansion while opening applications across industry, hydrogen and carbon dioxide removal.

 

Decarbonising Hard-to-Abate Sectors

 

Hard-to-Abate Sectors (steel, cement, refineries/chemicals, fertilisers) release carbon dioxide directly from their processes. Their emissions can be difficult to eliminate through electrification (transition to renewables) alone. Emissions from these sectors and thermal power generation are expected to reach nearly 2,300 million tonnes per annum by 2030, making their capture and abatement critical. CCUS technology provides a means of addressing these emissions from ongoing industrial activity.

 

 

Did you know? Green Hydrogen is produced by electrolysis of water using power generated from renewable energy sources. Blue Hydrogen is produced using natural gas or coal as the primary feedstock.

 

 

Enabling the Low Carbon Hydrogen Economy

 

CCUS is expected to play an important part in India’s shift towards hydrogen, through blue hydrogen production using coal gasification coupled with carbon capture. This complements India’s efforts to develop a low-carbon hydrogen economy.

 

Coal Gasification

 

Coal gasification converts solid coal into a clean, useful gas using controlled heat. This gas is called synthesis gas, or syngas. The process of producing it from coal is known as coal gasification. There are two established methods of doing this. Surface coal gasification processes mined coal in above-ground gasifiers. Underground coal gasification converts coal directly within the underground layer. In both cases, coal is not fully burned, unlike conventional combustion. Instead, it reacts with a limited supply of oxygen and steam. This takes place at high temperatures, typically between 800°C and 1,600°C. These conditions break coal's complex structure into simpler gases.

 

Sustaining Existing Energy Infrastructure                                                                              

 

As of August 2026, fossil-fuel-based sources accounted for 45.12% of India’s total installed power capacity. This existing infrastructure will remain part of India’s energy system during the transition to cleaner sources. Managing emissions from these assets will therefore be important for achieving long-term climate goals. CCUS can support this effort by enabling existing thermal power plants and industries to reduce emissions. Steel and cement facilities can also potentially be retrofitted with CCUS systems. This can reduce carbon dioxide emissions while allowing essential energy and industrial infrastructure to continue operating.

 

Carbon Utilisation

 

Within the Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage framework, captured carbon dioxide can serve as a feedstock for materials, fuels, chemicals and biological products, creating pathways for both carbon management and industrial value. Applications include building materials such as concrete and aggregates, synthetic fuels and chemicals, polymers, enhanced oil recovery with underground carbon storage, and algae-based products including biofuels. These applications extend carbon dioxide utilisation across materials, fuels, chemicals and biological products, while improving resource efficiency.

 

India’s First of Its Kind CCU Test Beds In Coal- Gasification Facilities

Through one of its recent interventions, DST has supported two Technology Deployment Testbeds to be implemented by Industry-Research Consortia between IIT Delhi – Thermax Ltd and CSIR-IICT Hyderabad – BHEL for setting up pilot-scale demonstrations in Coal Gasification plants for Methanol and DME production, with Industry partnering as a solution provider along with a Technology designer (knowledge partner) to deploy CCU in hard-to-abate sectors like Thermal power.

India’s First Integrated CCUS Field Laboratory

India’s first integrated CCUS Field Laboratory at IIT Bombay, inaugurated in May 2026, brings carbon capture, utilisation and permanent geological storage together on a single pilot-scale platform. The indigenous facility can capture up to 3 tonnes of carbon dioxide per day from industrial emissions and ambient air, using non-potable water, and convert it into advantageous carbonate and bicarbonate products. Scientific drilling in Deccan Traps basalt formations will further assess India’s potential for safe and permanent carbon dioxide storage. The facility provides a national testbed for developing and scaling indigenous carbon management technologies, supporting Net Zero 2070 and solutions for hard-to-abate industries. Read more: India’s First Integrated CCUS Field Laboratory Facility

Strengthening India’s CCUS Ecosystem

The Government of India has undertaken initiatives spanning research, policy and industry to advance CCUS development and reduce emissions. These measures strengthen the foundation for India’s Net Zero target by 2070.

  • Union Budget 2026–27, CCUS Scheme: Announced in February 2026, the Ministry of Finance allocated ₹20,000 crore over five years to promote carbon capture, utilisation and storage in five major industrial sectors: Power, Steel, Cement, Refineries, and Chemicals.

 

  • Department of Science & Technology- CCUS R&D Roadmap: Launched in December 2025, the roadmap provides strategic direction for CCUS research, funding, technology development and deployment, with a focus on commercial readiness, breakthrough technologies and enabling frameworks. Click to Access the DST Roadmap

 

  • NITI Aayog CCUS Policy Framework & Mechanism: Released in November 2022, the report examines CCUS as an emissions reduction strategy for deep decarbonisation of hard-to-abate sectors and outlines sector-specific policy interventions for its deployment. Click to Access NITI Aayog Report

 

  • National CCUS Centres: Established in 2022 at IIT Bombay and JNCASR, Bengaluru, with backing from the Department of Science and Technology, these centres focus on CCUS research, technology development, pilot-scale demonstration and industry collaboration.                                                            

  • India’s CCUS Initiative: Spearheaded jointly by the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), India launched a major research drive on CCUS. As part of Mission Innovation, a global clean energy platform, India collaborated with 13 partner countries to advance technologies to capture, separate, safely store, and convert CO2 into useful value-added materials.

 

India Launches First Ever CCU Testbed Cluster for Cement Industry

India launched its first cluster of five Carbon Capture and Utilisation testbeds for the cement industry on 11th May 2025. Led by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), the initiative brings leading cement companies and premier research institutions together under a Public-Private Partnership model to develop and deploy industrial CCU technologies. The testbeds cover applications ranging from carbon dioxide capture and mineralisation to its conversion into concrete products, advancing practical CCU applications for cement sector decarbonisation.

India Accelerates on CCU

India has several CCU projects as of April 2026, spanning operational, under execution and proposed stages. The portfolio includes public sector enterprises, private industry, and academic institutions across multiple States. Projects focus on reducing carbon emissions, productive carbon utilisation and circular economy applications.

  • Operational: Three projects are operational, with one each in Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra.
  • Under Construction/Execution: Six projects are under construction or execution. Andhra Pradesh leads with three projects, followed by Telangana with two and Maharashtra with one.
  • Proposed: Sixteen projects are at the proposed stage. Assam and Odisha lead with four projects each, followed by Gujarat and Rajasthan with two each. Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana and Tamil Nadu have one project each.

The project pipeline reflects growing momentum towards carbon management solutions across India. It also provides a foundation for scaling indigenous Carbon Capture and Utilisation applications.

Shaping India’s Low Carbon Industrial Future

India’s Panchamrit commitments provide the broader context for advancing low-carbon growth and achieving Net Zero by 2070. CCUS adds an important technology dimension by addressing emissions from sectors where complete elimination remains challenging. Government initiatives spanning research, technology development, financing and demonstration are creating the foundations for wider deployment. As these efforts progress, CCUS could improve resource efficiency, support industrial decarbonisation, and help develop a more circular carbon economy.

2328810.title: Union Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Reviews Key Initiatives, Projects and Programmes of DoWR, RD & GR
2328810.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Union Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Reviews Key Initiatives, Projects and Programmes of DoWR, RD & GR
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 10:56AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil chaired a review meeting with HoDs in the presence of Minister of State of Jal Shakti Sh. Raj Bhushan Choudhary of the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation to assess the overall progress of projects, programmes, schemes and initiatives being undertaken by the Department and its various wings and organisations.

During the meeting, Flood Management Wing (FM Wing), Farakka Barrage Project, National Water Mission, Modernisation of Command Area Development and Water Management (M-CADWM), Basin Management–I & II, National Water Development Agency, Ken–Betwa Link Project Authority, Brahmaputra–Barak River Matters, Brahmaputra Board, Minor Irrigation Statistics, and National Institute of Hydrology (NIH) gave detailed presentations on their ongoing projects and activities.

The discussions focused on the status of ongoing projects including progress of projects under the Flood Management and Border Areas Programme (FMBAP), progress of major works, including replacement of barrage gates and anti-erosion measures under implementation-related challenges under Farakka Barrage Project, priority activities and initiatives of the National Water Mission, implementation status of 35 pilot clusters under M-CADWM, status of the Ken–Betwa Link Project, including the link canal, Daudhan Dam and progress of preparation of master plans/DPRs by Brahmaputra Board, progress of four ongoing censuses under the Minor Irrigation Statistics programme, targets and progress of major programmes and activities of NIH, etc. The Minister issued directions and recorded decisions aimed at expediting project implementation and strengthening coordination with the States for completion of projects in time bound manner.

Emphasizing the need for expeditious implementation, the Union Minister directed that bottlenecks affecting the progress of projects be identified and resolved speedily in order to ensure timely completion of projects. He called upon senior officers and heads of the concerned wings and organisations of the Department to ensure effective follow-up on the decisions taken during the review and maintain close monitoring of implementation, with a focus on achieving the desired outcomes within stipulated timelines.
